summary: 巴黎——一家英国公司藏在法国郊区会议中心的一个黑暗角落里，掌握着美国最新战舰的下一个设计方案。上周，2026 年欧洲海军陆战队巴布科克国际展台上的展示台上展示了​​ 31 型“箭头”号的模型。它是白宫设计的美国海军外国护卫舰竞赛的六个竞争者之一，目的是在美国掀起新一轮造船和投资浪潮。随着特朗普政府不断追求外国军舰设计和造船，几家欧洲国防公司在本两年期
content:
巴黎——一家英国公司藏在法国郊区会议中心的一个黑暗角落里，掌握着美国最新战舰的下一个设计方案。上周，2026 年欧洲海军陆战队巴布科克国际展台上的展示台上展示了​​ 31 型“箭头”号的模型。这是白宫设计的美国海军外国护卫舰竞赛的六个竞争者之一，目的是在美国掀起新一轮造船和投资浪潮。随着特朗普政府不断追求外国军舰设计和造船，在两年一度的会议上，几家欧洲防务公司急于讨论如果美国来敲门，他们可以在潜在的国际竞争中提出的选择。美国海军目前正在建造两艘护卫舰设计。一年前前海军部长约翰·费兰取消了该计划后，芬坎蒂尼马里内特海军陆战队仍在威斯康星州造船厂建造前两艘星座级护卫舰。与此同时，HII 的英格尔斯造船公司签订了一份长期合同，用于启动基于美国海岸警卫队国家安全巡逻舰的 FF(X) 护卫舰。据美国海军学院新闻了解，虽然美国海军几十年来一直未能成功推出护卫舰项目，但美国海军正在努力在未来几年内将外国设计用于新型舰艇。哈德逊研究所海军分析师布莱恩·克拉克表示，新护卫舰的工作要求已基本完成。
现在，海军优先考虑的是能够护航其他船只的护卫舰，而不是执行反潜战，这是现已取消的星座级计划的主要任务。克拉克表示，海军需要一个能够实施封锁并防御中层威胁的平台，就像美国中央司令部目前面临的中等威胁。 “一艘护卫舰可以防御我们所看到的来自伊朗的那种规模的威胁，”克拉克在欧洲海军之前告诉美国海军学院新闻。 “并不是真正的[反潜战]——更多的是执行这种海上控制、海上安全类型的任务。”为此，来自全球各地的六种设计已成为国际竞赛的潜在候选者，该竞赛将遵循唐纳德·特朗普总统在八月份的造船备忘录中所呼吁的设计。白宫文件呼吁海军推行所谓的“芬兰模式”，即在外国投资美国造船基础设施之前，可以在外国造船厂开始建造最多前两艘船体。白宫正在利用芬兰模式，在芬兰、德克萨斯州和路易斯安那州的造船厂建造两个独立的设计，以启动北极安全巡逻艇计划。白宫管理和预算办公室主任拉斯·沃特一直直言不讳地主张对小型水面作战舰艇和辅助舰艇使用相同的模型。
但国会抵制了这一努力，在众议院和参议院版本的《2027 财年国防授权法案》中都加入了草案，该法案将阻止海军购买外国建造的军舰。国会对购买海外辅助舰艇持更开放的态度。尽管遭到国会的抵制，八月的一份备忘录还是勾勒出了这场竞赛的蓝图——由国防部长皮特·赫格斯和代理海军部长曹洪制定。该计划将于周四向白宫提交。竞争者 Type 31 Babcock 图片 自 2023 年以来，Babcock 一直与美国领先者保持合作关系

【原文 English Original】
PARIS — Tucked in a dark corner of a convention center in the French suburbs, a British company could hold the next design for America’s newest warship. A model of the Type-31 Arrowhead sailed on a display table at the Babcock International booth at Euronaval 2026 last week. It was one of a half a dozen contenders for the U.S. Navy’s foreign frigate competition designed by the White House to jumpstart a new wave of shipbuilding and investment in the U.S. With the Trump administration’s ongoing pursuit of foreign warship design and shipbuilding, several European defense companies at the biennial conference were eager to discuss the options they could propose in a potential international competition should the U.S. come knocking at their doors. The U.S. Navy currently has two frigate designs under construction in the U.S. Fincantieri Marinette Marine is still building the first two Constellation-class frigates at its Wisconsin yard after former Navy Secretary John Phelan canceled the program one year ago . Meanwhile, HII’s Ingalls Shipbuilding has a long lead-time contract to start the FF(X) frigate that is based on the U.S. Coast Guard’s National Security Cutter. While a successful frigate program has eluded the U.S. Navy for decades, the service is working toward using a foreign design for a new class of ships in the next few years, USNI News understands. The working requirements for a new frigate are mostly done, according to Hudson Institute naval analyst Bryan Clark. Now the Navy is prioritizing frigates that can escort other ships instead of performing anti-submarine warfare, which was the main mission of the now-cancelled Constellation-class program. The service wants a platform that can enforce a blockade and protect against medium tiered threats like what the military is currently facing in U.S. Central Command, according to Clark. “A frigate could defend against the kind of scale of threat that we’re seeing from the Iranians,” Clark told USNI News ahead of Euronaval. “Not really [anti-submarine warfare] – more about doing this kind of sea control, maritime security type mission.” To that end, six designs from around the globe have emerged as potential candidates in an international competition that would adhere to the one President Donald Trump called for in an August shipbuilding memo. The White House document called on the Navy to pursue the so-called “Finland model,” in which construction could begin in a foreign shipyard for up to the first two hulls before a foreign investment in U.S. shipbuilding infrastructure. The White House is using the Finland model to jumpstart the Arctic Security Cutter program by building two separate designs in shipyards in Finland, Texas and Louisiana. White House Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought has been vocal about using the same model for small surface combatants and auxiliaries. But Congress has resisted the effort by including draft language in both the House and Senate versions of the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act that would prevent the Navy from buying foreign-built warships. Congress is more open to buying auxiliaries overseas. Despite congressional resistance, an August memo outlined a blueprint for that competition – crafted by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao. The plan was due to the White House on Thursday. The Contenders Type 31 Babcock image Since 2023, Babcock has maintained a partnership with lead American shipbuilder HII as part of the AUKUS security pact. The British company also works with HII on the unmanned surface vessel Romulus, which the U.K.’s Royal Navy is purchasing. Sir Nick Hine, the chief executive of Babcock’s marine division, said he thinks the Type 31 frigate could fill the U.S. Navy’s need for a small surface combatant. That platform should be able to “perform anti‑submarine warfare, surface warfare and convoy escort duties,” according to the White House memo. The Type 31 frigate could function as a command vessel in a fleet that includes a mix of manned and unmanned ships, according to Hine. Babcock has already worked with Lockheed Martin, meaning the platform could integrate the AEGIS Combat System and the AN/SPY-7 radar. The design also features a Mark 41 launcher with 32 Vertical Launching System cells, but Hine says it could potentially take additional cells. “Navies are short of two things always, even yours, short of money and people,” Hine, making the case for the Type 31, told USNI News on the sidelines of Euronaval last week. “You need a cheaper frigate because the cost of some of these platforms is insane, and you need a platform that’s got less people in it because you don’t have enough people. The Type 31 was designed to be more adaptable, more affordable, more available, and it was designed to have less people in it,” he added. “It was designed for a crew of a complement of 100, not to exceed 100. It’s 6,000 tons, 140 meters in length, and therefore it was designed for North Atlantic operations, so it’s designed to operate in high sea states for long periods of time.” To field the platform in the U.S. fleet faster, the hull could be built abroad to the point where it’s ready to sail away while the combat system is integrated back in the U.S., Hine said. Another option is out of Spain’s Navantia, which is working on an export version of its Bonifaz-class F-110 anti-submarine warfare frigate. Navantia, which is partnered with Lockheed Martin for the F-110, plans to submit a bid should the U.S. Navy issue a request for proposals, Navantia commercial director Juan de la Cueva told USNI News during a wine and tapas-fueled reception on the convention center floor. F-110 frigate. Navantia image “All Navantia ships have a U.S. legacy because we came from a very long-standing relationship with the United States,” de la Cueva said. “We learned from Bath Iron Works, Gibbs & Cox how to build ships. So these ships pass … [Naval Sea Systems Command]” standards. De la Cueva noted the long relationship Navantia has maintained with major U.S. yards like General Dynamics Bath Iron Works and HII. The company has already provided the U.S. Navy with some information and is waiting to hear about the next steps in the competition. A U.S. variant could feature Lockheed Martin’s Aegis Combat System and the SPY-7 air and defense radar, de la Cueva said. In addition to the Brits and the Spanish, the Italians also have an option for the U.S. should it kick off an international competition. Italy’s Fincantieri, which has its own American subsidiary at Marinette Marine in Wisconsin, could propose the FREMM EVO. That platform is an updated version of the FREMM multi-mission frigate that the U.S. used as the parent design for the Constellation class. “I would call us untapped potential,” Fincantieri Marinette Marine chief executive officer George Moutafis told USNI News in September. The yard is still finishing the Royal Saudi Navy’s multi-mission surface combatant while building the first two Constellation-class frigates and preparing to build the Marine Corps’ Landing Ship Medium. “It’s an evolution of the original version, which is meant to say all the benefits are still there,” Moutafis said of the FREMM EVO. “The hard lines that work well for an [anti-submarine warfare] mission all is there, and they’ve been working on the areas that you would think would be the attractive ones – you know making it more lethal, making it ready to host energy-wise future growth for future missions, bringing in capabilities that have to do again with the ASW mission – and at the same time identifying the ways that it can integrate well with deploying, recovering and managing unmanned elements of across all domains.” The Wisconsin yard currently has about 2,200 employees and would need to hire about 500 over time should it receive a contract to build more frigates. Other possible designs could come out of Japan, South Korea and Turkey, USNI News previously reported . Following a discussion between Trump and Turkish leadership on the sidelines of July’s NATO summit, the Istanbul-class guided-missile frigate built by several Turkish shipyards entered the mix, two sources previously told USNI News. Fincantieri image Perhaps the nation most closely associated with the ongoing conversation about foreign shipbuilding is South Korea, which has pledged to invest $150 billion in the U.S. shipbuilding industry as part of a trade deal in the works with the Trump administration. The Chungnam-class guided-missile frigate, which several South Korean companies build, is one option under consideration, USNI News has learned. Meanwhile, the export version of Japan’s Mitsubishi Heavy Industries’ FFM Mogami-class guided-missile frigate is also on the table. While the Trump administration has repeatedly made its preference for an international competition known, the Navy has experienced setbacks when pursuing foreign designs. When altering the FREMM parent design for the Constellation-class program, Gibbs & Cox made so many changes to meet NAVSEA’s requirements that the commonality between the FREMM and the FFG(X) went from 85 percent to under 15 percent, USNI News reported in 2024 . “The thing that will prevent Constellation 2.0 is stop changing the requirement. If you set the requirement and leave it alone, and just let industry build it, whoever that is, that will stop Constellation 2.0,” Babcock’s Hine told USNI News. “Don’t even change the color of the curtains. Just build it,” he added. “It’s this sort of constant fiddling, and I know from being in the [U.K. Royal] Navy for most of my life, that we can’t help ourselves.”

content:
以下是上周西太平洋主要舰船活动和演习的摘要。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，新加坡，一名隶属于第 137 电子攻击中队 (VAQ) 的美国水手在尼米兹级航空母舰西奥多·罗斯福号 (CVN-71) 机库湾对 E/A-18G 咆哮者进行维护。美国海军照片 西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群于周日从新加坡出发。该打击群包括西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰（CVN-71）及其第11舰载机联队（CVW）、长津号巡洋舰（CG-65）以及保罗·汉密尔顿号驱逐舰（DDG-60）和迪凯特号（DDG-73）。西奥多·罗斯福、长津和迪凯特向西航行进入马六甲海峡，而保罗·汉密尔顿则向东航行进入南中国海。西奥多·罗斯福号、长津号和迪凯特号目前正在印度洋前往美国中央司令部。日本横须贺附近 印度海军 Shivalik 级隐形多用途护卫舰 INS Sahyadri (F 49)、日本海上自卫队日向级直升机驱逐舰 JS Ise (DDH 182)、最上级护卫舰 JS Mogami (FFM 1)、澳大利亚皇家海军安扎克级护卫舰 HMAS Stuart (FFH 153) 和美国海军 San 2026 年 11 月 7 日，安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞运输舰安克雷奇号 (LPD-23) 和约翰·穆萨号 (LPD-26) 在 2026 年马拉巴尔演习期间在西太平洋编队航行。美国海军照片 2026 年马拉巴尔四方演习于周四在日本横须贺附近海域结束。
参与的资产包括日本海上自卫队直升机驱逐舰 JS Ise (DDH-182)、护卫舰 JS Mogami (FFM-1)、日本海上自卫队潜艇和 P-1 海上巡逻机 (MPA)、印度海军护卫舰 INS Sahyadri (F49)、澳大利亚皇家海军护卫舰 HMAS Stuart (FFH153) 和澳大利亚皇家空军 P-8A Poseidon MPA、美国海军 P-8A 海神 MPA 和两栖运输船坞 USS Anchorage (LPD-23) 和 USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26)。安克雷奇号和约翰·P·穆萨号与两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 以及已登船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队组成了马金岛两栖待命大队。据当地船舶观察员称，这三艘船均于周六从横须贺舰队活动司令部（CFAY）出发。 2026 年 11 月 8 日，在日本横须贺，美国海军陆战队海军陆战队海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364（加强型）的飞行员从圣安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞舰安克雷奇 (LPD-23) 的飞行甲板上驾驶一架 MV-22B 鱼鹰。美国海军照片安克雷奇于周五返回横须贺，目前停泊据当地船舶观察员称，那里近海。据当地船舶观察员称，澳大利亚皇家海军斯图尔特号护卫舰在参加 2026 年马拉巴尔演习后于周四返回横须贺。据当地船舶观察员称，印度海军护卫舰 INS Sahyadri 于周四返回横须贺，并于周五离开。
据当地船舶观测员称，潜艇补给船弗兰克·凯布尔号 (AS-40) 于周三驶入横须贺指挥官舰队活动基地。在西太平洋，隶属于海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364 的美国海军陆战队 CH-53 种马准备从圣安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞舰约翰·P·穆萨号 (LPD-26) 的飞行甲板起飞， 2026 年 11 月 9 日。美国海军照片 两栖攻击舰马金岛号和两栖运输船坞约翰·P·穆萨号正在美国第七舰队作战区域航行。在菲律宾海 台湾民族党秘书长吴钊燮于 2026 年 11 月 12 日发布的图片

In Singapore A U.S. sailor assigned to Electronic Attack Squadron (VAQ) 137 conducts maintenance on an E/A-18G Growler in the hangar bay of Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), Nov. 9, 2026. The strike group includes aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) with embarked carrier air wing (CVW) 11, cruiser USS Chosin (CG-65) and destroyers USS Paul Hamilton (DDG-60) and USS Decatur (DDG-73). Theodore Roosevelt , Chosin and Decatur sailed west to enter the Malacca Strait while Paul Hamilton sailed east into the South China Sea. Theodore Roosevelt , Chosin and Decatur are now in the Indian Ocean en route to U.S. Central Command. Murtha (LPD-26) sail in formation in the Western Pacific Ocean during Exercise Malabar 2026, Nov. 7, 2026. RAN frigate HMAS Stuart returned on Thursday to Yokosuka after its participation in Exercise Malabar 2026, according to local ship spotters . Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri returned on Thursday to Yokosuka and departed on Friday, according to local ship spotters . Submarine tender USS Frank Cable (AS-40) pulled into Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka on Wednesday, according to local ship spotters . In the Western Pacific A U.S. Marine Corps CH-53 Stallion, attached to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364, prepares to take off from the flight deck aboard San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock ship USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26), Nov. 9, 2026. US Navy photo Amphibious assault ship Makin Island and amphibious transport dock John P. Murtha are underway in U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations. In the Philippine Sea A graphic posted Nov. 12, 2026, by Joseph Wu, Secretary General of Taiwan’s National Security Council. Taiwan National Security Council graphic The People’s Liberation Army Navy Liaoning CSG is operating in the Philippine Sea waters east of the Philippine island of Samar as of Thursday, according to a graphic posted by Joseph Wu, Secretary General of Taiwan’s National Security Council. The CSG was last visually sighted in October. The Liaoning CSG previously included aircraft carrier CNS Liaoning (16) cruisers CNS Anshan (101) and CNS Wuxi (104) and destroyer CNS Huainan (123) but the accompanying ships to the carrier may have changed since. In the South China Sea (L-R) Able Seaman Maritime Logistic – Supply Chain Leah Locke and Able Seaman Maritime Logistic – Supply Chain Grace Reading lay wreaths during a wreath laying ceremony for Remembrance Day during a Regional Presence Deployment 2026 on Nov. 10, 2026. Australian Defense photo Royal Australian Navy fleet oiler HMAS Stalwart (A304) is operating in the South China Sea waters near Brunei on the Royal Australian Navy’s regional presence deployment. On Wednesday , the ship conducted a Remembrance Day wreath laying ceremony with Royal Brunei Navy offshore patrol vessel KDB Darulaman (08). In Guam The ROKN Joint Cruise Training Task Force, 741 second year cadets from three service academies and the Armed Forces Nursing Academy were in Guam for a port visit on Nov. 9, 2026. US Navy photo The ROKN Joint Cruise Training Task Force, 741 second year cadets from three service academies and the Armed Forces Nursing Academy were in Guam as of Monday on a port visit. The task force includes amphibious assault ship ROKS Marado (LPH-6112) and amphibious landing ships ROKS Ilchulbong (LST-688) and ROKS Nojeokbong (LST-689), along with embarked Republic of Korea Marine Corps (ROKMC) MUH-1 Marineon helicopters. In Kangwon Province, North Korea North Korea leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction site of a new naval base on Nov. 11, 2026, in Thongchon County, Kangwon Province. State media Korea Central News Agency photo North Korea leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction site of a new naval base on Wednesday in Thongchon County, Kangwon Province, located on North Korea’s east coast, state media Korean Central News Agency reported. In Maizuru, Japan Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) departed JMSDF Maizuru Naval Base on Nov. 10, 2026. JMSDF photo Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) departed JMSDF Maizuru Naval Base on Tuesday after completing a five-day port visit that began on Nov. 6. Spey with sister ship HMS Tamar (P233) are forwarded deployed to the Indo-Pacific. Near Yonaguni Island and Taiwan A Chinese BZK-005 reconnaissance UAV on Nov. 11, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Wednesday, a suspected Chinese Unmanned Aerial Vehicle flew in from the East China Sea, passed between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan and reached the Philippine Sea. The UAV then turned back when it reached a point east of the northeast tip of Taiwan and flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan to return to the East China Sea. Fighter aircraft from the Japan Air Self-Defense Force Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. Also on Wednesday, a Chinese BZK-005 reconnaissance UAV flew in from the East China Sea, passing between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan to enter the Philippine Sea. The drone then flew south until it was east of the northwest tip of Taiwan and conducted a circuit flight before returning back the same way to the East China Sea. JASDF fighter aircraft from the JASDF Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. Suspected Chinese UAV flight paths on Nov. 11, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office map On Thursday, a suspected Chinese UAV flew in from the East China Sea and entered the Philippine Sea, flying between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan. The suspected drone was east of the northeast tip of Taiwan before its track was lost. Later that same day, another suspected Chinese UAV was tracked from the Philippine Sea east of the northeast tip of Taiwan. The UAV flew north and entered the East China Sea after flying between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan. Japan’s Joint Staff Office issued a news release on the flights, indicating the flights were conducted by different UAVs. Fighter aircraft from the JASDF Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled to intercept. In the East China Sea A Chinese Y-9 Electronic Intelligence aircraft on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Tuesday, a Chinese Y-9 Electronic Intelligence aircraft flew in from China and flew from an area south of the Danjo Islands in the East China Sea to a position northwest of Okinawa. After completing a patrol circuit, the Y-9 flew back to China. In response, JASDF fighter aircraft were scrambled. In the Miyako Strait PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fast combat support ship CNS Hulunhu (901) on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fast combat support ship CNS Hulunhu (901) were spotted on Thursday sailing south 60 kilometers – 37 miles – west of Kume Island. The ships sailed southeast between Okinawa and Miyako Island to enter the Philippine Sea. A JMSDF P-1 MPA of Fleet Air Wing 1 and a JMSDF P-3C Orion MPA shadowed the PLAN ships. In La Pérouse Strait A Russian Navy Kilo-class submarine, amphibious landing ship RFS Nikolai Vilkov (081) and tugboat Fotiy Krylov on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo A Russian Navy Kilo-class submarine, amphibious landing ship RFS Nikolai Vilkov (081) and tugboat Fotiy Krylov were sighted sailing west 40 kilometers – 25 miles – northeast of Cape Soya on the main island of Hokkaido late Tuesday. From Tuesday to Wednesday, the submarine and ships sailed west through La Pérouse Strait, which separates Hokkaido from Russia’s Sakhalin Island, to enter the Sea of Japan. JMSDF fast attack craft JS Umitaka (PG-828) and a JMSDF P-3C Orion MPA shadowed the Russian submarine and ships. This post was written by Dzirhan Mahadzir.

title: Japan Pledges Drones, Coastal Defense Radar in Latest Philippine Defense Package
zh_title: 日本承诺在菲律宾最新的国防计划中提供无人机和海防雷达
source: 美国海军学院工作人员（大量国会报告每周2-3次）
summary: BRP Jose Rizal 与两艘日本海上自卫队舰艇进行演习。菲律宾海军照片 日本将在东京最新的防御计划中向菲律宾军方转让无人机和海岸防御雷达系统，以增强马尼拉的军队。日本驻菲律宾大使北川胜郎和菲律宾外交部长特蕾莎·拉扎罗周一签署了一项协议，涵盖通过官方安全援助计划提供价值高达 2700 万美元的防务转移。此次援助标志着首次通过
content:
BRP Jose Rizal 与两艘日本海上自卫队舰艇进行演习。菲律宾海军照片 日本将在东京最新的防御计划中向菲律宾军方转让无人机和海岸防御雷达系统，以增强马尼拉的军队。日本驻菲律宾大使北川胜郎和菲律宾外交部长特蕾莎·拉扎罗周一签署了一项协议，涵盖通过官方安全援助计划提供价值高达 2700 万美元的防务转移。据日本外务省周一发布的新闻稿称，此次援助标志着首次通过专用海岸雷达系统向菲律宾转移国防设备。该雷达将由菲律宾海军操作，菲律宾海军是日本类似监视系统的先前接收者。上个月在马尼拉举行的日本自卫队成立 72 周年招待会上，日本公司展示了各种打算出售或转让给菲律宾军方的海岸监视系统。这些雷达包括能够跟踪 24 海里外船只的短程系统，以及能够感知 140 海里外海上目标的功能更强大的多用途雷达。除了海域意识援助外，菲律宾空军还将接收型号和数量不详的无人机。 2025年夏天，东京通过OSA向马来西亚转让了14架Aerobo Wing AS-VT02A无人机，价值高达270万美元。
此次移交是马尼拉和东京之间的首次无人移交。此前，日本将TC-90涡轮螺旋桨飞机移交给菲律宾海军航空联队用于海上巡逻。日本大使馆的新闻稿称：“该项目对于进一步促进日本和菲律宾之间的安全合作、加强日本重要海上通道的安全以及维护和加强地区和平与稳定具有重要意义。”近年来，由于对南中国海和吕宋海峡的共同担忧，东京与马尼拉寻求更密切的防务关系。自 2010 年代以来一些最重要的进展包括承诺为菲律宾海岸警卫队提供 17 艘巡逻舰，以及日本自卫队作战部队抵达东南亚群岛进行演习。今年，日本军队与美国、菲律宾和加拿大军队一起演习，保卫吕宋岛北部的海滩。东京首次全面实战演习以在击沉演习中发射反舰导弹而达到高潮。新的国防装备转让指南也为前日本自卫队装备出售或转让给菲律宾军方开辟了新的机会。目前正在讨论将即将退役的阿巴库巴级护卫舰转移给菲律宾海军。

【原文 English Original】
BRP Jose Rizal conducts exercises with two Japan Maritime Self-Defense ships. Philippine Navy photo Japan will transfer unmanned aerial vehicles and a coastal defense radar system to the Philippine military in Tokyo’s latest defense package to bolster Manila’s forces. Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Katsuro Kitagawa and Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Theresa Lazaro signed an agreement on Monday covering the defense transfer worth up to $27 million via the Official Security Assistance program. The assistance marks the first transfer of defense equipment to the Philippines via a dedicated coastal radar system, as classified by a Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs news release published on Monday. This radar will be operated by the Philippine Navy, which has been the previous recipient of similar surveillance systems from Japan. At the 72nd Japan Self-Defense Force anniversary reception in Manila last month, Japanese firms showcased a variety of coastal watch systems intended for sale or transfer to the Philippine military. These ranged from short-range systems capable of tracking vessels out to 24 nautical miles to more capable multirole radars that can sense maritime targets 140 nautical miles away. Alongside the maritime domain awareness assistance, the Philippine Air Force will receive an unspecified variant and quantity of UAVs. In the summer of 2025, Tokyo transferred 14 Aerobo Wing AS-VT02A UAVs worth up to $2.7 million to Malaysia through OSA. The latest transfer is the first instance of unmanned transfers between Manila and Tokyo. Previously, Japan handed over TC-90 turboprops to the Philippine Naval Air Wing for maritime patrols. “This project is of great importance in further promoting security cooperation between Japan and the Philippines, enhancing security of important sea lanes for Japan, and contributing to maintaining and strengthening regional peace and stability,” reads the Japanese Embassy release. In recent years, Tokyo has pursued closer defense relations with Manila amid mutual concerns over the South China Sea and Luzon Strait. Some of the most significant developments since the 2010s include the commitment of 17 patrol ships for the Philippine Coast Guard and the arrival of Japan Self-Defense Force combat troops for drills across the Southeast Asian archipelago. This year, Japanese troops drilled alongside American, Philippine and Canadian forces to defend a beach in Northern Luzon. Tokyo’s full-scale combat exercise debut culminated with the launch of anti-ship missiles at a sinking exercise. New defense equipment transfer guidelines are also opening up new opportunities for ex-JSDF equipment to be sold or transferred to the Philippine military. Discussions are ongoing to transfer soon-to-be retired Abakumba-class destroyer escorts to the Philippine Navy.

title: Destroyer returns from 11-month-deployment
zh_title: 驱逐舰结束 11 个月的部署返回
summary: 夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。斯普鲁亚
content:
夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《国防一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

【原文 English Original】
PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . But a Navy official confirmed to Defense One that his plans were changed when the Michael Murphy’s previous boss, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, was relieved on Sept. 27 due to a “loss of confidence” after roughly 11 months in charge.    At Thursday’s homecoming, Petty Officer 3rd Class Jesse Bryson was first off the ship, as the winner of the “first kiss” raffle. Standing with his wife, Arianna Rios, he joked that the deployment involved “a lot of water.” “Join the Navy, see the world—but the world is 70-percent water,” he said with a laugh. But, he added, the crew was great. “I think you could put anyone from this ship on any other ship and they’d stand out,” Bryson said. ]]>

title: New Bow Sonar Dome For Heavily Damaged Submarine USS Connecticut Seen For The First Time (Updated)
zh_title: 首次出现严重受损的康涅狄格号潜艇的新弓声纳罩（更新）
summary: TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 达成了
content:
TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 联系我们，要求在进行额外审查时删除圆顶的图像。出于礼貌，我们同意了，如果完全获得批准，我们将重新发布它。 Janicki Industries 今天告诉我们，该公司在大约 10 个月内生产出了新型船首声纳导流罩，并于 2024 年交付给海军。据其网站称，Janicki 拥有为美国核潜艇项目生产“声纳罩和精密加工硬件”的历史。它还支持各种备受瞩目的航空航天项目，包括 B-21 袭击者轰炸机和 F-35 联合攻击战斗机。根据一份经过大量编辑的海军事故报告，康涅狄格号的船头在五年前的碰撞事件发生后，最初至少在某种程度上仍然保持着连接状态。然而，当潜艇一瘸一拐地驶向关岛时，整个船首结构随后断裂。
随后，这艘船驶往加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥，然后前往华盛顿州的普吉特海湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施 (PSNS-IMF)，此后一直待在那里。 2023 年，在普吉特湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施中看到的康涅狄格号航空母舰，其船首圆顶明显缺失。美国海军“普吉特海湾海军造船厂和国际货币基金组织（中间维护设施）需要按照船的计划，在其后面没有生产线的情况下安装一个精密的替换圆顶，”贾尼基在撰写本文时还在其网站上表示。 “Janicki 比次佳选择快了 24 个月，因为工作所需的一切都集中在一个屋檐下：适合半球的 5 轴铣床、证明这一点的计量方法以及形成双曲板的 1,000 吨压力机。”本文顶部的部分图片和下面的完整图片显示了 Janicki 专有的五轴铣床在圆顶上工作的情况。海狼级潜艇艏声纳导流罩的尺寸和复杂性怎么强调都不为过。这些船上的船首声纳阵列直径为 24 英尺。圆顶本身的结构必须按照非常严格的规格建造，以使声纳系统正常工作。海狼级潜艇上的艏声纳阵列，其艏穹顶被拆除。公共领域 过去的五角大楼预算文件和国会拨款法案已经强调了更换康涅狄格州弓形声纳罩的预期成本和复杂性。
2021 年，立法者批准了 1000 万美元专门用于圆顶的资金，以及 4000 万美元用于其他“紧急维修”。全部维修费用仍不得而知，但预计将远高于 5000 万美元。 在 2024 年发布的 2025 财年预算提案中，海军还概述了购买额外船首圆顶的计划，以防其任何一艘“海狼”级潜艇再次遭受类似的严重事故。 “海狼级潜艇的保障战略不包括提供替换潜艇

【原文 English Original】
TWZ has obtained new details about the ongoing repairs to the Seawolf class submarine USS Connecticut following collision with an underwater seamount in the South China Sea in 2021. The Navy had been looking at a roughly three-year timeline for the construction of a replacement bow sonar dome. In the end, it took just under a year for it to be built. The overall schedule for repairs to Connecticut has suffered delays, and we were the first to report that the boat is now not expected to return to service until next summer. Editor’s note: After this story was published, Janicki Industries reached out to us to ask that the image of the dome be taken down while an additional review is conducted. Out of courtesy, we agreed, and we will repost it if and when it is fully approved. Janicki Industries produced the new bow sonar dome in approximately 10 months and delivered it to the Navy in 2024, the company told us today. Janicki has a history of producing “sonar domes and precision machined hardware” for U.S. nuclear submarine programs, according to its website . It has also supported various high-profile aerospace programs, including the B-21 Raider bomber and F-35 Joint Strike Fighter . Connecticut ’s bow had initially remained attached, at least to some degree, following the collision five years ago, according to a heavily redacted Navy report on the accident . However, the entire bow structure subsequently broke away as the submarine limped to Guam . The boat then sailed to San Diego, California , and then to the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS-IMF) in Washington State, where it has been ever since. USS Connecticut seen at the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility in 2023 with its bow dome prominently missing. USN “Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & IMF [Intermediate Maintenance Facility] needed a precision replacement dome with no production line behind it, on the boat’s schedule,” Janicki also says on its website at the time of writing . “Janicki delivered it 24 months faster than the next-best option because everything the job needed sits under one roof: 5-axis mills that fit a hemisphere, the metrology to prove it, and the 1,000-ton press that forms double-curved plate.” The picture seen in part at the top of this story and in full below shows one of Janicki’s proprietary five-axis milling machines at work on the dome. The size and complexity of the bow sonar dome on Seawolf class submarines cannot be overstated. The bow sonar arrays on these boats is 24 feet in diameter. The structure of the dome itself has to be built to very exacting specifications for the sonar system to work properly. A look at the bow sonar array on a Seawolf class submarine with its bow dome removed. Public Domain Past Pentagon budget documents and appropriations bills from Congress had already highlighted the expected costs and complexities of replacing Connecticut ’s bow sonar dome. In 2021, lawmakers approved $10 million in funding specifically for the dome, as well as $40 million for other “emergent repairs.” The full repair bill is still unknown, but is expected to be far steeper than just $50 million. In its Fiscal Year 2025 budget proposal , released in 2024, the Navy also outlined plans to acquire an additional bow dome in case any of its Seawolf class submarines suffered another similarly severe mishap. “The Seawolf Class submarines sustainment strategy did not include the provisioning of replacement bow domes; therefore, no replacement bow domes for these in-service submarines are within the Navy’s inventory,” the budget documents explained. “This program would procure one Seawolf Class bow dome for use in the event replacement is required. Funds in FY25 are to purchase a bow dome which has a three plus year lead time.” Note here the mention of a lead time of at least three years, which is in line with Janicki’s statement that the “next-best option” would have taken two years more to do this work. As TWZ has highlighted in years of reporting now, repairs to Connecticut , in general, were always set to be challenging and costly due to the small size of the Seawolf class and the design being long out of production. The Navy originally planned to acquire 29 of these boats, but ultimately bought just three as a result of post-Cold War drawdowns. In addition, shrinking the program of record so severely caused the unit price of each one to rise substantially, just over $10 billion in 2025 dollars. At the time of writing, they are still the most costly attack submarines ever built. The last of the Seawolf class submarines, the highly secretive USS Jimmy Carter , which entered service in 2005, is also a heavily modified sub-type optimized for underwater espionage missions . USS Connecticut at sea in 2009. USN It is also worth noting that the U.S. Navy, as well as some of its foreign counterparts , have repaired similarly severe damage to submarines by cannibalizing entire sections from decommissioned boats in the same class. However, this is not an option given the size of the Seawolf class and the still very high demand for them operationally . The core design offers advanced capabilities that make even USS Seawolf and USS Connecticut especially well suited to a variety of specialized tasks . This is clearly why the Navy has continued to invest so much in returning Connecticut to the fleet. As mentioned, repairs to Connecticut are now not expected to be finished until sometime in the summer of next year. This is the latest in a succession of schedule slips in recent years. The original goal had been for the boat to be back in service by September 2025. “The Navy’s target completion date for the availability is the summer of 2027. PSNS & IMF is dedicated to executing this work with the highest standards of safety, technical accuracy, and craftsmanship to ensure the ship returns to the fleet ready to take its place at the tip of the spear in defense of our nation’s interests,” a Navy official told TWZ in September. “Current work consists of structural and systems restoration and required lifecycle maintenance.” Earlier in the year, the Navy also revealed that it is now planning on sending Connecticut into retirement in 2031. This means the submarine has just four more years of service ahead of it if the current repair schedule holds. The Navy does have plans to acquire a new class of nuclear attack submarines, currently referred to as SSN(X). In the past, the service has described those future boats as more of a direct successor to the Seawolf class than the versions of the Virginia class it is buying now. A picture of the first-in-class USS Seawolf . USN “The analytical conclusion was unequivocal: to dominate high-end peer threats in the middle of this century, a clean sheet design is required. The Virginia class is a fantastic, unmatched world-class warship, and it will remain the backbone of our attack fleet for decades,” Navy Rear Adm. Andrew Miller said at the Naval Submarine League’s main annual conference last week, per USNI News . “As adversary capabilities evolve, we require expanded payload capacity, greater electrical and hydrodynamic margins and unprecedented architectural flexibility that simply cannot be backfitted into an existing hull form.” Miller is currently the head of the Undersea Warfare Division with the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations. In terms of desired key capabilities for SSN(X), the Navy wants “first, higher flank speed and tactical control speed. Two, improved operational availability. Three, decisive lethality. Four, superior stealth and layered survivability, and finally organic robotic and autonomous systems hosting and command and control,” Miller added. “We are redefining the role of the submarine from a standalone hunter-killer to a capital mothership. By launching uncrewed systems directly from submarine torpedo tubes and integrating unmanned [robotic] vehicles into our battle plans, we dramatically expand the tactical reach of our manned fleet.” The first SSN(X) submarines are not expected to begin entering service until the mid-2040s, at the earliest. The Navy will continue acquiring Virginia class submarines in the interim. This includes stretched Block IV and V versions with Virginia Payload Modules (VPM) that will now be categorized as guided-missile types (SSGN). There will also be a one-of-a-kind seabed warfare version of the Virginia , which could well take over for the USS Jimmy Carter. A briefing slide from General Dynamics Electric Boat detailing existing and future planned subvariants of the Virginia class nuclear submarine. The Block VI and V types have now been reclassified as nuclear-powered guided missile submarines (SSGN) rather than nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSN). General Dynamics Electric Boat When it comes to USS Connecticut , if there are no further delays, the fully repaired submarine with its new bow sonar dome should be back in service by the middle of next year. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post New Bow Sonar Dome For Heavily Damaged Submarine USS Connecticut Seen For The First Time (Updated) appeared first on TWZ .

title: USS Theodore Roosevelt Now in the Middle East, Lincoln’s Last Escorts Finally Home
zh_title: 西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰现已抵达中东，林肯最后的护航终于回家
summary: 2026 年 11 月 15 日，西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 穿越印度洋。作为计划部署的一部分，该航母目前正在美国中央司令部责任区执行任务。美国海军照片 美国第三艘航空母舰及其护航舰现在位于中东。西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 于周日加入美国第五舰队。随着美国和伊朗之间的紧张局势持续存在，西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群的到来使美国在中东地区出现了三个航母打击群。周末，胡塞武装继续占领巴布埃尔附近地区。
content:
2026 年 11 月 15 日，西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 穿越印度洋。作为计划部署的一部分，该航母目前正在美国中央司令部责任区执行任务。美国海军照片 美国第三艘航空母舰及其护航舰现在位于中东。西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 于周日加入美国第五舰队。随着美国和伊朗之间的紧张局势持续存在，西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群的到来使美国在中东地区出现了三个航母打击群。周末，胡塞武装继续对曼德海峡（连接亚丁湾与红海的战略要道）周围地区提出主权要求，而伊朗军队则声称他们周五袭击了位于巴林的美国雷达。美国中央司令部否认了社交媒体网站 X 上发布的有关伊斯兰革命卫队在巴林发射两架单向无人机并被击落的说法。 2026 年 11 月 16 日，美国水兵在尼米兹级航空母舰西奥多·罗斯福号 (CVN-71) 的飞行甲板上使用分配给第 8 直升机海上作战中队 (HSC) 的 MH-60S 海鹰进行飞行作业。西奥多·罗斯福号被部署到美国第五舰队作战区域，以支持中东的海上安全与稳定。美国海军照片 西奥多·罗斯福预计将接替 8 月底抵达中东的乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73)。
虽然 GW 最终接替了亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰 (CVN-72)，但在安倍回国之前，这两艘航母都与乔治·H·W·布什号航空母舰 (CVN-77) 一起在中东执行任务大约一个月。目前尚不清楚 GW 将在 TR 抵达后在该地区停留多久。布什、GW和TR在中东的存在是以美国航母在印太地区的存在为代价的。安倍在部署 321 天后启程回国，而其两艘护航舰——迈克尔·墨菲号 (DDG-112) 和斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111)——则留在了后方。迈克尔·墨菲 (Michael Murphy) 在服役 346 天后于周四返回家中，而斯普鲁恩斯 (Spruance) 在服役 357 天后于周六返回家中。斯普鲁恩斯的部署时间比安倍多了 36 天，创下了驱逐舰部署的记录。阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111) 于 2026 年 11 月 13 日返回圣地亚哥海军基地母港，结束了在美国第 3、第 7 和第 5 舰队作战区域为期 12 个月的战斗部署。美国海军照片 对于驱逐舰来说，长达近一年的部署是罕见的，它们通常会部署六到七个月。然而，海军警告水手和家属，随着海上服务试图满足政府的需求，部署将持续近一年。斯普鲁恩斯于 2025 年 11 月 21 日从加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥海军基地部署。
据海军发布的宣布该驱逐舰回归的消息称，该驱逐舰在第三、第五和第七舰队中服役，在整个部署过程中航行了超过 88,000 海里。 2026 年 11 月 13 日，海军水手和亲人欢迎阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111) 返回其母港圣地亚哥海军基地，结束了在美国第三、第七和第五舰队行动区为期 12 个月的战斗部署。美国海军照片 斯普鲁恩斯号在部署期间参与了史诗狂怒行动，在此期间，作为持续海上封锁的一部分，驱逐舰禁用了货船 M/V Touska。虽然新闻稿称该舰发射了战斧导弹，但没有详细说明

【原文 English Original】
USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) transits the Indian Ocean, Nov. 15, 2026. The aircraft carrier is currently operating in the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility as part of a scheduled deployment. US Navy photo A third U.S. aircraft carrier and its escorts are now in the Middle East. USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) chopped into U.S. 5th Fleet on Sunday. The arrival of the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group makes three U.S. carrier strike groups in the Middle East, as tensions persist between the U.S. and Iran. Over the weekend, the Houthis continued to claim areas around the Bab el-Mandeb – the strategic chokepoint that connects the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea – while Iranian forces claim they attacked a U.S. radar in Bahrain on Friday. U.S. Central Command denied the claim posting on social media site X that the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps launched two one-way drones at Bahrain, which were shot down. U.S. sailors conduct flight operations with an MH-60S Sea Hawk assigned to Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron (HSC) 8 on the flight deck of Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), Nov. 16, 2026. Theodore Roosevelt is deployed to the U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations to support maritime security and stability in the Middle East. US Navy photo Theodore Roosevelt is expected to relieve USS George Washington (CVN-73), which arrived in the Middle East toward the end of August . While GW ultimately relieved USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72), the two carriers both operated in the Middle East, along with USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77), for about a month before Abe headed home. It is unclear how long GW will stay in the area with TR’s arrival. Bush , GW and TR’s presence in the Middle East comes at the cost of the U.S. carrier presence in the Indo-Pacific region. While Abe headed home after 321 days on deployment, two of its escorts – USS Michael Murphy (DDG-112) and USS Spruance (DDG-111) – stayed behind. Michael Murphy returned home Thursday after 346 days deployed, while Spruance returned home on Saturday after 357 days deployed. Spruance’s deployment came in at 36 days more than Abe and set a record for destroyer deployments. Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance (DDG-111) returns to its home port of Naval Base San Diego, Nov. 13, 2026, concluding a 12-month combat deployment across the U.S. 3rd, 7th, and 5th fleet areas of operations. US Navy photo Nearly year-long deployments are rare for destroyers, which usually go out for six to seven months. However, the Navy has warned sailors and families to expect deployments that approach a year as the sea service attempts to keep up the needs of the administration. Spruance deployed on Nov. 21, 2025, from Naval Base San Diego, Calif. The destroyer operated in the 3rd, 5th and 7th fleets, traveling more than 88,000 nautical miles throughout its deployments, according to a Navy release announcing the destroyer’s return. U.S. Navy sailors and loved ones welcome Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance (DDG-111) as it returns to its home port of Naval Base San Diego, Nov. 13, 2026, concluding a 12-month combat deployment across the U.S. 3rd, 7th, and 5th fleet areas of operations. US Navy photo While deployed, Spruance was part of Operation Epic Fury, during which the destroyer disabled cargo vessel M/V Touska as part of the ongoing maritime blockade. While the release said the ship launched Tomahawk missiles, it did not go into details about the Iranian military targets. The destroyer did take out 12 drones and four anti-ship cruise missiles while in the Middle East, according to the Navy release. The “Raptors” of HSM-71 embarked on Spruance and flew 190 sorties during the deployment, reads the release. Spruance received the Presidential Unit Citation and Combat Action Ribbon following its role in Operation Epic Fury. The destroyer has been busy over the past two years. Before its most recent deployment, the ship was part of U.S. Northern Command’s southern border operations, leaving San Diego in March 2025. Prior to that, Spruance spent five months in the Middle East as part of the U.S. response to Houthi attacks on commercial shipping, coming home on Dec. 19, 2024.

summary: 2026 年 2 月 28 日，阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰小弗兰克·E·彼得森号 (DDG-121) 在支持史诗狂怒行动的行动中发射战斧对地攻击导弹。美国海军照片 海军空战中心武器部门上周宣布，将于 2027 年 6 月开始制造战斧巡航导弹弹头的组件，届时一种新型炸药和推进剂混合器上线。 11 月 9 日，由 B&P Littleford 制造的新型 300 加仑搅拌机在加利福尼亚州中国湖推进实验室举行剪彩仪式。一旦混音器上线
content:
2026 年 2 月 28 日，阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰小弗兰克·E·彼得森号 (DDG-121) 在支持史诗狂怒行动的行动中发射战斧对地攻击导弹。美国海军照片 海军空战中心武器部门上周宣布，将于 2027 年 6 月开始制造战斧巡航导弹弹头的组件，届时一种新型炸药和推进剂混合器上线。 11 月 9 日，由 B&P Littleford 制造的新型 300 加仑搅拌机在加利福尼亚州中国湖推进实验室举行剪彩仪式。 NAWCD 在一份新闻稿中表示，一旦混合器上线，NAWCD 的弹头生产团队将努力在制造商雷神公司需要弹头之前准备好弹头，帮助确保连续、准时地将战斧交付给舰队。 8月，海军授予雷神公司一份价值229亿美元的合同，以加速战斧生产，目标是每年生产1000多枚导弹。在“史诗狂怒行动”之后，国防部一直在努力增加和加速导弹和弹药的生产，该行动导致弹药迅速消耗。五角大楼的努力还集中于扩大制造商和供应商的国防工业基础，建设产能和冗余。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，来宾聚集在大型混合湾，观看中国湖推进实验室剪彩后新型 300 加仑混合机的演示。
一旦在 2027 年 6 月左右上线，混合器将使海军空战中心武器部门的能量团队达到为舰队生产战斧弹头的生产率。美国海军照片推进和能量部门负责人瑞安·亨特在新闻稿中表示，更快的生产需要更大的弹头容量。中国湖的海军实验室和马里兰州海军水面作战中心印度司令部表示，他们可以进行弹头的生产工作。目前，雷神公司是战斧制造的主要承包商，而通用动力军械和战术系统公司负责加工弹头箱，而 L3Harris 则为其装载炸药。 9 月，L3Harris 和 NAWCWD 签署了一项多年的公私合作伙伴关系，以制造导弹部件。亨特说，根据该协议，NAWCWD 计划生产部分战斧弹头。一年前，当 NAWCD 能源团队从博物馆取出一个战斧弹头盒时，NAWCD 开始了拥有制造战斧弹头能力的过程。能源团队将炸药和火箭推进剂混合，并将其装入海军武器中。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，中国湖推进实验室大型混合舱中，新型 300 加仑行星混合器的叶片位于混合碗上方。该混合器将于 2027 年 6 月左右投入使用，将使海军空战中心武器部门的能量团队达到舰队战斧弹头的生产率。
美国海军照片 该团队清理了箱子并混合了 PBXN-107 炸药并填充了 WDU-36/B 弹头。测试、成像和 X 射线证实该团队正确填充了它。经过这一努力，今年秋天，同一个团队填充了七个首件战斧弹头，这是新生产商建造的第一批用于检查的装置。能量处理部门负责人赞恩·戈德特表示，一旦通过，它们将成为“中国湖”的第一批生产弹头。弹头由中国湖运行了数十年的 150 加仑混合器填充，新的混合器将取代它。在演示构建过程中，团队还发现

Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121) fires a Tomahawk Land Attack Missile during operations in support of Operation Epic Fury, Feb. 28, 2026. US Navy photo The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division will begin making a component for Tomahawk cruise missile warheads in June of 2027 when a new explosive and propellant mixer comes online, the division announced last week. A new 300 gallon mixer, built by B&P Littleford was inaugurated in a ribbon cutting ceremony on Nov. 9 at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory in California. Once the mixer is online, NAWCD’s warhead production team will work to have warheads ready before manufacturer Raytheon needs them, helping ensure continuous, on-time Tomahawk deliveries to the fleet, NAWCD said in a news release . In August, the Navy awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion contract to accelerate Tomahawk production with a target of producing more than 1,000 missiles annually. The Department of Defense has been carrying out efforts to increase and accelerate productions of missiles and munitions following Operation Epic Fury, which has seen munitions rapidly expended. Pentagon efforts have also focused on expanding the defense industrial base of manufacturers and suppliers, building both capacity and redundancy. Guests gather in the large mix bay to watch a demonstration of a new 300-gallon mixer after its ribbon cutting at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. US Navy photo Faster production calls for more warhead capacity, said Ryan Hunter, head of the Propulsion and Energetics Division, in the release. Navy labs at China Lake and at Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division in Maryland said they could do the work to produce warheads. Currently, Raytheon is the prime contractor building Tomahawks while General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems machines the warhead cases and L3Harris loads them with explosives. In September, L3Harris and NAWCWD signed a multi-year public-private partnership to manufacture missile components. Under it, Hunter said, NAWCWD plans to produce a portion of the Tomahawk warheads. NAWCD began the process of having the capability to build Tomahawk warheads a year ago when the NAWCD energetics team pulled a Tomahawk warhead case out of a museum. The energetics team mixes explosives and rocket propellants and loads them into Navy weapons. The blades of a new 300-gallon planetary mixer rest above the mix bowl in the large mix bay at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. US Navy photo The team cleaned the case and mixed PBXN-107 explosive and filled the WDU-36/B warhead. Testing, imaging and X-rays confirmed the team filled it correctly. Following that effort, this fall, the same team filled seven first-article Tomahawk warheads, the first units a new producer builds for inspection. Once they pass, they become China Lake’s first production warheads, said Zane Goedert, head of the Energetics Processing Branch. The warhead was filled by a 150-gallon mixer China Lake has run for decades, which the new mixer will replace. During the demonstration build, the team also found the warhead specification needed a major update. Key parts and materials to address the issue can take up to a year to arrive, reads the NAWCD release. Patricia Hottowe, director of the Tomahawk Technical Project Office at NAWCWD, said in the release that the team spent much of the past year updating the specification and the approved supplier list. The Navy’s technical authority for the warhead must approve each new supplier and every future producer – Navy or industry – must build to that specification. NAWCWD also bought long-lead materials ahead of the multi-year contract, Hottowe said. A dozen new personnel have been hired to join the team, Goedert said. They will train under experienced technicians on safety, quality and procedures for about a year before working on their own. He added that loading the warhead is the easiest part while buying materials, bringing on people and getting answers are harder. Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Delbert D. Black (DDG-119) fires a Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM) in support of Operation Epic Fury, Feb. 28, 2026. US Navy photo The branch has filled warheads for the AGM-84H/K Stand-off Land Attack Missile-Expanded Response (SLAM-E) missile since the mid-1990s. Goedert said his team routinely turns one-of-a-kind prototypes around on short timelines. That experience allowed the team to move faster on Tomahawk. According to Hunter, the challenge comes from a system built for fixed multi-year schedules. Now that system must move faster on a shorter clock. China Lake’s facilities will be able to meet that challenge due to its layout. “Because our plant is dispersed and because we will be curing the warheads in a different area than we’re casting them, we’re able to do simultaneous processes that will get higher throughput,” said Hunter. The plant’s newest buildings grew out of a rebuild as the July 2019 earthquakes destroyed three energetics compounds in the Salt Wells area of the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, reads the release. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command broke ground on their replacements, known as the trio, in April of 2022. Goedert said the team designed the Motor Assembly Compound to cut handling. Large rocket motors risk damage each time crews move them after casting. The same layout will speed warhead work. Rear Adm. Eric Gardner, principal deputy for the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Munitions, spoke at the ribbon cutting and said the first-article warheads will lay the groundwork for China Lake to become an additional source of Tomahawk warhead production. “At PAE Munitions, we know that increasing weapons production takes more than contracts and funding,” Gardner said. “It takes people, infrastructure, materials, and strong partnerships across our Navy, our warfare centers and industry.”

title: The Nvidia Scandal Exposes American Blind Spots
zh_title: 英伟达丑闻暴露美国盲点
source: 欧洲政策分析中心 （CEPA） - CEPA
summary: 华盛顿已经建立了一个复杂的出口管制和许可要求网络，以防止人工智能芯片进入中国。然而，英伟达创始人黄仁勋与被指控向北京传递信息的中国女商人黄爱丽之间明显的“美人计”事件，不仅仅是这些控制措施的盲点问题。它讲述了在全球化、互联的世界中关闭先进技术的困难，以及一家公司、监管机构和行政部门看到了警告信号却迟迟未采取行动。如果现有规则得到执行，Nvidia
content:
华盛顿已经建立了一个复杂的出口管制和许可要求网络，以防止人工智能芯片进入中国。然而，英伟达创始人黄仁勋与被指控向北京传递信息的中国女商人黄爱丽之间明显的“美人计”事件，不仅仅是这些控制措施的盲点问题。它讲述了在全球化、互联的世界中关闭先进技术的困难，以及一家公司、监管机构和行政部门看到了警告信号却迟迟未采取行动。如果现有规则得到执行，英伟达就不应该向总部位于新加坡的云计算公司 Megaspeed International 出售先进芯片。 Alice Huang 是 Megaspeed 的高管，该公司成为 Nvidia 的主要客户，并因可能违反美国出口管制而受到审查。英伟达董事会已聘请外部顾问来调查中国情报部门是否针对其前首席执行官，后者在其事务曝光后辞职。该公司坚称，没有理由相信其机密或国家安全受到损害。这个故事的核心是供应链的不透明性，而它始于 Megaspeed 错综复杂的所有权。该公司于2015年在新加坡注册成立，名称为第七大道国际，是中国网络游戏行业中的新兴企业。它于 2023 年采用现名。
同年晚些时候，Megaspeed 的股份通过一家在英属维尔京群岛注册的公司转让给另一家在新加坡注册的公司 Swiftdata。谁最终控制 Swiftdata 目前尚不清楚。错综复杂的注册流程并不能证明国家控制，中国投资也不等同于中国政府所有权。但中国的国有资本和私人资本经常通过子公司、控股公司和离岸工具进行流动。 Megaspeed 复杂的企业历史本应引发严格审查，审查谁控制该公司以及谁最终将从其购买美国芯片中受益。尽管存在警告信号，Megaspeed 仍成为 Nvidia 的官方云合作伙伴，并购买了价值数十亿美元的先进计算设备。其印度尼西亚子公司进口了最先进的 Nvidia 硬件。美国当局已调查Megaspeed是否也帮助中国客户获得Nvidia芯片。 Megaspeed 否认非法转让，也没有任何公开调查结果证实存在出口管制违规行为。但英伟达面临的问题从来不是违规行为是否得到证实；而是问题。问题在于具有这种特征的客户是否值得信任和访问。 2025 年 8 月，Nvidia 总法律顾问通过电子邮件向负责调查 Megaspeed 的部门特工发送电子邮件，称商务部高级官员已批准此次外展活动。调查已暂停并移交给司法部。
其他机构提议将 Megaspeed 添加到被认为对美国国家安全构成风险的外国企业和组织的实体名单中。商务部从未这样做过。官员们敦促商务部采取行动，国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) 于 2026 年 5 月向商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 发送了一份有关 Megaspeed 的备忘录。据报道，财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 最近与卢特尼克对质，问道：“Megaspeed 为何不在实体名单上？”商务部否认发生过交易。白宫收到警告。据报道，唐纳德·特朗普总统去年年底听取了简报和一份关于爱丽丝的机密备忘录

【原文 English Original】
Washington has built an elaborate web of export controls and licensing requirements to keep artificial intelligence chips from reaching China. Yet Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s apparent “honeytrap” affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing, is about more than the blind spots of those controls. It is about the difficulty of shutting down access to advanced tech in a globalized, interconnected world — and about a company, a regulator, and an executive branch that saw warning signs and were slow act on them. Had existing rules been enforced, Nvidia should never have been selling advanced chips to the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International. Alice Huang was an executive at Megaspeed, which became a major Nvidia customer, and attracted scrutin y over possible violations of American export controls. Nvidia’s board has retained outside counsel to investigate whether Chinese intelligence targeted their former CEO, who resigned after his affairs were revealed. The company maintains that it has no reason to believe its secrets or national security were compromised. At its core, the story is about the opacity of supply chains, and it begins with Megaspeed’s convoluted ownership. The company incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International, emerging from the Chinese online gaming industry. It adopted its current name in 2023. Later that year, Megaspeed’s shares were transferred , through a company registered in the British Virgin Islands, to another Singapore-registered company, Swiftdata. Who ultimately controls Swiftdata remains unclear. Convoluted incorporation trails do not prove state control, and Chinese investment is not synonymous with Chinese government ownership. But state-linked and private Chinese capital often  moves  through subsidiaries, holding companies, and offshore vehicles. Megaspeed’s complex corporate history should have triggered rigorous scrutiny of who controlled the firm and who would ultimately benefit from its purchases of US chips.  Despite the warning signs, Megaspeed became an official Nvidia cloud partner and purchased billions of dollars’ worth of advanced computing equipment. Its Indonesian subsidiary imported cutting-edge Nvidia hardware. US authorities have investigated whether Megaspeed also helped Chinese customers obtain Nvidia chips. Megaspeed has denied illicit transfers, and no public finding has established an export-control violation. But the question for Nvidia was never whether a violation had been proven; it was whether a customer with this profile warranted trust and access. In August 2025, Nvidia’s general counsel  emailed  Department agents investigating Megaspeed, saying that a senior Commerce official had approved the outreach. The investigation was paused and transferred to the Justice Department.  Other agencies proposed adding Megaspeed to the entity list of foreign businesses and organizations that are deemed to pose a risk to US national security. Commerce never did. Officials  pressed  Commerce to act, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick a memorandum on Megaspeed in May 2026. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently reportedly  confronted  Lutnik, asking: “How come Megaspeed isn’t on the entities list?” Commerce denies that the  exchange  took place. The White House was warned. President Donald Trump was reportedly briefed late last year and a classified memorandum on Alice Huang circulated among senior officials before his May visit to China. Apparently, no action was taken. Instead, Nvidia CEO Huang joined the presidential delegation to Beijing and, in September, attended the White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping. Jensen Huang’s own conduct compounded the failure. An executive with his access to the president and to sensitive policy discussions carries a responsibility that goes beyond his obligations to shareholders. A relationship with a foreign national linked to a customer under federal investigation was, at best, reckless. Washington depends on companies such as Nvidia to sustain its technological lead over China, expand domestic computing capacity, and support an increasingly AI-dependent defense posture. Yet these companies  remain  commercial enterprises that  are  accountable to shareholders and driven by incentives that might not always align with national security objectives.  Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular Bandwidth emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. Although enforcing existing export controls would have gone a long way to prevent this crisis, the case reveals a genuine gap. US export controls focus on where advanced chips are shipped, yet access to computing power no longer requires owning the hardware.  Renting “offshore” computing is often legal. A Chinese company banned from purchasing certain advanced US processors may be able to buy computing capacity from servers in another jurisdiction. Megaspeed reportedly  provided computing services to Chinese technology customers, including the Chinese e-commerce leader Alibaba. This gap risks widening as AI infrastructure expands across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and other regions. The US needs to enforce existing rules and close the gaps. First, that means applying export controls consistently. When the evidence warrants, enforcement must be separated from corporate lobbying — and acted on. Second, add access to advanced computing power to export controls, not just the chips themselves. That means know- your-customer  requirements for cloud providers and close monitoring of overseas cloud infrastructure. Third, invest in systematic mapping of corporate ownership and financial networks. Screening named entities is insufficient when relationships extend across holding companies, investment vehicles, and multiple jurisdictions. Chipmakers should be expected to know who ultimately owns their customers. Fourth, establish clear security expectations and channels for intelligence-sharing with executives at the commanding heights of American technology. Congress is preparing to act. Top Republican and Democratic lawmakers hope to  include  three proposed measures toughening rules on exporting AI chips. Three House committee chairs have  demanded  a closed-door briefing from Huang.  His resignation should not end the inquiry. Congress should examine not only whether sensitive information was compromised, but how Megaspeed won Nvidia’s trust, why Commerce never acted, and why intelligence warnings to the executive branch failed to translate into meaningful action. The US has spent years building the tools to control what crosses its borders. But tools are only as strong as the institutions that wield them.
