title: Launch Preview: Ariane 6 to launch Amazon satellites, Falcon 9 to launch government missions
zh_title: 发射预览：阿丽亚娜 6 号将发射亚马逊卫星，猎鹰 9 号将发射政府任务
summary: 经过一周繁忙的发射活动，本周全球发射清单预计将进行六次发射，其中包括范登堡发射的 3 次 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号发射任务、中国的两次发射任务以及南美洲的阿丽亚娜 6 号发射任务。 SpaceX 将为美国太空部队和国家侦察办公室发射有效载荷，而本周的中国任务和阿丽亚娜 6 号任务中至少有一次将发射一批互联网卫星。长征2D |有效载荷未知 11 月 18 日星期三，中国将发射长征 2D (CZ-2D) 火箭，预计将从 9 号发射场 (LC
content:
经过一周繁忙的发射活动，本周全球发射清单预计将进行六次发射，其中包括范登堡发射的 3 次 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号发射任务、中国的两次发射任务以及南美洲的阿丽亚娜 6 号发射任务。 SpaceX 将为美国太空部队和国家侦察办公室发射有效载荷，而本周的中国任务和阿丽亚娜 6 号任务中至少有一次将发射一批互联网卫星。长征2D |有效载荷未知，将于 11 月 18 日星期三从中国发射，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 预计将于世界标准时间 22:50 从太原卫星发射中心的 9 号发射场 (LC-9) 发射。官方警告通知表明发射轨迹是向南的，但有效载荷及其预定轨道的详细信息要等到发射后才会发布。两级、40.77 米高的 CZ-2D 由上海航天技术研究院 (SAST) 制造。 2D 版本不需要额外的捆绑式助推器。此次飞行将是长征2D的第108次飞行，也是今年的第七次。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX 将于 11 月 18 日星期三进行本周两次发射中的第一次发射，发射时间为四小时，发射窗口于太平洋标准时间晚上 7:00（世界标准时间周四 03:00）开始。
USSF-317 任务是美国太空军 (USSF) 本周的唯一任务，将从加利福尼亚州范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 的东 4 号航天发射场 (SLC-4E) 发射，向东南飞行，将其机密有效载荷送入低地球轨道 (LEO)。所有系统看起来都很好，天气也有利于升空。猎鹰 9 号发射的 USSF-627 任务即将开始从加利福尼亚州发射推进剂 → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) 2026 年 11 月 12 日助推器 B1100 将支持此次任务，这是自近一年前 11 月 23 日首次支持星链集团 11-30 以来的第十一次飞行， 2025 年。除了 NROL-105 和 USSF-385 之外，助推器之前的八次飞行支持了星链任务。 SpaceX 的西海岸无人机飞船 Of Course I Still Love You 将在 B1100 升空后约 8 分钟着陆时驻扎在地面。猎鹰 9 号是一枚直径 3.9 米、高 70 米的两级火箭。九台 Merlin 1D 发动机为第一级助推器提供动力，而第二级则使用一台真空优化的 Merlin 发动机。猎鹰 9 号和猎鹰重型火箭是第一批实现定期重复使用的轨道火箭，其中一枚猎鹰助推器已飞行 37 次。飞行后，两个有效载荷整流罩也被回收并重复使用。长征8A | SatNet LEO Group 本周第二次中国发射计划于 11 月 11 日星期五举行。
世界标准时间 20 日 11:00，在中国文昌航天发射场的商业 LC-1 发射台上发射。长征 8A (CZ-8A) 将携带 9 颗通信卫星进入近地轨道，这些卫星由 SatNet 拥有并由中国卫星网络集团运营。 CZ-8A火箭有两个直径3.35米的级，总高度为50.54 m。第一级由两个捆绑式液体燃料助推器辅助。此次飞行将标志着 CZ-8A 的第 13 次飞行，也是 2026 年的第七次飞行。 NROL-136 SpaceX 本周的第二次猎鹰 9 号任务定于 11 月 21 日星期六太平洋标准时间凌晨 4:30（世界标准时间 12:30）发射，同样是从加州 VSFB 的 SLC-4E 发射。 NROL-136 任务将携带未知数量的有效载荷进入近地轨道，供国家侦察办公室 (NRO) 的增殖建筑星座使用，该星座由 Space 建造

【原文 English Original】
Following a week of busy launch activity, the worldwide launch manifest is set to see six launches this week, with three SpaceX Falcon 9 missions from Vandenberg, two Chinese missions, and an Ariane 6 mission from South America. SpaceX will launch payloads for the United States Space Force and the National Reconnaissance Office, while at least one of this week’s Chinese missions and the Ariane 6 will launch a batch of internet satellites. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload Wednesday, Nov. 18, will see a launch from China, with a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) expected to launch from Launch Complex 9 (LC-9) at the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center at 22:50 UTC. Official warning notices indicate a southerly launch trajectory, but details of the payload and its intended orbit will not be released until after launch. The two-stage, 40.77-m-tall CZ-2D is manufactured by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST). The 2D variant requires no additional strap-on boosters. This flight will mark the 108th CZ-2D to fly, the seventh of this year. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX’s first of two launches this week comes on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the start of a four-hour launch window that opens at 7:00 PM PST (03:00 UTC on Thursday). The only mission for the United States Space Force (USSF) this week, the USSF-317 mission will launch from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) in California, flying southeast to place its classified payload into low-Earth orbit (LEO). All systems are looking good, and weather is favorable for liftoff. Propellant load is about to begin for Falcon 9’s launch of the USSF-627 mission from California → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 12, 2026 Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its eleventh flight since first supporting Starlink Group 11-30 nearly a year ago on Nov. 23, 2025. Eight of the booster’s previous flights supported Starlink missions, in addition to flying NROL-105 and USSF-385. SpaceX’s west coast droneship, Of Course I Still Love You, will be stationed downrange for B1100’s landing approximately eight minutes after liftoff. Falcon 9 is a 3.9-m-diameter, 70-m-tall two-stage rocket. Nine Merlin 1D engines power the first-stage booster, while the second stage uses a single vacuum-optimized Merlin engine. Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy were the first orbital rockets to achieve regular re-use, with one Falcon booster having flown 37 flights. The two payload fairings are also recovered and reused after flight. Chang Zheng 8A | SatNet LEO Group The second Chinese launch of the week is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, at 11:00 UTC from the Commercial LC-1 pad at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in China. A Chang Zheng 8A (CZ-8A) will carry nine communications satellites into LEO, with the satellites owned by SatNet and operated by the China Satellite Network Group. The CZ-8A rocket features two 3.35-m-diameter stages, with a total height of 50.54 m. The first stage is assisted by two strap-on liquid-fuelled boosters. This flight will mark the 13th overall CZ-8A flight, the seventh of 2026. Falcon 9 | NROL-136 SpaceX’s second Falcon 9 mission of the week is scheduled to launch on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 4:30 AM PST (12:30 UTC), again from SLC-4E at VSFB in California. The NROL-136 mission will carry an unknown number of payloads into LEO for the National Reconnaissance Office’s (NRO) Proliferated Architecture constellation, built by SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The booster supporting this mission will be B1097, flying for the 14th time. This booster first flew on Sept. 3, 2025, and has previously flown eight Starlink missions, as well as NROL-172, Transporter 17, Sentinel-6B, Twilight (Pandora & Others), and USSF-259. Following stage separation, B1097 will conduct a return-to-launch-site landing at Landing Zone 4 (LZ-4), located directly next to SLC-4E. Ariane 64 | Amazon Leo (LE-04) Amazon is continuing to put together its constellation of Leo satellites and will add another 36 on Monday, Nov. 23, at 10:12 UTC aboard an Ariane 64. The rocket will launch from Ensemble de Lancement Ariane 4 (ELA-4) at the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana, with the launch window lasting five hours and 27 minutes. Ariane 64 will follow a northeastern trajectory, delivering 22,000 kg of Leo satellites into LEO. Ariane 64 is a 62-m-tall, 5.4-m-diameter, expendable two-stage rocket built by the ArianeGroup on behalf of the European Space Agency. Both stages are powered by liquid hydrogen and oxygen-fuelled engines. The 64 variant of the basic Ariane 6 utilizes four P129 strap-on solid rocket boosters to provide additional lift-off thrust. This will be the fifth Ariane 6 mission of 2026. Watch the full replay of #VA269 . Relive Ariane 6's successful mission carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit. First flight with P160C boosters Heaviest Ariane payload ever #LaunchingAmbitions #Ariane6 #VA269 @Amazonleo @ArianeGroup @esa @CNES @EuropeSpacePort pic.twitter.com/YLxW60wAo1 — Arianespace (@Arianespace) June 17, 2026 Falcon 9 | USSF-266 (TH-3) Closing out the week, a Falcon 9 launch is currently scheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, at 8:04 AM PST (16:04 UTC) — the third this week from SLC-4E at VSFB. The classified USSF-266 mission has a four-hour launch window extending to 12:04 PM PST (20:04 UTC). Falcon 9 will fly due south, indicating a polar orbit for the payload. While the payload is classified, the launch trajectory and other factors suggest that this may be an additional batch of satellites for the USSF’s Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator (SB-AMTI) program. These are based on the SpaceX Starshield satellite bus. The Falcon 9 booster supporting this flight will be B1081, making its 29th flight. B1081 first flew on Aug. 26, 2023, and flew four missions from SpaceX’s Florida launch sites before moving to Vandenberg for Transporter 10, where it has operated since then. The booster will land atop Of Course I Still Love You , stationed approximately 640 km downrange in the Pacific Ocean. If the current schedule holds, this will mark the 122nd Falcon 9 flight of 2026, and the 273rd orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. (Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches into the Florida morning skies. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Ariane 6 to launch Amazon satellites, Falcon 9 to launch government missions appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .

title: Russian Tu-95 Bombers Arrive In Vietnam After Flurry Of Northeast Asia Air Alerts
zh_title: 东北亚空中警报频发后，俄罗斯Tu-95轰炸机抵达越南
summary: 俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，Tu-95MS 飞行员于 2026 年 1 月 21 日在日本海上空进行了一次飞行。照片由 Russian Defence Min 摄
content:
俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，2026 年 1 月 21 日，一架 Tu-95MS 的飞行员在前一次飞越日本海时。照片由俄罗斯国防部/阿纳多卢通过 Getty Images 拍摄 Anadolu 11 月 16 日至 17 日，Tu-95MS 轰炸机是几架俄罗斯军用飞机之一，在东北亚进行了广泛的演习，引发了三个地区政府的防空反应。据分析师 AviVector 称，共有五架涡轮螺旋桨动力轰炸机于 11 月 16 日从俄罗斯远东的乌克兰基地起飞。据报道，其中三架轰炸机在三架 Il-78M Midas 空中加油机的支援下，在日本海上空进行了大约 11 小时的训练飞行。据报道，一架 A-50U Mainstay 空中预警和控制飞机也在日本海上空飞行。与此同时，另外两架 Tu-95MS 继续向南驶向越南。今天，乌克兰空军基地的三架 Tu-95MS 和三架 Il-78M 在日本海上空进行了 11 小时的训练飞行。
一架 A-50U（RF-94268，红色 41）从符拉迪沃斯托克机场起飞，在日本海上空进行了一次侦察飞行。两架 Tu-95MS（RF-94202，红色 43；RF-94188，红色 44）… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) 11 月 17 日， 2026 日本和台湾均未正式确定参与各自空域事件的飞机类型。日本防卫省证实，11 月 17 日早些时候，两架据信是俄罗斯的飞机侵犯了福冈县冲之岛西北部的领空。第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分左右进入，于凌晨 4 点 10 分起飞。第二架飞机于凌晨 4 点 09 分左右进入，于 2026 年 4 月 10 日起飞。据日本防卫省称，凌晨 4 点 12 分，日本认为俄罗斯飞机于 11 月 17 日早些时候进入福冈附近冲之岛西北部的日本领空，第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分左右进入日本领空，第二架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分左右进入日本… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — 台湾安全监察站 (@TaiwanMonitor) 2026 年 11 月 17 日，日本防卫省称，日本航空自卫队 (JASDF) 紧急出动西方防空部队的战斗机，发出警告并采取其他措施。
穿过对马海峡后，飞机在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后继续进入太平洋。 2026年11月17日，推测的俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本联合参谋部 该航线使飞机经过连接日本海、东海和西太平洋的几个具有重要战略意义的海上通道。据报道，俄罗斯飞机随后进入韩国防空识别区（KADIZ）。不过，据韩国国防部称，此次事件并未侵犯韩国领空。

【原文 English Original】
Russia has sent a pair of Tu-95MS Bear bombers for a rare visit to Vietnam. Unusually, the aircraft appear to have briefly intruded into Japanese airspace and passed through Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ) along the way. The activity unfolded just 48 hours before Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump are due to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. A screen grab from a video shows the pilot of a Tu-95MS during a previous flight over the Sea of Japan on January 21, 2026. Photo by Russian Defense Ministry/Anadolu via Getty Images Anadolu The Tu-95MS bombers were among several Russian military aircraft conducting extensive maneuvers across Northeast Asia on November 16-17, prompting air defense responses from three regional governments. According to analyst AviVector , a total of five of the turboprop-powered bombers departed their home base of Ukrainka in Russia’s Far East on November 16. Three of the bombers reportedly conducted an approximately 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan, supported by three Il-78M Midas aerial refueling tankers. An A-50U Mainstay airborne early warning and control aircraft was also reported operating over the Sea of Japan. Meanwhile, the other two Tu-95MS continued south towards Vietnam. Today, three Tu-95MS and three Il-78M from Ukrainka Air Base conducted an 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan. An A-50U (RF-94268, 41 Red) from Vladivostok Airport conducted a reconnaissance flight over the Sea of Japan. Two Tu-95MS (RF-94202, 43 Red; RF-94188, 44… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) November 17, 2026 Neither Japan nor Taiwan officially identified the aircraft types involved in their respective airspace incidents. Japan’s Ministry of Defense confirmed that two separate aircraft believed to be Russian violated its territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, in Fukuoka Prefecture, early on November 17. The first aircraft entered at approximately 4:07 a.m. local time and departed at 4:10 a.m. A second aircraft entered at approximately 4:09 a.m. and departed at 4:12 a.m. Two aircraft Japan believes are Russian entered Japanese territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, off Fukuoka, early Nov. 17, per Japan's Ministry of Defense. The first was inside from about 4:07 to 4:10 a.m. local time and the second from about 4:09 to 4:12 a.m. The Japan… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — Taiwan Security Monitor (台灣安全觀測站) (@TaiwanMonitor) November 17, 2026 The Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) scrambled fighters from its Western Air Defense Force to issue warnings and take other measures, according to the country’s Ministry of Defense. Tokyo subsequently lodged what it described as a strong protest with Moscow over the incident. Japan also provided details of the aircraft’s subsequent route. After passing through the Tsushima Strait , the planes flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before continuing into the Pacific Ocean. Flight path of the presumed Russian aircraft on November 17, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office The route placed the aircraft through several strategically important maritime approaches connecting the Sea of Japan , East China Sea , and western Pacific. The Russian aircraft then reportedly entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ). However, there was no violation of South Korean airspace, according to the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff. Finally, Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense reported detecting two Russian military aircraft entering its ADIZ from the northeast. Overall, 2 sorties of Russian military aircraft were detected early this morning. The aircraft entered #Taiwan 's ADIZ from the northeast, flew through airspace east of Taiwan, and exited the ADIZ south of Taitung. The #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded… — 國防部 Ministry of National Defense, ROC(Taiwan) (@MoNDefense) November 17, 2026 The aircraft proceeded through airspace east of Taiwan before exiting south of Taitung. Taiwan’s armed forces monitored the activity and responded accordingly, the Ministry of National Defense said. The incident is notable because Taiwan’s defence ministry publicly identified the aircraft as Russian, rather than simply reporting unidentified military aircraft activity. As we have reported in the past , Chinese aircraft commonly fly into the southwestern part of Taiwan’s ADIZ. It is, however, worth noting that the ADIZ declared by Taiwan covers not only the entirety of the Strait but also portions of mainland China. In terms of Russian aircraft operating in Taiwan’s ADIZ, there are historical precedents, but such activity has been greatly reduced since the end of the Cold War. Taiwanese military analyst Chieh Chung told Focus Taiwan that Soviet and Russian military aircraft had previously operated inside Taiwan’s ADIZ in 1986 and January 2010. "The incident was not the first time Russian or former Soviet military aircraft had entered Taiwan's ADIZ, although such flights have become much less frequent since the end of the Cold War." https://t.co/TPUJL9hfp1 https://t.co/SDB6p3E3pD — Bryce C. Barros 白若詩 (@barros_bryce) November 17, 2026 The two remaining Tu-95MS aircraft continued south towards Vietnam and were subsequently reported at Da Nang on November 17. They were accompanied by a pair of Il-76MD Candid transports, one of which was a modernized -90A variant , to support the deployment. Tu-95MS strategic missile carriers RF-94202, RF-94188. Il-76MD, Da Nang Airport / "Danang 35K Feet". pic.twitter.com/22DaoD8PLP — Massimo Frantarelli (@MrFrantarelli) November 17, 2026 [Russie Vietnam] 2 Tu-95MS des forces aérospatiales russes sont arrivés à l'aéroport international de Da Nang (DAD/VVDN), au Vietnam. 2 avions de transport militaire IL-76 (MD et MD-90A) les accompagnaient. (c) AviaNews pic.twitter.com/4bWfFXFOik — La souris (@La_souris_DA) November 17, 2026 The flights took place against the backdrop of preparations for the November 19 meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin in China. The summit is set to be held on the sidelines of meetings of the  Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), which kick off tomorrow. Putin arrived in Shenzhen today. Trump has traveled first to the Philippines as part of a short tour of Asia before heading to China. Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen in the early hours of Nov. 18 to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. ： @PDChina pic.twitter.com/5YotpjYY6R — Shenzhen Daily (@szdaily1) November 17, 2026 The proximity of the Russian operation to the Shenzhen meeting raises questions about the strategic signaling of the Russian flights, particularly as the three governments prepare to discuss nuclear arms control, regional security, and other major international issues. The meeting is particularly unusual given the different priorities each leader is bringing to the table . Trump has indicated that he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and addressing the war in Iran. The expiration of the New START treaty in February 2026 removed the remaining bilateral limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear forces, adding urgency to the question of future arms-control arrangements. U.S. President Barack Obama, at left, and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, at right, shake hands after signing the New START treaty in 2010. Government of Russia Washington has tempered expectations of an immediate agreement, describing the gathering as an initial opportunity for the three nuclear powers to begin a conversation. Putin, meanwhile, is expected to seek discussion of Russia’s war against Ukraine and the possibility of a negotiated settlement. Moscow has signalled that Ukraine will remain a priority in its discussions with Washington. Beijing’s position is more cautious. China has resisted joining trilateral nuclear arms-control negotiations at this stage, arguing that its nuclear arsenal remains substantially smaller than those of the United States and Russia. Xi is also seeking to present China as a central diplomatic actor capable of facilitating dialogue between the other two powers. An apparent new field of Chinese intercontinental ballistic missile silos identified by Matt Korda and Hans Kristensen from the Federation of American Scientists (FAS) and located near the city of Hami in the eastern end of Xinjiang province, in the northwest of China. Kristensen/Korda/FAS 2021 The timing of the Russian aviation activity is therefore difficult to ignore. The operation demonstrated the geographic reach of Russian long-range aviation, with aircraft moving from Russia’s Far East through the approaches to Japan and Taiwan before continuing towards Vietnam. The Southeast Asian nation was a regular late Cold War operating location for Soviet naval Tu-95 Bear reconnaissance aircraft. Of course, as well as strategic signalling, flights of this kind provide valuable long-range training and intelligence collection, including assessment of regional air defense responses. The November 19 meeting may not produce an agreement on nuclear weapons or other major disputes. Still, the Russian flights underscore the fact that strategic stability in the Indo-Pacific also involves the security concerns of the regional states operating along the approaches to the western Pacific. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post Russian Tu-95 Bombers Arrive In Vietnam After Flurry Of Northeast Asia Air Alerts appeared first on TWZ .

title: Suspected Russian Aircraft Violated Japan’s Airspace, Says Defense Minister
zh_title: 防卫大臣称俄罗斯飞机疑似侵犯日本领空
source: 美国海军学院工作人员（大量国会报告每周2-3次）
summary: 2026 年 11 月 12 日可疑俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本防卫大臣周二宣布，可疑俄罗斯飞机周四两次侵犯日本领空，促使战斗机紧急升空予以回应。日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎在周二的例行新闻发布会上表示，周四凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分，一架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯了东海冲之岛西北部的日本领空。随后，凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分，第二架疑似俄罗斯飞机
content:
2026 年 11 月 12 日可疑俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本防卫大臣周二宣布，可疑俄罗斯飞机周四两次侵犯日本领空，促使战斗机紧急升空予以回应。日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎在周二的例行新闻发布会上表示，周四凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分，一架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯了东海冲之岛西北部的日本领空。随后，凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分，第二架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯同一地区的日本领空。飞机穿过对马海峡，在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后进入菲律宾海。作为回应，日本航空自卫队西部防空司令部的日本航空自卫队战斗机紧急紧急升空。日本飞机向可疑的俄罗斯飞机发出了通知和警告。日本飞机无法看到俄罗斯飞机，也无法目视确认进入空域的飞机类型。
会议记录显示，小泉纯一郎表示：“虽然很难明确说明俄罗斯飞机这次行动背后的意图或目的，但无论如何，防卫省和自卫队将继续高度关注俄罗斯的军事行动，并将采取一切可能措施，确保对领空侵犯保持警惕、监视和适当反应。”不仅侵犯了日本的主权，而且对日本的安全构成了威胁。小泉表示，日本政府已通过外交渠道向俄罗斯政府提出抗议，要求类似事件不再重演。俄罗斯飞机周四进入日本、韩国和台湾的防空识别区（ADIZ）。防空识别区始于主权空域结束处，是一段确定的国际空域，为了国家安全利益，在其中检测和跟踪飞机。战斗机经常紧急起飞拦截和跟踪外国飞机，直到其离开防空识别区。虽然国际法不承认，但许多国家都设有防空识别区，因为领空距离一个国家的海岸线仅延伸 12 海里。这三个国家没有确认这架俄罗斯飞机的身份。
据当地航空观察员称，当天晚些时候，两架 Tu-95MS 轰炸机和两架 IL-76 运输机降落在越南岘港国际机场。岘港的一个社区社交媒体页面发布了轰炸机抵达的照片以及停在机场的四架俄罗斯飞机的视频。截至发稿时，俄罗斯和越南均已就越南境内出现轰炸机问题发表官方声明。日本军队于 2026 年 6 月 27 日拍摄到一架俄罗斯 Tu-95 轰炸机。日本联合参谋部照片 2015年，路透社报道称，美国已要求越南停止允许俄罗斯加油机使用金兰湾。据报道，这些加油机被用来为在关岛附近进行挑衅性飞行的俄罗斯轰炸机加油。俄罗斯轰炸机最后一次部署到东南亚是在 2017 年 12 月 5 日，当时两架 Tu-95MS 轰炸机和两架 Il-76 运输机降落在印度尼西亚比亚克岛。印尼空军表示，此次访问的目的是

【原文 English Original】
Flight path of the suspect Russian aircraft on Nov. 12, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office map Suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese territorial airspace twice on Thursdays, prompting fighter aircraft to be scrambled in response, Japan’s Defense Minister announced Tuesday. Between 4:07 and 4:10 a.m. on Thursday, one suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace northwest of Okinoshima, which lies in the East China Sea, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said in his regularly scheduled Tuesday press conference. Subsequently, between 4:09 and 4:12 a.m., a second suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace in the same area. The aircraft passed through the Tsushima Strait, flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan, and proceeded into the Philippine Sea. Japan Air Self-Defense Force fighter aircraft from the JASDF’s Western Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. The Japanese aircraft issued notifications and warnings to the suspected Russian aircraft. Japan’s aircraft were unable to see the Russian aircraft and visually confirm the type of aircraft that entered the airspace. “Whilst it is difficult to state with certainty the intent or purpose behind the Russian aircraft’s actions on this occasion, the Ministry of Defense and the Self-Defense Forces will, in any case, continue to monitor Russia’s military movements with the utmost attention and will take every possible measure to ensure vigilance, surveillance and appropriate responses to airspace violations,” said Koizumi, according to a transcript of the conference . Koizumi called the violation of Japan’s territorial airspace by Russian aircraft not only a serious infringement of Japan’s sovereignty but also a threat to Japan’s security. The Japanese government has lodged a protest with the Russian government through diplomatic channels and demanded that such incidents not be repeated, Koizumi said. The Russian aircraft entered the Air Defense Identification Zones (ADIZs) of Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Thursday. An ADIZ begins where sovereign airspace ends and is a defined stretch of international airspace in which aircraft are detected and tracked in the interest of national security. Fighter aircraft are often scrambled to intercept and shadow the foreign aircraft until it leaves the ADIZ. While not recognized under international law, a number of countries have ADIZs because territorial airspace extends just 12 nautical miles from a country’s coastline. The three countries did not identify the Russian aircraft. Two Tu-95MS bombers and two IL-76 transports landed at Da Nang International Airport, Vietnam, later that day, according to local aviation spotters. A Da Nang-based community social media page posted photos of the bombers arriving and videos of the four Russian aircraft parked at the airport. Russia nor Vietnam, as of publication, have issued official statements on the presence of the bombers in Vietnam. A Russian Tu-95 bomber photographed June 27, 2026, by Japanese forces. Japan Joint Staff Office photo In 2015, Reuters reported that the U.S. had requested Vietnam to stop allowing Russian tanker aircraft to use Cam Ranh Bay. The tankers were reportedly being used to refuel Russian bombers that conducted provocative flights near Guam. The last known Russian bomber deployment to Southeast Asia was on Dec. 5, 2017, when two Tu-95MS bombers and two Il-76 transports landed on Biak Island, Indonesia. The Indonesian Air Force said that the visit was for a navigation exercise. The Russian Defense Ministry said at the time that the bombers were refuelled in the air by Ilyushin Il-78 tankers over the Pacific Ocean. The last time a Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace was on Sept. 23, 2024 , when a Russian IL-38 Maritime Patrol Aircraft violated Japan’s territorial airspace three times north of Rebun Island. The Defense Minister Minoru Kihara said at the time that JASDF F-15J and F-35 Lightning II fighter aircraft were scrambled and discharged flares after the Russian aircraft appeared to have ignored the warnings issued. The incident was the first time Japan had released flares against foreign aircraft.

title: How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA
zh_title: 中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜
summary: 中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜 H.Seidl 星期二，11/17/2026 - 11:58 图片联盟/新华社 |高泽明评论 2026 年 11 月 17 日 阅读 4 分钟 中国军队的战斗准备如何？解放军的困惑 中国的武装部队比以往任何时候都更有能力，但也陷入混乱。安德鲁·斯科贝尔表示，无论中国军队有什么缺点，它在任何战争中都可能成为可怕的对手。 10月下旬中共二十届五中全会选举中央军事委员会副主席
content:
中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜 H.Seidl 星期二，11/17/2026 - 11:58 图片联盟/新华社 |高泽明评论 2026 年 11 月 17 日 阅读 4 分钟 中国军队的战斗准备如何？解放军的困惑 中国的武装部队比以往任何时候都更有能力，但也陷入混乱。安德鲁·斯科贝尔表示，无论中国军队有什么缺点，它在任何战争中都可能成为可怕的对手。 10月下旬，中共二十届五中全会选举中央军委副主席张生民将军为中共政治局委员。党的领导层还确认了九月份中央军委高级将领被开除的消息，但没有任命任何继任者。这使得中国相当于美国军队参谋长联席会议的成员从通常的七人减少到只有两名成员：习近平担任文职主席，还有一名穿制服的军官张将军。中国人民解放军（PLA）被许多人认为是中华人民共和国（PRC）历史上最现代化、最有能力、最专业、装备最精良的军队。但它也正在经历自 20 世纪 60 年代毛泽东文化大革命以来的 6 年来最大的动荡。作为习近平反腐运动的一部分，自 2022 年以来，清洗行动已清除了 100 多名高级官员。
值得注意的是，这些被罢黜的将领中，有 50% 到 80% 是各级作战指挥官。 清洗运动震撼了国防机构 与此同时，中国的国防机构仍在承受四十年来最彻底的组织重组的冲击。 2016年启动的这次改革，不仅是为了增强解放军发动二十一世纪联合作战的能力，也是为了精简和集中军队，使其受中央军委主席习近平的直接指挥。这次重组被称为“中国的戈德华特-尼科尔斯”，以强调与美军在越战后时期强制各军种联合作战的举措的相似之处，这一举措花了几十年才完全实施。没有人知道习近平雄心勃勃的计划进展如何，因为中国人民解放军——包括空军、海军、陆军、火箭军和其他特种军种——尚未在21世纪发动战争，战争是对任何一支军队的严峻考验。现代化已将一支技术含量低、以轻步兵为中心、拥有陈旧空军和小型褐水海军的军队转变为一支机械化地面部队​​，拥有大量第四代和第五代战斗机空中力量，以及世界上最大的蓝水海军舰队。
此外，今天的解放军部队进行了更加真实的战斗训练，并且在过去二十年中参加了无数次（尽管大部分是小规模的）多国野战演习。中国武装部队在中国周边地区变得越来越积极主动和具有侵略性。在遥远的西部，地面部队的部署数量越来越多，在两国有争议的喜马拉雅边境沿线与印度军队偶尔发生小规模流血冲突。在南海，中国人民解放军海军、中国海警和海上民兵加大了对海军舰艇、海警快艇和渔船的骚扰力度，特别是菲律宾和越南的海军舰艇、海警快艇和渔船。在东海，中国海上力量已

How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA H.Seidl Tue, 11/17/2026 - 11:58 picture alliance / Xinhua News Agency | Gao Zeming Comment Nov 17, 2026 4 min read How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA The country’s armed forces are more capable than ever but in turmoil. Whatever the shortcomings of China's military, Andrew Scobell says it is likely to prove a formidable adversary in any war. The Fifth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) in late October elected the vice chair of the Central Military Commission (CMC), General Zhang Shengmin, to the CCP Politburo . The party leadership also confirmed the September expulsions of top generals from the CMC, but did not appoint any replacements. This left China’s rough equivalent to the US military’s Joint Chiefs of Staff with just two members, down from its usual seven: Xi Jinping as its civilian chair and one single uniformed officer, General Zhang.   The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is by many accounts the most modern, capable, professional and best equipped military in the history of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). But it is also enduring its greatest upheavals in six decades—since the turmoil of Mao Zedong’s Cultural Revolution in the 1960s. Purges have swept away more than 100 senior officers since 2022 as part of Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption crusade. Remarkably, between 50 and 80 percent of these ousted general officers have been operational commanders at various levels . Purges have rocked the defense establishment At the same time, China’s defense establishment is still absorbing the shock of the most thoroughgoing organizational restructuring in four decades. This revamping, launched in 2016, was not only intended to make the PLA more capable of waging twenty-first century joint warfare, but also to streamline and centralize it under the direct chain of command of CMC chairman Xi. This reorganization, dubbed “ China’s Goldwater-Nichols ” to underscore the parallels with the US military’s post-Vietnam War era initiative to compel separately stovepiped services to fight jointly—an effort that took decades to fully implement.  No one knows how well Xi’s ambitious initiative is faring, since the PLA – comprising the PLA Air Force, PLA Navy, PLA Ground Force, PLA Rocket Force, and other specialized services – has yet to wage war in the 21st century, warfighting being the acid test of any military. Modernization has transformed a low-tech, light infantry-centric military with an antiquated air force and a small brown-water navy into a mechanized ground force, with a sizeable airpower inventory of fourth-  and fifth-generation fighter jets, and the world’s largest blue-water naval fleet. Moreover, today’s PLA units engage in more realistic combat training and, for the past two decades, have participated in numerous, albeit largely small-scale, multinational field exercises. China’s armed forces have become increasingly activist and aggressive around the PRC’s periphery. In the far west, ground forces have deployed in ever greater numbers, engaging in occasional bloody small-scale clashes with India’s army along the two countries’ disputed Himalayan border . In the South China Sea , the PLA Navy, PRC Coast Guard and People’s Maritime Militia have stepped up harassment of naval ships, coast guard cutters and fishing boats, notably those of the Philippines and Vietnam. In the East China Sea , PRC maritime forces have conducted similar operations against Japanese and South Korean vessels. Perhaps most alarming is the dramatic escalation of so-called gray zone provocations around Taiwan. Modernization has strengthened the PLA  PLA formations are also operating further and further from China’s borders. Ground force units have served on United Nations peacekeeping missions around the world, while some air formations have also operated overseas. In 2026, the PLA acknowledged its first air installation outside of the PRC in Laos. Yet the most routinely deployed service overseas has been the PLA Navy. Its vessels have operated continuously in the Gulf of Aden since late 2008 and have been more active across the Western Pacific, Indian Ocean and Mediterranean, and even making appearances in the Atlantic, Arctic and Baltic seas. The PLA Navy has operated a support base in Djibouti on the Red Sea since 2017 and opened a naval base in Ream, Cambodia, in 2025.  But increased peacetime operational experience and tempo do not guarantee wartime successes. While PLA drills and deployments do not seem to have been impacted by the unprecedented waves of purges continuing across all echelons of China’s military, their effects could be different under actual combat conditions. The PLA has not fought a major war since China’s conflict with Vietnam in 1979. Muscular and intimidating shows of force around the PRC’s periphery and the periodic spectacle of smartly turned-out troops with gleaming military hardware on parade in Beijing are not incontrovertible proof of combat readiness. Nevertheless, as a former US defense chief famously remarked , “You go to war with the army you have.” In the event of conflict, the leaders of the PRC – just as much as those of other great powers – will have no choice but to send their militaries into battle irrespective of their condition or level of combat readiness – and their armed forces will salute and follow orders, executing operations as best they can. The PLA will remain something of a puzzle for a while, but it is likely to make a credible account of itself in any conflict. Its combat record over the decades has shown that it can fight effectively, absorb heavy casualties and adapt under fire. The views expressed in this piece are those of the author. title: Hong Kong private hospital apologises after doctor mistakenly removed patient’s ovaries during operation
zh_title: 香港私家医院因医生手术时错误摘除患者卵巢致歉
summary: 一名医生在手术期间错误地切除了一名女性的卵巢，一家私立医院向患者及其家人道歉。香港中文大学医学中心。照片：水浪/谷歌地图。香港中文大学（中大）医院行政总裁钟健丽周三在记者会上表示，涉事医生是一位经验丰富的合约妇产科医生。郑说，医生承认这起事件是由于手术当天与郑通电话时的失误造成的。医院没有透露这名患者的姓名
content:
一名医生在手术期间错误地切除了一名女性的卵巢，一家私立医院向患者及其家人道歉。香港中文大学医学中心。照片：水浪/谷歌地图。香港中文大学（中大）医院行政总裁钟健丽周三在记者会上表示，涉事医生是一位经验丰富的合约妇产科医生。郑说，医生承认这起事件是由于手术当天与郑通电话时的失误造成的。该医院没有透露该医生的姓名或任何纪律处分的细节，但表示将根据其人力资源政策实施纪律处分。首席执行官向患者、她的家人和公众致歉。他补充说，患者情况稳定，将获得免费的后续预约。卫生部周二在医疗哨点事件定期更新中表示，一名 45 岁女性患者的双侧卵巢在 9 月中旬被错误地、无意中切除。卫生部。资料图片：香港政府一站通。该患者被安排在一家私立医院接受腹腔镜子宫切除术和双侧输卵管切除术——切除全部或部分子宫，并切除双侧输卵管。
中大医院周二发布新闻稿称，手术前，手术同意书及原手术方案均明确注明保留双侧卵巢。声明称，“手术标本提取后，在对标本进行例行验证时，护士发现双侧卵巢被包括在内”。 “护士立即将这一差异通知了医生，因为这偏离了原来保留卵巢的手术计划。” “认知盲点” 医院的中文版声明因称医生在手术过程中存在“认知盲点”，因此“未能执行原定的保留卵巢手术方案”而招致批评。网上，有人留言称医院只是玩文字游戏，掩盖医疗事故。香港中文大学医院是一家新私立医院，于 2021 年开业。照片：Wai Ki Wong/Google 地图。钟周三表示，英文声明之后的中文声明翻译得很差。英国声明称，这名医生“情境意识暂时崩溃”。 “简单来说，涉案医生当时注意力不集中，”钟用粤语说。该私立医院表示，在9月12日发生医疗事故后，立即向患者及其家人“坦白”透露了情况，并表示诚挚的歉意。
它还在24小时内向卫生部通报了这一事件，并成立了根本原因分析小组进行全面调查。

【原文 English Original】
A private hospital has apologised to a patient and her family after a doctor mistakenly removed a woman’s ovaries during an operation. CUHK Medical Centre. Photo: 水浪/Google Maps. Chung Kin-lai, chief executive officer of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) Medical Centre, said during a press conference on Wednesday that the doctor involved is an experienced contract obstetrician and gynaecologist resident. The doctor admitted the incident was due to mistakes during a phone call with Chung on the day the operation was conducted, Chung said. The hospital did not disclose the name of the doctor or details of any disciplinary action, but said it would impose disciplinary actions in accordance with its human resources policies. The CEO sent apologies to the patient, her family and to the public. He added that the patient is in stable condition and will be provided free follow-up appointments. The Department of Health said on Tuesday in its regular update of medical sentinel events that a 45-year-old female patient’s bilateral ovaries were mistakenly and inadvertently removed in mid-September. The Department of Health. File photo: GovHK. The patient was scheduled for laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingectomy surgery – the removal of all or part of the uterus, and the removal of both fallopian tubes – in a private hospital. The CUHK Medical Centre said in a press release on Tuesday that prior to the operation, both the surgical consent form and the original surgical plan clearly specified the preservation of both ovaries. “After the surgical specimens were extracted, during the routine verification of the specimens, a nurse discovered that the bilateral ovaries were included,” the statement read. “The nurse immediately notified the doctor of this discrepancy, as it deviated from the original surgical plan to preserve the ovaries.” ‘Cognitive blindspot’ The hospital’s Chinese version of the statement draw criticism over its description that the doctor had “a cognitive blindspot” during the operation and therefore “failed to carry out the original surgical plan of preserving the ovaries.” Online, people left comments saying that the hospital was just playing with words to gloss over medical malpractice. CUHK Medical Centre, a new private hospital opened in 2021. Photo: Wai Ki Wong/Google Maps. Chung said on Wednesday that the Chinese statement, which followed the English one, was poorly translated. The English statement said the doctor had a “temporary collapse of his situational awareness.” “Put simply, the doctor involved had a lapse in concentration at the time,” Chung said in Cantonese. The private hospital said it “candidly disclosed” the situation to the patient and her family and offered sincere apologies immediately after the malpractice took place on September 12. It also informed the Department of Health about the incident within 24 hours and established a Root Cause Analysis Panel to conduct a comprehensive investigation.

title: Hong Kong whistleblower of student app scandal charged with doxxing
zh_title: 香港学生应用程序丑闻举报人被控人肉搜索
summary: 一名香港女子因质疑一名中学生获奖应用程序的合法性而引发学术诚信争议，她被指控人肉搜索。郑海莉.照片：Hailey Cheng，来自 Facebook。根据周三的法庭文件，海莉·程 (Hailey Cheng) 面临四项未经数据主体同意披露个人数据并造成特定伤害的指控。曾就读于香港城市大学、现就读于纽约哥伦比亚大学的郑女士当天在Threads上表示，该案已在法庭上提及，并已获准保释。一个
content:
一名香港女子因质疑一名中学生获奖应用程序的合法性而引发学术诚信争议，她被指控人肉搜索。郑海莉.照片：Hailey Cheng，来自 Facebook。根据周三的法庭文件，海莉·程 (Hailey Cheng) 面临四项未经数据主体同意披露个人数据并造成特定伤害的指控。曾就读于香港城市大学、现就读于纽约哥伦比亚大学的郑女士当天在Threads上表示，该案已在法庭上提及，并已获准保释。根据指控书，程被指控披露四名未透露姓名的人（X、Y、Z 和 A）的个人数据。据称，她这样做的目的是为了对这些人或其家人造成特定伤害，或者不顾后果地考虑是否会造成伤害。程被指控在未经“X”同意的情况下，披露了“X”的中英文全名、她的年龄、学校、学年、家庭关系、社交媒体资料、照片、居住区域、资格和行程。据称，她还披露了其他三人的个人信息，包括姓名、照片和家庭关系。 Y 的出生日期被泄露，Z 的住所被泄露，A 的社交媒体资料被泄露。
周三，郑在东区裁判法院出庭，在首席裁判官苏泽豪面前出庭，无需答辩。裁判官批准了辩方休庭寻求法律意见的请求，以及控方为受害者申请匿名令的申请。案件押后至12月23日审理。文件显示，郑先生以3,000港元现金保释。 2025 年 6 月，Cheng 担心 MediSafe（一款荣获多项奖项的药物处方应用程序）实际上并非由中学生 Clarisse Poon 制作，引发了病毒式的学术诚信丑闻。一家名为 AI Health Studio 的美国软件开发公司后来表示，该应用程序是受潘的母亲委托开发的，并且该应用程序未经其同意就提交给了比赛。早些时候被捕 这名大学生二月份在社交媒体上表示，她因举报事件而被捕。在八月份的一份声明中，她说她拒绝保释并被无条件释放。拒绝更新保释是指一个人拒绝接受延长保释期限并要求警方正式指控或释放他们的程序。警方稍后仍可以重新逮捕并指控嫌疑人。东部裁判法院。照片：何凯莉/HKFP。四月，程面临亲北京支持者要求被城大开除的呼吁。
香港编程协会 Facebook 群组的一名匿名成员当月发布了请愿书，敦促“香港庞大的蓝营”分享该请愿书。请愿书还表示，签名者将与警方、国家安全部门和中联办等当局联系，要求将她驱逐。据当时的当地媒体报道，在最初披露的三个月后，这家委托的软件公司证实了其参与，随后该学生的父母——著名肝病专家 Ronnie Poon 和 Roberta Pang——表示，他们的女儿将归还与 MediSafe 相关的所有奖项。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong woman who sparked a viral academic integrity controversy after questioning the legitimacy of a secondary student’s award-winning app has been charged with doxxing. Hailey Cheng. Photo: Hailey Cheng, via Facebook. Hailey Cheng faces four counts of disclosing personal data without a data subject’s consent causing specified harm, according to court documents dated Wednesday. Cheng, a former student at the City University of Hong Kong now admitted to Columbia University in New York, said on Threads the same day that the case had been mentioned in court and that she was granted bail . According to the charge sheet, Cheng was charged with disclosing personal data of four unnamed people referred to as X, Y, Z, and A. She allegedly did so with an intent to cause specified harm to those people or their family members, or being reckless as to whether the harm would be caused. Cheng was accused of disclosing the full English and Chinese names of “X,” her age, school, school year, family relationships, social media profiles, photos, living area, qualifications, and itinerary, without her consent. She also allegedly disclosed personal information of the other three people, including their names, photos, and family relationships. The person known as Y had her date of birth disclosed, while Z had his residence leaked, and the individual known as A had her social media profile disclosed. Cheng appeared before Chief Magistrate Victor So at the Eastern Magistrates’ Courts on Wednesday and was not required to enter a plea. The magistrate granted the defence’s request for an adjournment to seek legal advice and the prosecution’s application for an anonymity order for the victims. The case was adjourned to December 23. According to the document, Cheng was released on a HK$3,000 cash bail. In June 2025, Cheng raised concerns that MediSafe – a medication prescription app that won multiple awards – was not actually made by secondary school student Clarisse Poon, triggering a viral academic integrity scandal. A US-based software development company called AI Health Studio later said it was commissioned by Poon’s mother to build the app, and that the app was submitted to competitions without its consent. Earlier arrest The university student said on social media in February that she had been arrested in relation to the whistleblowing incident. In an August statement, she said that she refused bail and was released unconditionally. Refusing to renew bail is a procedure where a person declines to accept an extension of bail terms and requires the police to either formally charge or release them. The police can still re-arrest and charge the suspect later. Eastern Magistrates’ Courts. Photo: Kelly Ho/HKFP. In April, Cheng faced calls from pro-Beijing supporters to be expelled from CityU. An anonymous member of a Facebook group for the Hong Kong Programming Society posted the petition that month urging “Hong Kong’s vast blue camp” to share it. The petition also said that signatories would be in touch with the authorities, including the police, its National Security Department, and Beijing’s Liaison Office to demand her expulsion. Three months after the original revelation, the commissioned software company confirmed its involvement, following which the student’s parents – renowned liver disease specialist Ronnie Poon and Roberta Pang – said their daughter would return all the awards associated with MediSafe, according to local media reports at the time.

title: Hong Kong gov’t seeks HK$19.8 billion from legislature to fund early Ngau Tam Mei development
zh_title: 香港政府向立法会寻求198亿港元资助牛潭尾早期开发
summary: 香港政府正在寻求立法会批准为牛潭尾早期开发阶段提供 198 亿港元的资金，牛潭尾是庞大的北方都会项目的一个主要区域。 2026 年 10 月 30 日，一幅横幅展示了牛潭尾的新开发区，新田大学城的一个校园区将坐落于此。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。发展局及土木工程拓展署在周二向立法会提交的文件中估计牛潭尾新D区的工地平整及基础设施工程
content:
香港政府正在寻求立法会批准为牛潭尾早期开发阶段提供 198 亿港元的资金，牛潭尾是庞大的北方都会项目的一个主要区域。 2026 年 10 月 30 日，一幅横幅展示了牛潭尾的新开发区，新田大学城的一个校园区将坐落于此。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。发展局及土木工程拓展署在周二向立法会提交的文件中估计，牛潭尾新发展区的工地平整及基础设施工程将耗资约198亿港元。根据该部门的预测，该地区占地约 130 公顷，将创造约 26,000 个就业岗位，并容纳 35,400 至 38,500 人。新田大学城是北部都会项目规划的三个高等教育集群之一，位于牛潭尾，占地约52公顷。该地区的五公顷土地已预留给香港科技大学管理的香港第三所医学院。政府表示，医学院周围约10公顷的土地将被开发为综合医院，以支持研究并为未来的北方都市居民提供服务。
牛潭尾开发区约一半（66公顷）是私人土地，政府估计大约有1,300户家庭和120家企业需要被驱逐，才能为该项目让路。油潭尾村入口，2025年1月25日。该村庄位于牛潭尾新发展区内，村民将从明年开始被驱逐。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。政府称，该项目将影响约5.7公顷农田、4.1公顷鱼塘和1个养鸡场。工地平整和基础设施工程预计将于 2034 年基本完成，居民最早可于 2033 年搬入。当局计划建设政府和社区设施以及休闲区，但尚未明确时间表。 2021 年宣布的北方都会项目计划将约 300 平方公里（约占城市面积的三分之一）改造成香港与深圳边境的创新和技术中心。另请参阅：科技城到大学城：为什么香港北部都会区将重点从高科技转向高等教育牛潭尾新发展区位于北部都会区项目设想的核心“创新科技区”内，该区还将包括专业服务和物流中心以及旅游和保护设施。发展区内的油潭尾村的居民将于明年起被驱逐。

【原文 English Original】
The Hong Kong government is seeking the Legislative Council’s approval of HK$19.8 billion in funding for the early development phase in Ngau Tam Mei, a major area in the sprawling Northern Metropolis project. A banner shows the new development area in Ngau Tam Mei, where one of the campus areas of the San Tin University Town will be located, October 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In a paper submitted to the Legislative Council on Tuesday, the Development Bureau and the Civil Engineering and Development Department estimated that site formation and infrastructure works in the Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area would cost about HK$19.8 billion. The area, spanning about 130 hectares, will create around 26,000 jobs and house a population between 35,400 and 38,500 people, according to the department’s forecasts. The San Tin University Town, one of three higher education clusters planned in the Northern Metropolis project, will cover about 52 hectares in Ngau Tam Mei. Five hectares of that area has been reserved for the city’s third medical school, which will be run by the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. Around 10 hectares surrounding the medical school will be developed into a general hospital to support research and provide services for future Northern Metropolis residents, the government said. About half of the Ngau Tam Mei development area – 66 hectares – is private land, and the government estimates that roughly 1,300 households and 120 businesses need to be evicted to make way for the project. The entrance to Yau Tam Mei Tsuen, on January 25, 2025. The village sits within the Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area and villagers are set for eviction from next year. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The project will affect about 5.7 hectares of farmland, 4.1 hectares of fish pond, and one chicken farm, the government said. Site formation and infrastructure works is estimated to be largely completed by 2034, while residents can move in as early as 2033. Authorities plan to build government and community facilities and leisure areas, but have not yet specified a timeline. The Northern Metropolis project, announced in 2021, is set to transform about 300 square kilometres – roughly a third of the city’s territory – into an innovation and technology hub along Hong Kong’s border with Shenzhen. See also: Technopole to University Towns: Why Hong Kong’s Northern Metropolis shifted focus from hi-tech to higher ed The Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area sits within a core “innovation and technology zone” envisioned under the Northern Metropolis project, which will also encompass a professional services and logistics hub as well as tourism and conservation facilities. Residents of Yau Tam Mei Tsuen, a village within the development area, will be evicted from next year .

title: Beijing bolsters South China Sea push with new island runway: analysts
zh_title: 北京通过新岛屿跑道加强南海推进：分析人士
summary: 根据专家和法新社看到的卫星图像，中国正在有争议的南海另一个岛屿上修建一条跑道，这可能会大大加强其在战略水道上的军事足迹。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 10 月 17 日拍摄的讲义卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁上的一个港口的基础。照片：星球实验室/法新社。北京声称对南海大部分地区拥有主权，尽管国际裁决认为其主张没有法律依据，而且与几个国家经常发生对抗
content:
根据专家和法新社看到的卫星图像，中国正在有争议的南海另一个岛屿上修建一条跑道，这可能会大大加强其在战略水道上的军事足迹。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 10 月 17 日拍摄的讲义卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁上的一个港口的基础。照片：星球实验室/法新社。北京声称对南海大部分地区拥有主权，尽管国际裁决认为其主张没有法律依据，而且与几个东南亚国家就西沙群岛和南沙群岛的控制权经常发生对抗。这两个岛链基本上都是由珊瑚礁和露头组成，但分析人士表示，中国一直在稳步填海造地和建设基础设施，以获得对海洋的军事控制权。美国战略与国际研究中心（CSIS）和洛伊研究所在最近的详细报告中援引卫星图像称，北京去年年底开始在西沙群岛羚羊礁进行大规模疏浚和填海造地，中国、越南和台湾均声称对该群岛拥有主权。洛伊研究所报告的作者洛厄尔·鲍蒂斯塔告诉法新社，中国在 10 个月内将西沙群岛的珊瑚礁从最小的西沙群岛前哨基地之一转变为可以与最大的环礁相媲美的岛屿。
羚羊礁上近三公里的跑道将是北京在西沙群岛的第二条跑道，与南沙群岛和海南岛上的基础设施一起，有助于“建立一个跨越大海的跑道、港口和传感器的综合网络”，包蒂斯塔说。1974年，中国和越南在西沙群岛发生了一场短暂但血腥的小冲突。70多名越南士兵被杀，从那时起，中国实际上控制了这些岛屿。据战略与国际研究中心称，该跑道的大小与西沙群岛永兴岛和南沙群岛其他三个机场的跑道相似。分析人士表示，羚羊角沿西北-东南轴线约六公里，可能成为中国在南海最重要的前哨基地之一，有可能帮助北京在发生冲突时限制美国及其盟国海军的进入。中国表示，西沙群岛的开发是出于民用目的，并补充说，西沙群岛的居民人口较少，主要是渔民。外交部发言人三月份表示，中国在该岛的填海造地活动是“必要的建设”，目的是“改善岛上的生活和工作条件，发展当地经济”。运输机、轰炸机 在地球成像公司 Planet Labs 9 月份拍摄的照片中，清晰可见一个看起来像跑道的结构。
这些图像是日本情报公司 Deep Dive 最近报告的一部分，法新社也看到了这些图像。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 11 月 8 日拍摄的分发卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁。照片：星球实验室/法新社。 Deep Dive 主任、前驻中国武官 Bonji Ohara 在报告中表示，该结构不仅能够容纳战斗机，还能够容纳更大型的飞机，包括运输机、空中加油机和轰炸机。他说，新跑道可能会让中国更接近实现“对整个南海的完全控制”。 CSIS 表示，Antelope 可以增强中国传感能力的覆盖范围

【原文 English Original】
China is building a runway on another island in the disputed South China Sea that could significantly strengthen its military footprint in the strategic waterway, according to experts and satellite images seen by AFP. This handout satellite image taken by Planet Labs PBC on October 17, 2026 shows the foundations of a harbour on the disputed Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands in the South China Sea. Photo: Planet Labs/AFP. Beijing claims most of the South China Sea, despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis, and confrontations have occurred regularly with  several Southeast Asian nations over control of the Paracel and Spratly islands. Both island chains are essentially made up of reefs and outcrops, but analysts say China has been steadily reclaiming land and building infrastructure to gain military control of the sea. Beijing late last year began large-scale dredging and reclaiming land at Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands, which are claimed by China, Vietnam and Taiwan, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) and the Lowy Institute said in recent detailed reports, citing satellite images. Lowell Bautista, author of the Lowy Institute report, told AFP that China transformed the reef in 10 months from one of its smallest Paracel outposts into an island that can rival its largest atoll. The nearly three-kilometre runway on Antelope Reef would be Beijing’s second in the Paracels and — together with infrastructure on the Spratly Islands and on Hainan island — helps “create an integrated network of runways, harbours and sensors stretching across the sea”, Bautista said. China and Vietnam fought a brief but bloody skirmish over the Paracels in 1974. More than 70 Vietnamese soldiers were killed and China has had de facto control over the islands since then. The runway is a similar size to an airstrip on the Paracels’ Woody Island and three others across the Spratlys, according to CSIS. Analysts say Antelope — which is around six kilometres along its northwest-southeast axis — could become one of China’s most important outposts in the South China Sea, potentially helping Beijing limit the access of US and allied naval forces in the event of conflict. China says the development of the Paracel Islands, which it adds have a small resident population of mostly fishers, is for civilian purposes. A spokesperson for the foreign ministry said in March that China’s land reclamation activities there are “necessary construction” for “improving living and working conditions on the islands and growing the local economy”. Transport planes, bombers A structure that appears to be a runway is clearly visible in photos taken in September by Earth imaging company Planet Labs. The images were reviewed as part of a recent report by Japanese intelligence firm Deep Dive and were also seen by AFP. This handout satellite image taken by Planet Labs PBC on November 8, 2026 shows the disputed Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands in the South China Sea. Photo: Planet Labs/AFP. Deep Dive director Bonji Ohara, a former defence attache in China, said in the report that the structure would be able to handle not just fighter jets but also larger aircraft, including transport planes, aerial refuelling tankers and bombers. The new runway could potentially bring China closer to achieving “full control over the entire South China Sea”, he said. The CSIS has said that Antelope could enhance the reach of Chinese sensing capabilities closer to Vietnam’s shores and help expand its military capacity in an area of the northern South China Sea which is close to major shipping lanes. Antelope Reef’s runway is expected to be operational by mid-2027, although other analysts were more cautious about its significance. The runway and harbour will “add additional capacity and resilience to the facility that enable China’s military and paramilitary operations in the South China Sea,” Harrison Pretat, deputy director at CSIS’s Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative, told AFP. But “Southeast Asian claimants have still largely maintained access to offshore resources and occupy their own outposts,” he said. Limited pushback Nevertheless, Pretat warned that “international attention and pushback… has been far less than might be expected given the scale and significance” of construction, due in part “to distraction from other global crises”. “Regional countries…along with the United States and the international community, should be speaking with a stronger voice against island building and other attempts to permanently alter conditions in disputed areas,” he said. Vietnam in August called construction at Antelope Reef “completely illegal” and demanded “such activities cease immediately”. And in October, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said that China’s military build-up was creating a “condition of pressure” in Southeast Asia, and urged allies and partners to deepen cooperation. But Hunter Marston of the Lowy Institute told AFP that “ASEAN (member states) will never be capable of communicating with one voice” due partly to their different views of China. A crew member of the China Coast Guard vessel 5205 removes the cover of a 70 mm cannon and aims it toward the BRP Teresa Magbanua near Second Thomas Shoal in the South China Sea in August 2022. File photo: Philippine Coast Guard. US ally the Philippines has been engaged in years of confrontations with China over disputed areas of the sea, and Filipino and Chinese ships have engaged in repeated confrontations in recent years, some leading to collisions and injuries. Ohara said that Beijing views the sea as “a sanctuary… where it does not want foreign powers to enter in the event of a contingency” in the region. “While it will not restrict freedom of navigation in peacetime, if some incident occurs, China intends to prevent not only US naval forces but also those of its allies — for example, Australian submarines — from entering,” he said.

title: Trump seeks diplomatic gains on Asia tour as Putin arrives in China
zh_title: 普京抵达中国，特朗普寻求亚洲之行的外交收获
summary: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京周三抵达中国，准备与中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普举行峰会。在国内选举惨败后，特朗普正在亚洲之行寻求外交成果。 2026 年 11 月 17 日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达尼诺·阿基诺国际机场，出席在马尼拉举行的第 49 届东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 峰会，他挥舞着美国和菲律宾国旗。照片：Eloisa Lopez/法新社。特朗普周二在菲律宾与所谓的“四方”国家和地区的领导人会面。
content:
俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京周三抵达中国，准备与中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普举行峰会。在国内选举惨败后，特朗普正在亚洲之行寻求外交成果。 2026 年 11 月 17 日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达尼诺·阿基诺国际机场，出席在马尼拉举行的第 49 届东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 峰会，他挥舞着美国和菲律宾国旗。照片：Eloisa Lopez/法新社。特朗普周二在菲律宾与所谓的四方国家领导人会面，并表示他计划在下一站中国深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会上与普京和朝鲜金正恩进行一对一会谈。特朗普在与四国领导人印度纳伦德拉·莫迪、日本首相高市早苗和澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞合影时对记者说：“如果有的话，我会这么做。”他补充说，朝鲜金正恩“希望”在中国会面，几小时前北京表示没有关于两人会面的信息。另请参阅：中国称习近平、特朗普和普京将在深圳峰会上讨论“世界和平” 特朗普在东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 11 名成员国峰会上举行的四方会议是他 2025 年 1 月重新掌权以来该安全联盟的首次会议。
分析人士称，虽然主要旨在制衡中国的地区影响力的四方会谈在深化协调方面取得了悄然进展，但周二会议的时间很短，这意味着会议不可能超越寒暄。在马尼拉，特朗普在机场停机坪上受到了游行乐队和仪仗队的欢迎，而在其他地方，约有 2000 名示威者与警察对峙，他们举着写着“特朗普现在下台”和“拒绝 Pax Silica”的横幅——指的是美国的供应这一连锁倡议在菲律宾引起了分歧。关税、芯片和稀土 虽然东盟领导人花了三天时间努力解决一系列地区问题，但特朗普正在进行的关税闪电战的幽灵已经隐约可见。中国总理李强周一猛烈抨击了他所谓的“单边主义和保护主义的逆流”，同时宣传了北京与欧盟不断扩大的贸易。巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦和加拿大总统马克·卡尼在贸易问题上也唱出了类似的调子，两人都明确表示需要摆脱对美国市场的依赖。加拿大总理马克·卡尼于 2026 年 10 月 17 日在深圳与中国国家主席习近平握手。照片：马克·卡尼，来自 Threads。周二，好斗的特朗普在与北京的贸易战中丝毫没有放松，他表示美国将“在10个月内”在稀土产量上赶上中国。 “我们正在以前所未有的水平生产稀土。
他们说，我们将在 10 个月内抓住他们。”他说。在特朗普抵达马尼拉前几个小时，华盛顿宣布了有关先进人工智能芯片转让的新规则，此举可能会激怒东盟成员国。向新加坡、马来西亚、泰国和印度尼西亚运送高端芯片的公司现在需要特殊许可证，因为据说这些国家代表着“高于正常的转移风险”。新加坡回应称，它正在探索为总部位于新加坡的公司提供“可信准入”的方法。特朗普将于周三在总统府会见菲律宾领导人费迪南德·马科斯，然后前往。

【原文 English Original】
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday arrived in China ahead of a summit with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, who is on an Asian tour in search of diplomatic gains after a bruising election defeat back home. US President Donald Trump waves US and Philippine flags upon arriving at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport to attend the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on November 17, 2026. Photo: Eloisa Lopez/AFP. Trump was in the Philippines on Tuesday for a meeting with the leaders of the so-called Quad countries and said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and North Korea’s Kim Jong Un at his next stop, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China’s Shenzhen. “If it’s available, I would do that,” Trump told reporters as he stood for photos with fellow Quad leaders Narendra Modi of India, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australia’s Anthony Albanese. He added that North Korea’s Kim “would like” to meet in China, hours after Beijing said it had no information about an encounter between the two. See also: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ at Shenzhen summit Trump’s Quad meeting at the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit was the security alliance’s first since his January 2025 return to power. While the Quad –- broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence — has quietly progressed in deepening coordination, the short time allotted for Tuesday’s meeting meant it was unlikely to extend beyond pleasantries, according to analysts. While Trump was greeted in Manila by a marching band and honour guard on the airport tarmac, elsewhere some 2,000 demonstrators faced off with police, carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica” — a reference to a US supply chain initiative that has divided opinion in the Philippines. Tariffs, chips and rare earths While ASEAN leaders have spent three days grappling with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large. Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with the bloc. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada’s Mark Carney sang a similar tune on trade, with both explicitly citing a need to wean themselves off dependence on the US market. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shakes hands with China’s Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on October 17, 2026. Photo: Mark Carney, via Threads. On Tuesday, a combative Trump showed no let-up in his trade war with Beijing, saying the United States would catch China in rare earths production “within 10 months”. “We are making rare earths at a level that we’ve never made before. We’re going to catch them within 10 months, they say,” he said. Hours before Trump touched down in Manila, Washington announced new rules on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle ASEAN members. Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special licence, as the countries were said to represent a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”. Singapore responded by saying it was now exploring ways to facilitate “trusted access” for firms based in the city-state. Pax Silica Trump will meet Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen. Hayley Channer, economic security director at the Sydney-based United States Studies Centre, said the Manila visit was “likely because the US is trying to further its Pax Silica initiative, to build a complete mine-to-chip supply chain”. Aimed at countering China’s dominance in semiconductors and rare earths, the initiative has been the focus of months of protests in the Philippines, as its flagship 1,620-hectare (about 4,000-acre) AI manufacturing hub north of Manila threatens to displace Indigenous families. “We are gathered here today to call for the stop of Pax Silica and to save the lands of the Filipino people,” Mariposa, a 21-year-old drag queen, told AFP at Tuesday’s protest while wearing a long black cape emblazoned with the words “Pax Silica Sashay Away!” Pax Silica signing ceremony. Photo: US Department of State. US Ambassador Lee Lipton said last week that a long-rumoured deal signing for the site would not take place during the president’s visit. As the ASEAN summit came to a close on Tuesday, President Marcos touted the bloc’s signing of a Digital Economy Framework Agreement — aimed at streamlining digital trade and cross-border payments — as its signature achievement. But he also acknowledged the failure to deliver a “Code of Conduct” on the South China Sea between ASEAN and China during the Philippines’ year as bloc chair. Marcos told reporters that “85-90 percent of it has actually been done”, leaving the ball in Singapore’s court when it takes the ASEAN reins next year.

title: Europe and China 3 – The Coming Showdown
zh_title: 欧洲与中国 3 – 即将到来的对决
source: 欧洲政策分析中心 （CEPA） - CEPA
summary: 这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第三部分。 2001年底中国加入世界贸易组织后，欧洲资产负债表上的负数就开始蔓延。但对于所有欧洲人来说，成本效益计算并不相同。德国等一些国家最初从高价值出口和合资企业中获益。其他国家，如希腊和葡萄牙，面临着大量低成本中国商品和与中国政府有关的实体的战略投资。中国经济规模仅为欧洲经济规模的八分之一
content:
这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第三部分。 2001年底中国加入世界贸易组织后，欧洲资产负债表上的负数就开始蔓延。但对于所有欧洲人来说，成本效益计算并不相同。德国等一些国家最初从高价值出口和合资企业中获益。其他国家，如希腊和葡萄牙，面临着大量低成本中国商品和与中国政府有关的实体的战略投资。在中华人民共和国于1978年12月十一届三中全会开始实施“改革开放”政策之前，中国经济规模仅相当于欧洲经济共同体的八分之一。到2025年，中国和欧盟的相对经济影响力几乎持平。它们合计约占世界贸易的三分之一。 1975 年，两国双边贸易额每年约 20 亿欧元（22 亿美元）；根据雅克·德洛尔研究所编制的数据，50 年后，这一数字为每天 20 亿欧元。无论如何衡量，这都应该是一个成功的故事。但两人并没有在同一个球场上比赛。中国的国家补贴，从优惠土地交易到直接财政援助和优惠的地方税收，为中国企业带来了竞争优势，从而降低了劳动力成本。
大量的保护主义规则和非关税准入壁垒让外国企业感到沮丧，并将投资引导到不可避免地与强制技术转让挂钩的合资企业。欧盟对中国的贸易逆差无情地攀升，从2001年的396亿欧元增至2022年Covid-19大流行后的峰值3970亿欧元，然后每年稳定在3500亿欧元以上。尽管欧盟保持着服务业顺差，但也只有数百亿美元。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。电子邮件提交 Δ document.getElementById( "ak_js_2" ).setAttribute( "value", ( new Date() ).getTime() ); gform.initializeOnLoaded( function() {jQuery('#gform_ajax_frame_1').on('load',function(){var content = jQuery(this).contents().find('*').html();var is_postback =contents.indexOf('GF_AJAX_POSTBACK') >= 0;if(!is_postback){return;}var form_content = jQuery(this).contents().find('#gform_wrapper_1');var is_confirmation = jQuery(this).contents().find('#gform_confirmation_wrapper_1').length > 0;var is_redirect =contents.indexOf('gformRedirect(){') >= 0;var is_form = form_content.length > 0 && is_redirect &&！

This is the third of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe.   The negative numbers began to cascade across European balance sheets as soon as China entered the World Trade Organization in late 2001.   But the cost-benefit calculations were not equal for all Europeans. Some nations, such as Germany, initially gained from high-value exports and joint ventures. Others, like Greece and Portugal, faced a surge of low-cost Chinese goods and strategic investments by entities linked to the Chinese state.  The Chinese economy was barely one-eighth the size of that of the European Economic Community before the People’s Republic embarked on its policy of “reform and opening up” at the Third Plenum of the Eleventh Central Committee in December 1978. By 2025, the relative economic weight of China and the European Union was almost equal. Together they account for about a third of world trade. In 1975, their bilateral trade was worth about €2bn ($2.2bn) annually; 50 years later, it was €2bn a day , according to figures compiled for the Institut Jacques Delors.   By any measure, it should have been a success story. But the two were not playing on the same field. State subsidies in China, ranging from concessionary land deals to direct financial aid and favorable local taxation, handed Chinese firms a competitive advantage which added to their low labor costs. A thicket of protectionist rules and non-tariff barriers to entry frustrated foreign enterprises and channeled investment into joint ventures tied, inevitably, to forced technology transfer.   The EU trade deficits with China climbed remorselessly, from €39.6bn in 2001 to peak at €397bn in 2022 after the Covid-19 pandemic, before settling above €350bn annually. While the EU maintains a surplus in services, it is only in the tens of billions.   Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. New infrastructure accelerated the flow of exports. While Chinese goods had to be shipped or flown to the United States, they could be loaded onto trains to Europe, cutting the transit time from more than a month to less than two weeks, avoiding bottlenecks and crisis points. Traffic on the railway link multiplied almost tenfold in the last decade.  At the same time, China’s leaders redirected their own investments abroad from buying fixed assets, like ports and factories, into new plants built to get around tariffs on electric vehicles and similar items. The Communist Party encouraged rapid growth in research and development, no longer content to copy and to sell. It meant to originate and to own the value in new products.  China’s patent filings now dwarf those by the EU, its universities regularly outrank their European counterparts, and Chinese academics lead the world in scientific publications. In short, a juggernaut was coming for the workplaces and welfare systems of Europe. The response has been episodic and ineffective.  In 2003, the European Commission declined to recognize China as a market economy, prompting ire in Beijing. The next year, the two made a customs co-operation agreement and pursued “dialogues” on tricky subjects like intellectual property and industrial policy.   A decade later, the EU changed its anti-dumping regulations to stay compliant with its WTO obligations but still refused to define China’s economy as playing by market rules. By then, Xi Jinping was settled in power, having taken all the great offices of the Chinese system between 2012 and 2013. Xi encouraged engagement on big-picture issues like climate change, but his focus on exports and technology acquisition was relentless. Meanwhile, waves of repression inside China created political barriers, notably to a bilateral agreement on investment which foundered amid strident criticism in Europe of the human rights abuses against the Uyghur Muslim minority in the far west of China. Such protests were never likely to move the Chinese leader. They merely encouraged him to grow economic ties with Russia and countries in what China was soon calling the “Global South.” The Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, followed by EU economic sanctions, deepened the dependency between Moscow and Beijing.   Their bilateral trade almost doubled as Russian oil and gas fueled Chinese factories and Chinese-made electric cars poured into the Russian market.  European leaders found that the political climate turned hawkish; Europe found itself caught between trade wars, a new strain of assertiveness in Chinese politics and the search for a balance between co-operation and rivalry, both between China and the West and within the EU. The Chinese decision starting in April 2025 to restrict exports of rare earths, valuable minerals for manufacturing everything from catalytic exhausts to pharmaceuticals, in reprisal for President Donald Trump’s tariffs, shocked business and political elites.  The “second China shock” has hollowed out the German industrial belts, forcing Berlin to move closer to the French preference for tariffs and barriers. By some counts in the German media, the country is losing more than 10,000 industrial jobs a month, fueling support for the right-wing AFD party, while France is struggling with its public debts.  In October, the two nations submerged their differences to write to the European Commission, urging it to use the trade weapon against competitors who exploited state subsidies and undervalued currency to destroy their rivals. There is also talk of diversifying supply chains and a “buy Europe” policy. The letter did not name names, but everyone knew the target was China. The proposed “second strike” capacity aimed at imposing duties on countries that retaliate when the EU imposes trade measures is an escalatory step that has uncomfortable echoes of nuclear deterrence doctrine. In Beijing, the Ministry of Commerce is unsheathing its own weapons and already talks of countries harming themselves by “wrong steps.”   The scene is set for a showdown of some kind. It is a far cry from the hopes of 2001.  Michael Sheridan is a veteran British foreign correspondent and is the author of ‘ The Gate to China ’, an acclaimed history of Hong Kong, and ‘ The Red Emperor: Xi Jinping and His New China ’, which is published by Hachette Books and has been translated into a dozen languages, including Ukrainian, Polish, and Japanese.   Europe’s Edge  is CEPA’s online journal covering critical topics on the foreign policy docket across Europe and North America. content:
这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章中的第二部分。起初，必要性是欧洲商业与中华人民共和国之间伙伴关系之母。在瑞士商学院，电梯制造商辛德勒的例子仍然是一个主题研究。 1979年，这家瑞士公司成为早期与中国的合资伙伴，尽管它与怡和洋行（Jardine Matheson）有联系，怡和洋行是一家与19世纪鸦片贸易有关的香港贸易公司。原因是：中国出现了住房危机。它正在向天空扩展，因为不断增长的人口需要塔楼。该国缺乏尖端技术，不得不到国外采购。最终，这家瑞士公司战胜了日本和美国的竞争对手。政治起了一定作用。瑞士于1950年承认中华人民共和国，是一个中立国。如今，中国拥有庞大的国内电梯行业，并与芬兰通力公司和日本日立公司等建立了合资企业。中国也需要汽车。它与大众汽车达成协议，到 1983 年春天，大众帕萨特的一个版本（更名为桑塔纳）开始在道路上行驶。其棱角分明的风格成为私人交通革命的象征。这些汽车是由上海大众汽车公司（现称为上汽集团）与德国公司和当地投资者的合资企业生产的。如今，上汽集团已成为电动汽车和电池领域的领导者。
在航空领域，空中客车公司开创了合资制造的先河，比美国飞机制造商麦道公司的合资企业更长久，并为欧洲发动机和技术的盈利出口铺平了道路。尽管中国致力于建造自己的商业上可行的民用客机，但这些出口仍然强劲。这些故事体现了欧洲的乐观情绪，这种乐观情绪伴随着中国从 2001 年开始加入世界贸易组织 (WTO)，并推动了本世纪初的贸易交易和外国直接投资。正如香港驻日内瓦代表所说，这是“双赢”。紧张的早期迹象出现在专利和所有权纠纷中。中国官员经常将“技术转让”视为对双方都有利的好事。它成为在某些领域开展业务的条件。跨国公司的国家经理往往主要热衷于扩大在中国的业务，他们会向总部保证他们的中国合作伙伴是值得信赖的。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

This is the second of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. At first, necessity was the mother of partnership between European commerce and the People’s Republic of China. At Swiss business schools, the example of Schindler, the elevator maker, remains a keynote study. In 1979, the Swiss company became an early joint venture partner with China, even though it had ties with Jardine Matheson, the Hong Kong-based trading house associated with the opium trade of the 19 th century. The reason: China had a housing crisis. It was expanding skyward because a growing population required tower blocks. The country lacked sophisticated technology and had to shop abroad. Eventually, the Swiss firm won out over Japanese and American competitors. Politics played a part. Switzerland had recognized the People’s Republic in 1950, and it was a neutral power. Today China has a giant domestic elevator industry of its own plus joint ventures with, among others, Kone of Finland and Hitachi of Japan. China also needed cars. It made a deal with Volkswagen and by the spring of 1983 a version of the VW Passat, renamed the Santana, was plying the roads. Its angular style became a symbol of a revolution in private transport. The cars were manufactured by Shanghai Volkswagen Automotive, today known as SAIC, in a joint venture with the German firm and local investors. Today SAIC is a leader in the field of electric vehicles and batteries.   In aviation, Airbus pioneered joint venture manufacturing, outlasting a venture by the US plane maker McDonnell-Douglas and paving the way for profitable European exports of engines and technology, which remain strong despite China’s drive to build a commercially viable civil airliner of its own. These stories exemplified the optimism in Europe which accompanied China’s membership of the World Trade Organization (WTO) from 2001 and drove trade deals and foreign direct investment through the early years of this century. It was, as the Hong Kong representative in Geneva had said, “win-win.” The early signs of strain emerged in disputes over patents and ownership. Chinese officials regularly spoke of “technology transfer” as a good which would serve both sides. It became a condition of doing business in certain fields. Multinational country managers, often keen primarily to expand their footprint in China, would assure head offices that their Chinese partners could be trusted. Meanwhile, low-cost Chinese manufactured goods poured into European markets under the tariffs agreed on entry to the WTO. Initially confident of their negotiating power as a bloc, the Europeans refrained from resorting to rhetoric about trade wars or dumping. The Chinese export wave, known today as the China Shock, was seen by specialists as a transitional phenomenon that would eliminate itself through the magic of free trade. Today’s leader, Xi Jinping, watched from a critical vantage point as the manufacturing and export boom in China turned a pariah state into an economic powerhouse that had foreign governments, banks and corporations knocking on its door. His fortunes, indeed, advanced with the country’s renaissance. Xi’s career took off in the coastal province of Fujian, which stood at the forefront of China’s export zones. It received a flood of investment from Taiwan, whose manufacturers realized that instead of trying to sell goods into the Chinese market, they should make things cheaply in China to sell to others. This was the trick that turned the world economy inside out. At some point during this period, party elders decided to favor Xi Jinping as a rising official whose consciousness of the value of trade was matched by his cautious disposition. In China, the consensus remained that prosperity and peace were indivisible (which also lowered the risks of any adventure to seize Taiwan). When Xi moved up the hierarchy to vice president in 2008, he visited a slew of European nations as he worked to understand foreign countries and to grow into the top role. He, too, was being auditioned: he met Joe Biden, then also vice president. For all the courtship of Europe, it was the United States which mattered most to China. That is why the financial crisis in the West of 2008 dealt such a blow to Chinese reformers. It broke out in the American credit markets and then spread to Asia. The economic slowdown was the most serious problem the Chinese regime had faced in the new century. Exports collapsed by a fifth, foreign investment slowed, domestic consumption fell, and thousands of factories closed, leaving between 10 and 20 million workers jobless. The blow fell most heavily in the coastal export zones where Xi had made his name and the global trade experiment was at its height. The crisis almost consumed the administration of President Hu Jintao and Prime Minister Wen Jiabao. The technocrats rallied the central bank, raided currency reserves and threw the power of the state behind a $500bn stimulus package that poured funds into high-speed trains and urban infrastructure, reforming the tax system and doling out credit. It was the zenith of pragmatic managerialism in China, but the legacy would be more Communist Party control, a taste for intervention in markets and an iron determination on the part of Xi Jinping that China would never again be subject to the shocks of international capitalism. Facing down America and balancing Chinese economic interests with Europe would be his mission. 黄仁勋 Megaspeed 丑闻对欧洲意味着什么？乍一看，情况并不多：欧洲人将继续购买英伟达芯片。但仔细观察就会发现，连锁反应将对跨大西洋关系以及欧洲与北京日益紧张的关系产生影响。荷兰及其明星芯片制造商 ASML 看起来尤其容易受到影响。黄也许是华盛顿最有影响力的中国鸽派。他几乎单枪匹马地说服唐纳德·特朗普总统及其内阁采取宽松的方式执行拜登时代对英伟达芯片的出口管制，这激怒了两党鹰派。他的影响力减弱，再加上有关通过新加坡向中国非法走私芯片规模的新揭露，意味着鹰派再次得势。美国商务部已经采取行动，禁止中国人工智能公司使用海外数据中心。三项法案似乎将被纳入《国防授权法》，以进一步打击中国使用美国芯片。其中之一——MATCH法案——针对的是中国的芯片制造工具供应。荷兰公司 ASML 是这些工具的全球主要制造商。在美国制裁的威胁下，它将被迫遵守其美国竞争对手目前面临的相同限制。
包括荷兰王室在内的欧洲和荷兰外交官已经游说反对 MATCH 法案，该法案看起来不太可能成为法律——直到 Megaspeed 丑闻爆发。 实际上，该法案将禁止 ASML 向中国销售新的芯片制造机器（中国约占该公司年收入的五分之一），并禁止 ASML 履行为该国现有机器提供服务的合同义务。获取最新注册以定期接收带宽电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作情况。电子邮件提交 Δ document.getElementById( "ak_js_4" ).setAttribute( "value", ( new Date() ).getTime() ); gform.initializeOnLoaded( function() {jQuery('#gform_ajax_frame_9').on('load',function(){var content = jQuery(this).contents().find('*').html();var is_postback =contents.indexOf('GF_AJAX_POSTBACK') >= 0;if(!is_postback){return;}var form_content = jQuery(this).contents().find('#gform_wrapper_9');var is_confirmation = jQuery(this).contents().find('#gform_confirmation_wrapper_9').length > 0;var is_redirect =contents.indexOf('gformRedirect(){') >= 0;var is_form = form_content.length > 0 && is_redirect &&！

What does the Jensen Huang Megaspeed scandal mean for Europe? At first glance, not much: Europeans will keep buying Nvidia chips. But a closer look shows that the ripple effects will have consequences for transatlantic relations and for Europe’s increasingly tense relationship with Beijing. The Netherlands and its star chip machine manufacturer, ASML, look particularly vulnerable. Huang was perhaps Washington’s most influential China dove. He almost single-handedly persuaded President Donald Trump and his cabinet to take a lax approach to enforcing Biden-era export controls on Nvidia chips, to the fury of hawks on both sides of the aisle. His diminished influence, coupled with fresh revelations around the extent of illegal chip smuggling to China via Singapore, means that the hawks once again have the wind in their sails. The Department of Commerce has already moved to  block  Chinese AI companies from using overseas data centers. Three bills look  set  to be rolled into the National Defense Authorization Act that would further crack down on China’s use of US chips.  One of them — the MATCH Act — takes aim at China’s supply of chipmaking tools. Dutch company ASML is the major global manufacturer of these tools. It would be forced to comply with the same restrictions currently faced by its US competitors, under threat of US sanctions.  European and Dutch diplomats, including the Dutch Royal Family, have already  lobbied  against the MATCH Act, which looked unlikely to pass into law — until the Megaspeed scandal broke. In effect, the Act would ban ASML from selling new chipmaking machines to China, which accounts for around a  fifth  of the company’s annual revenue, and from fulfilling its contractual obligations to service existing machines already in the country.  Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular Bandwidth emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. Even if the MATCH Act passes, the White House will have discretion over how aggressively the legislation is applied. President Trump has tried to shield Nvidia and maintain good relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping. That gives Washington leeway to decline to enforce its toughest provisions — but still leaves ASML vulnerable to shifting political priorities or a future, more hawkish administration. If the US ultimately forces ASML to cut off servicing to Chinese companies, the Netherlands — and Europe — could find themselves exposed to Chinese retaliation. When Beijing  imposed  export controls on rare earths in 2025 in response to US trade actions, it ensured European companies were also caught in the crossfire. Beijing would likely not hesitate to make an example out of the Netherlands in order to discourage other countries from allying too closely with Washington. The MATCH Act is being discussed just as Europe itself is in the middle of executing a major hawkish turn on China, driven by the latter’s industrial overcapacities and supply chain dominance. Whereas the EU was unwilling to take a strong stance on China during Trump’s first term — when administration officials pressed European countries to remove Huawei telecoms equipment — and under former President Joseph Biden, the bloc is now developing powerful new trade instruments directed against Beijing. Despite this shift, Europe’s China policy remains fundamentally defensive. European capitals do not share Washington’s interest in undermining China’s AI sector. In fact, the EU benefits from Chinese competition to closed-source US frontier labs. Europe’s telecoms incumbents are resisting ripping out Huawei from their networks,  arguing  that the exclusion of Chinese suppliers would be  costly  and leave them dependent on expensive local vendors. US China hawks should think twice before trying to strong-arm Europe into mirroring US China policy. Such a move would likely backfire by galvanizing anti-US and pro-China figures in Europe. There is a deal to be done. For their part, EU countries need to follow through on the tough talk and deliver on China de-risking, with concrete measures such as improving coordination and closing gaps in EU and national licensing of chipmaking components. If Washington sees Europe acting of its own accord, it can formally take the threat of sanctions off the table. In the end, controls that allies adopt through their own volition are likely to prove more durable than those imposed on them by ultimatum.
