(Source: Author’s research) Gaming Served as Gateway to Data Centers For Ms. Huang, as for Nvidia, the gaming industry provided a route into the compute business. PRC game publishers often set up foreign entities to serve overseas markets, providing a legitimate reason to import graphics processors and expand data center capacity. Huang became involved with 7Road Holdings (第七大道), a Hong Kong-listed game developer, after it had acquired a portfolio of gaming businesses held by an entity wholly owned by her and registered in the British Virgin Islands ( Caizhongshe , November 11). A circular announcing the acquisition identified a company owned by Kang Wei, Ningbo Jingxuan (宁波镜瑄), as a “party acting in concert” (一致行动人) with Ms. Huang. It also listed among the portfolio’s operating entities in the PRC a company previously owned by a subsidiary of Century Huatong (世紀華通), another firm with ties to Kang and Huang ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 25, 2019).  [3] With Ms. Huang now behind the scenes, Yunxi expanded her business network into the semiconductor and data center industries through cooperation with 7Road starting in 2022. A 7Road subsidiary committed renminbi (RMB) 330 million ($49 million) to a limited partnership managed by Yunxi whose sole asset was a 5.29 percent stake in a Shanghai-based semiconductor wafer manufacturer ( Hong Kong Exchange , May 24, 2022). 7Road also expanded into the data center and cloud computing businesses in 2019, offering cloud services for gaming and the possibility of third-party data center services in a cooperation framework ( Hong Kong Exchange , December 30, 2019; Hong Kong Exchange , May 9, 2021). A 7Road subsidiary involved in Huang’s gaming portfolio later became a vehicle for 7Road’s cloud computing business, buying graphics processors and servers ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 25, 2019).  [4] In 2022, it raised RMB 150 million ($24 million at the time) through a sale-and-lease-back of equipment that included 9,800 graphics processors ( Hong Kong Exchange , March 15, 2022). reported control transfers in May-Jul. 2016"}]} Notes [1] A cooptee is an MSS collaborator, whom the ministry uses for operational support—typically in exchange for favors. They can help make introductions, serve as a go-between for the MSS and a source, provide excuses for sources to travel to the PRC, or otherwise assist the MSS in its operations. The MSS may also approach these people because of the access, business, or other ability that they have to support operations ( National Interest , June 11, 2017). [2] In November 2014, CITIC Securities (中信证券) bought a 3.8 percent stake in a technology firm under a stock return swap with Hexi, helping Gu gain control of the listed company ( CSRC , May 12, 2017). Ms. Huang worked in securities financing at CITIC at the time. The deal may have brought her into contact with Kang a year before she joined Hexi ( Hexi Investment , March 17, 2017). [3] In 2014, Hexi subscribed for shares in Century Huatong connected to its acquisitions of Tianyou Software (天游软件) and Wuxi SevenCool (无锡七酷网络). In 2017, Wuxi SevenCool sold the gaming company Hangzhou Shengfeng (杭州盛锋) to Ningbo Jingxuan (宁波镜瑄), whose ultimate controller is Kang (CNINF, March 9, 2014 , March 7, 2017 ). [4] The name of this firm, Shanghai Lingsu (上海凌素), closely resembles another firm within Ms. Huang’s business network, Shanghai Lingsuda (上海领素达), which invests primarily in smart mobility and ride-hailing platforms (see the Interactive Map) ( CAIC , August 16, 2023; Hong Kong Exchange , December 23, 2024). Yunxi also entered the ownership chain of a data center holding company, also based in Shanghai, and in 2025 changed its own registered name to Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing Data Group (上海珑腾智算数据集团) ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 13, 2023; Times Weekly , November 9). In Shanghai business circles, it is common to register a series of companies with names that share the same Chinese characters or use different characters with the same pronunciation. Other businesspeople can then easily tell who actually controls a company from its name alone. [5] Kang had previously used companies he controlled, including Hexi, to take over three major Phicomm shareholding vehicles ( Sina Finance , August 10, 2018). [6] Such data centers under Kang’s control, with refurbishment nearing completion, would very likely use Nvidia chips smuggled into the PRC through Huang’s Megaspeed. [7] The business tactic of offering one’s spouse to another man reaches even much further back. During the Warring States period, Zichu (子楚), a prince of Qin (秦), took an interest in Zhao Ji (赵姬), the consort of the merchant Lu Buwei (吕不韦). Lu, considering how much he had already bet on Zichu to be the next King of Qin, offered Zhao Ji, who was already pregnant, to him. After Zichu became king of Qin, Lu was appointed chancellor and wielded power over the Qin court ( Records of the Grand Historian , accessed November 11). A historical conspiracy theory even held that Qin Shi Huang (秦始皇), first emperor of ancient China, was Lu and Zhao Ji’s son. In the early 2010s, PRC financial media and business books often portrayed Lu Buwei as a merchant who knew how to bet on real power (through whatever means), fueling an interest in him among businessmen of the era (see Fortune China , March 23, 2011). That was precisely when Kang rose to prominence in business. The post Alice Huang’s Shady Shanghai Ties to Business and Government appeared first on Jamestown .

这对中国来说也是一个巨大的胜利。” （观看）关于空中交通管制：“这是有 50 年历史的设备，必须更换……上届政府花费了数十亿美元，然后他们试图将其连接起来，但没有成功；” “它不仅不起作用，而且还让它倒退。所以，我们希望它能得到修复，我们希望它能够正确修复……当它完成后，我们将拥有世界上最好的系统。” （观看）关于最近的技术中断：“一切都很好。这些都是个人事件……我也认为媒体对此很感兴趣。如果这些事情发生在两年前、三年前，在极其无能和腐败的拜登政府，没有人会提到它……如果有人对我们这样做并且我们发现了这件事，他们知道我会受到什么影响。没有人会和我们一起玩游戏。” （观看）关于伊朗：“他们想要达成协议，但我想要一项可以持久的协议……如果我们有一位糟糕的总统，一位软弱的总统，我想要一项能够取代总统的协议……无论如何，我们都会完成它。” （观看）关于在新国会中与民主党人合作：“民主党人对我的评价非常惊人。没有人会相信……他们想要做交易。我拥有否决权……我有一种感觉，这将是令人难以置信的富有成效的两年。
因为他们会向我发送一份有关医疗保健的法案，我会说不行，我会否决它，然后他们会给我打电话……然后我们就坐下来。” （观看）关于超级智能：“昨晚我整晚都和习主席在一起，在晚宴上坐在他旁边，就在他的右手边，我们整个晚上都在说话，我们谈论了这个问题，他对我们在这方面做得如此出色感到惊讶。我们正在领导中国，我们正在领导全世界。” （观看）关于伊朗脏弹阴谋的报道：“有迹象表明伊朗正在关注天然气，他们正在关注生物——生物武器，不是很好——以及其他东西，我们会看到......这些都是令人讨厌的人......听着，如果我

Trump delivered a message of American resurgence in an exclusive live interview on Fox News from Shenzhen, China — just hours before his historic meeting with President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin. He highlighted the respect America now commands under his leadership, the decisive steps he is taking to modernize critical infrastructure, America’s clear lead in Super Intelligence, and his confidence in working with Congress over the next two years as he negotiates from a position of strength. Key moments: On China and President Xi: “The relationship that I have with China is a great one. You know, it’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship. You saw the seating last night. You saw the greeting yesterday… This is a great President, one of the great Presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody — and not only that, the fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people… the soldiers, the whole thing. It was a great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China, too.” ( Watch ) On air traffic control: “This is 50-year-old equipment, and it has to be changed… They spent billions of dollars, the previous Administration, and then they tried to hook it up and it didn’t work; not only didn’t it work, it set it back. So, we want it fixed, and we want it fixed right… When it’s finished, we will have the best system anywhere in the world.” ( Watch ) On recent tech outages: “Everything’s good. These are individual events… I also think that the press is sort of having a lot of fun with it. If these things would have happened two years ago, three years ago in the Biden Administration, which was grossly incompetent and corrupt, nobody would have mentioned it… If anybody did that to us and we found out about it, they know what the repercussions would be with me. Nobody’s going to play games with us.” ( Watch ) On Iran: “They want to make a deal, but I want a deal that can be lasting… If we have a bad President, a weak President, I want a deal that will supersede the President… One way or the other, we’ll finish it off.” ( Watch ) On working with Democrats in the new Congress: “I’ve been called by Democrats at a level that’s pretty amazing. Nobody would even believe it… They want to make deals. I have the veto power… I have a feeling that this is going to be an unbelievably productive two years. title: Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers
zh_title: 以社区为中心的学术界为科罗拉多州农民带来人工智能工具
summary: 科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”东 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县扩建项目 Tit
content:
科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”董 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县推广 职称 推广区域专家 会员等级 高级会员 母校内蒙古师范大学，位于呼和浩特；北京师范大学；纽约州立大学环境科学与林业学院，位于锡拉丘兹；科罗拉多州立大学全球分校 她构建了人工智能驱动的农业旅游聊天机器人 (AgriTourismAI.com)，帮助农民和牧场主启动和经营“农业旅游”业务。农业旅游是指农民向游客开放他们的土地以进行娱乐、教育或购物活动。常见的例子包括采摘自己的果园、如何种植蔬菜的课程以及手工产品的销售。董还举办研讨会，向农民和牧场主展示如何使用人工智能工具来帮助发展和管理他们的业务。她说她将自己视为大学和农村之间的纽带。 “我们（推广专家）充当桥梁，”她说。
“我们将校园与我们服务的农村社区联系起来。”许多农民和牧场主年龄较大，通常没有接受过技术培训。他们的子孙常常离开农场到城市工作，或者无法教他们新工具。如果没有帮助，人工智能的好处可能会与农民失之交臂。 Dong 的研讨会为他们提供了一条出路。Dong 凭借她的 AgriPivot AI Agent 入围 2026 年 GenAI for Good Challenge 决赛。该挑战赛由 IEEE Humanarian Technologies 和联合国国际电信联盟组织，她的项目是从 79 个国家的 318 个团队中选出的。她还获得了国家推广技术社区 (NETC) 颁发的 2026 年创新奖，以及国家社区发展推广专业人员协会 (NACDEP) 颁发的 2025 年国家和西部地区教育技术奖。作为首席研究员或联合首席研究员，她获得了七项竞争性资助，总额超过 25 万美元，其中包括由农业部国家食品和农业研究所支持的资金。董出生于北京，从小就热爱设计和解决问题。她的父母都是医生。小时候，她喜欢画新的、有创意的东西。她说，素描可以让她用图片解决脑海中的问题，并将它们作为实际设计写在纸上。这个习惯逐渐成为她与周围环境相处的一种方式。
她说：“我一直热衷于创造一些有形的东西来解决现实世界中的问题。”她并不将自己的人生方向归功于任何一位导师。相反，她说她所有的老师都帮助她为她的职业生涯奠定了基础。她就读于位于呼和浩特的内蒙古师范大学，这是一所培训教师的机构。 2013 年，她在那里获得了两个学士学位——一个是地理科学学士学位，另一个是教育学士学位。然后，她获得了课程和教学硕士学位

【原文 English Original】
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

title: Spartan puts $683 million price tag on Victorio moly, tungsten mine in New Mexico
zh_title: Spartan 对新墨西哥州 Victorio 钼钨矿标价 6.83 亿美元
source: MINING.COM 全球矿业（稀土/关键矿产）
summary: Spartan Metals（多伦多证券交易所代码：W；美国场外交易代码：SPRMF）估计，在新墨西哥州维多里奥建造一座地下钨钼矿将耗资 6.83 亿美元，并建有一座工厂，将钨精矿转化为切削工具和其他工业产品的原料。根据周四发布的初步经济评估，该项目位于州首府圣达菲西南约 440 公里处，将运营 24 年。该研究估计，按 8% 的贴现率和 31% 的内部收益率计算，税后净现值 (NPV) 为 21.4 亿美元。该项目还需要20.3亿美元
content:
Spartan Metals（多伦多证券交易所代码：W；美国场外交易代码：SPRMF）估计，在新墨西哥州维多里奥建造一座地下钨钼矿将耗资 6.83 亿美元，并建有一座工厂，将钨精矿转化为切削工具和其他工业产品的原料。根据周四发布的初步经济评估，该项目位于州首府圣达菲西南约 440 公里处，将运营 24 年。该研究估计，按 8% 的贴现率和 31% 的内部收益率计算，税后净现值 (NPV) 为 21.4 亿美元。该项目还需要 20.3 亿美元的支出来维持整个生命周期的运营。斯巴达首席执行官布雷特·马什（Brett Marsh）在新闻稿中表示：“这两种金属都对这些经济做出了贡献，因此任何一种金属的持续价格上涨都可以对潜在的项目经济产生有意义的影响。” “维多利亚可能成为美国工业和国防客户持久的国内钨和钼来源。”根据美国地质调查局的数据，美国上一次商业开采钨是在 2015 年。 S&P Global 的数据显示，中国约占全球精炼仲钨酸铵产能的 85%，仲钨酸铵是 Victorio 生产的中间产品。据 Fastmarkets 周四报道，尽管一些买家对价格上涨犹豫不决，但中国的出口管制仍导致供应紧张。周四，Spartan 股价在多伦多收于每股 26 美分不变，该公司估值约为 1,540 万加元（1,070 万美元）。
价格敏感性 该研究假设每 10 公斤三氧化钨为 1,350 美元，每磅钼为 20 美元。在测试的最低价格下，三氧化钨每 10 公斤 750 美元，钼每磅 15 美元，税后 NPV 降至 3.92 亿美元，回报率降至 14%。维多利亚会使用块崩落法，这是一种利用重力破碎岩石的地下方法。该研究预计每年可回收仲钨酸铵中约 4,100 吨三氧化钨，以及精矿中约 865 万磅钼。推断资源量占预定植物饲料的 39%。 8 月份的资源估算显示，测得和指示资源量为 7670 万吨，三氧化钨品位为 0.1%，钼品位为 0.09%，分别含有 1.655 亿磅和 1.479 亿磅。另外推断品位为 0.09% 三氧化钨和 0.06% 钼的产量为 9,240 万吨，分别为 1.876 亿磅和 1.3 亿磅。下一步 斯巴达计划将维多利亚推进到预可行性阶段。该研究建议投入 1,320 万美元的工作，包括钻探、冶金测试以及供水和尾矿研究。斯巴达对多尼根资源公司的核心索赔拥有选择权。行使该权利需要现金支付、1400万美元的勘探支出以及根据3月份协议在2034年之前进行可行性研究。其他钨项目正在北美其他地区推进。
加拿大联邦政府周一有条件批准了 Fireweed Metals（多伦多证券交易所代码：FWZ；美国场外交易代码：FWEDF）最多 1,400 万加元的融资，以帮助推进其 Mactung 钨项目做出建设决定。

【原文 English Original】
Spartan Metals (TSXV: W; US-OTC: SPRMF) estimates it would cost $683 million to build an underground tungsten and molybdenum mine at Victorio in New Mexico, with a plant to turn tungsten concentrate into a feedstock for cutting tools and other industrial products. The project, about 440 km southwest of state capital Santa Fe, would operate for 24 years, according to a preliminary economic assessment released Thursday. The study estimates an after-tax net present value (NPV) of $2.14 billion, at an 8% discount rate, and a 31% internal rate of return. The project requires another $2.03 billion in spending to sustain the operation over its life. “Both metals contribute to those economics, so continued price appreciation for either metal can make a meaningful difference to the underlying project economics,” Spartan CEO Brett Marsh said in the release. “Victorio could become a lasting domestic source of tungsten and molybdenum for U.S. industrial and defense customers.” The United States last mined tungsten commercially in 2015, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. China accounts for about 85% of global capacity to refine ammonium paratungstate, the intermediate product Victorio would make, according to S&P Global. China’s export controls are keeping supply tight even as some buyers balk at elevated prices, Fastmarkets reported Thursday. Spartan shares closed unchanged at C26¢ apiece on Thursday in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$15.4 million ($10.7 million). Price sensitivity The study assumes $1,350 per 10 kg of tungsten trioxide and $20 per lb. of molybdenum. At the lowest prices tested, $750 per 10 kg for tungsten trioxide and $15 per lb. for molybdenum, the after-tax NPV falls to $392 million and the return to 14%. Victorio would use block caving, an underground method that uses gravity to break the rock. The study projects annual recovery of about 4,100 tonnes of tungsten trioxide contained in ammonium paratungstate and 8.65 million lb. of molybdenum in concentrate. Inferred resources account for 39% of scheduled plant feed. An August resource estimate puts measured and indicated resources at 76.7 million tonnes grading 0.1% tungsten trioxide and 0.09% molybdenum, containing 165.5 million lb. and 147.9 million lb., respectively. Another 92.4 million inferred tonnes grade 0.09% tungsten trioxide and 0.06% molybdenum, for 187.6 million lb. and 130 million lb., respectively. Next steps Spartan plans to advance Victorio to prefeasibility. The study recommends $13.2 million of work, including drilling, metallurgical testing and studies of water supply and tailings. Spartan has an option on the core claims from Donegan Resources. Exercising it requires cash payments, $14 million in exploration spending and a feasibility study by 2034 under a March agreement. Other tungsten projects are advancing elsewhere in North America. Canada’s federal government on Monday conditionally approved up to C$14 million in financing for Fireweed Metals (TSX: FWZ; US-OTC: FWEDF) to help advance its Mactung tungsten project toward a construction decision.

title: Hong Kong doctor found guilty over fraudulently issuing over 3,700 Covid-19 vaccine exemptions
zh_title: 香港医生因欺诈性发放超过 3,700 份 Covid-19 疫苗豁免而被判有罪
summary: 一名香港医生被指控在大流行期间欺诈性地签发约 3,700 份 Covid-19 疫苗豁免证书，被判以不诚实的意图访问计算机罪。 BioNTech Covid 疫苗。照片：BioNTech。大江城在不认罪后于周五在区域法院接受判决。他还被判犯有洗钱罪。该诊所的一名志愿者 Kriselle Young 也因恶意访问计算机而被判有罪。检方称，两人于2022年2月至9月期间串谋诈骗卫生局
content:
一名香港医生被指控在大流行期间欺诈性地签发约 3,700 份 Covid-19 疫苗豁免证书，被判以不诚实的意图访问计算机罪。 BioNTech Covid 疫苗。照片：BioNTech。大江城在不认罪后于周五在区域法院接受判决。他还被判犯有洗钱罪。该诊所的一名志愿者 Kriselle Young 也因恶意访问计算机而被判有罪。据检方称，两人在 2022 年 2 月至 9 月期间合谋诈骗卫生局，不诚实地声称一些患者在健康上不适合接种 Covid-19 疫苗。戴秉国发放了 3,751 份疫苗豁免，每份收费在 1,000 港元至 4,000 港元之间。在 Covid-19 大流行期间，公众必须接种疫苗才能进入餐馆、健身房和其他指定场所。湾仔区域法院。资料图片：HKFP。欧内斯特·林法官在作出判决时表示，该诊所利用“自私”公众的“不合理、不科学的恐惧”来获取商业利益。他表示，戴某作为一名医生，有足够的医学知识，能够理解医院管理局的指引。然而，他给予疫苗豁免只是因为他的病人付钱给他，而不是在评估他们的医疗状况之后。
林说，杨不是受过训练的医生，但她向诊所介绍病人，并给护士分配工作。法官补充说，她故意协助戴输入虚假信息。警方诱捕行动 在一次导致两人被捕的卧底行动中，三名警察乔装成病人，前往戴的诊所请求豁免 Covid-19 疫苗，称他们害怕接种疫苗。戴发布了豁免，其中包括一名未出席任命的军官的儿子的豁免。一名妇女在购物中心外扫描她的 LeaveHomeSafe 应用程序。照片：香港政府一站通。戴在审判期间作证说，他并没有盲目地向患者提供豁免，称他们患有胃炎、胸痛、哮喘和其他使他们不适合接种疫苗的疾病。杨也作证说，她是诊所的志愿者，她相信戴的判断。她说她从来没有想到他滥用了豁免证书的发放。当检方询问她向患者发送的一条 WhatsApp 消息，上面写着“别担心，[它]肯定会发放”时，杨否认向患者保证他们将能够获得豁免证书，而是说她是在安慰他们。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong doctor accused of fraudulently issuing around 3,700 Covid-19 vaccine exemption certificates during the pandemic has been found guilty of accessing a computer with dishonest intent. BioNTech Covid vaccine. Photo: BioNTech. Tai Kong-shing received his verdict at the District Court on Friday after pleading not guilty. He was also found guilty of money laundering. A volunteer at the clinic, Kriselle Young, was also found guilty of accessing a computer with dishonest intent. According to the prosecution, the pair conspired to defraud the Health Bureau between February and September 2022 by dishonestly claiming that some patients were medically unfit to receive the Covid-19 vaccine. Tai handed out 3,751 vaccine exemptions, charging between HK$1,000 and HK$4,000 each. During the Covid-19 pandemic, members of the public were required to be vaccinated to access restaurants, gyms and other specified premises. District Court in Wan Chai. File photo: HKFP. Delivering the verdict, Judge Ernest Lin said the clinic made use of the “unreasonable, unscientific fears” of “selfish” members of the public for commercial gain. He said Tai, as a doctor, had sufficient medical knowledge to understand the Hospital Authority’s guidelines. Yet he gave out vaccine exemptions simply because his patients were paying him, rather than after assessing their medical conditions. Lin said that Young was not a trained medical practitioner, but that she introduced patients to the clinic and allocated work to the nurses. She knowingly assisted Tai in inputting false information, the judge added. Police sting operation During an undercover operation that led to the pair’s arrest, three police officers disguised themselves as patients and visited Tai’s clinic to request Covid-19 vaccine exemptions, saying they were afraid to get the jab. Tai issued the exemptions, including one for an officer’s son who was not at the appointment. A woman scans her LeaveHomeSafe app outside a shopping mall. Photo: GovHK. Tai testified during the trial that he did not blindly give out exemptions to patients, saying they had suffered from gastritis, chest pain, asthma and other conditions that made them unfit for the vaccine. Young also testified, saying that she was a volunteer at the clinic and that she trusted Tai’s judgement. She said she never thought that he had abused the issuing of exemption certificates. When asked by the prosecution about a WhatsApp message she had sent to a patient reading “don’t worry, [it’ll] definitely be issued,” Young denied reassuring the patient that they would be able to obtain an exemption certificate, saying instead that she was comforting them.

title: Alleged UK spy for Hong Kong died by suicide ahead of trial, British jury rules
zh_title: 英国陪审团裁定，被指控的英国香港间谍在审判前自杀身亡
summary: 英国陪审团发现，一名被指控为香港从事间谍活动的前英国海军陆战队员自杀身亡。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）在一家公共服务公司未能找到他并安装他的电子标签后结束了自己的生命。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）是被伦敦警方指控涉嫌为香港从事间谍活动的三名男子之一。照片：皇家海军陆战队。 2024 年 5 月，这位 37 岁的男子被发现死于梅登黑德的格伦费尔公园。几周前，他因涉嫌协助香港情报部门而根据英国国家安全法被捕并受到指控。 Trickett – 内政部移民办公室
content:
英国陪审团发现，一名被指控为香港从事间谍活动的前英国海军陆战队员自杀身亡。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）在一家公共服务公司未能找到他并安装他的电子标签后结束了自己的生命。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）是被伦敦警方指控涉嫌为香港从事间谍活动的三名男子之一。照片：皇家海军陆战队。 2024 年 5 月，这位 37 岁的男子被发现死于梅登黑德的格伦费尔公园。几周前，他因涉嫌协助香港情报部门而根据英国国家安全法被捕并受到指控。特里克特是内政部移民官员，在拘留期间被发现在牢房内试图自残，但两天后被保释。 💡 如果您需要支援，请致电：撒玛利亚会 2896 0000（24小时，多语种）、预防自杀中心 2382 0000 或政府心理健康热线 18111。香港辅导及心理学会提供中英文 WhatsApp 热线：6218 1084。另请参阅：HKFP 心理健康热线卫生服务指南。据英国广播公司报道，雷丁验尸官法院的陪审团周三发现，为英国政府提供司法和惩教服务的 Serco 多次“未能采取合理措施”找到他的地址。特里克特的同案被告卫彼得·韦(Peter Wai)和袁国强(Bill Yuen)因协助香港外国情报部门于6月分别被判入狱10年和8年。
前英国边防部队官员韦伟被判在香港驻伦敦经济贸易办事处办事处经理袁先生的命令下进行“影子警务”行动。左起：香港经济贸易办事处（香港经贸办）官员袁国强和前英国边防部队官员韦伟伟。照片：伦敦警察厅。这两名具有中英双重国籍的人针对的是居住在英国的香港民主抗议者。香港否认与明显的间谍活动有任何联系。全文：解释者：英国当局为何逮捕与香港驻伦敦经济贸易办事处（香港经济贸易办事处）有联系的 3 名男子。照片：维基共享资源。据称，这两人监视的人中有活动人士罗冠聪 (Nathan Law)，他被香港国安警察通缉，悬赏 100 万港元。由于担心“羞辱”，特里克特于 2024 年 5 月 23 日（即他应出庭的前一天）写了一封给家人的最后一封信。据报道，陪审团表示：“在得知警方试图找到他并担心他会被逮捕并重新拘留后，马特提前了他的计划，并将信函的日期重新调整为 5 月 19 日。”特里克特的一位朋友上周告诉法庭，特里克特自 2013 年以来一直担任私人安全顾问，他担心可能的定罪会带来“耻辱”，并警告他可能会自杀。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）是被伦敦警方指控涉嫌为香港从事间谍活动的三名男子之一。
照片：LinkedIn via M.Trickett 高级验尸官 Heidi Connor 表示 Serco 尚未进行内部调查，并补充说该公司必须“改进其系统”以降低更多人死亡的风险。一个简单的谷歌地图搜索就可以避免她所说的“非常罕见”的情况。在周三的裁决之后，Serco 的发言人表示，该公司将审查验尸官的报告和建议。

【原文 English Original】
A former British marine who was charged with spying for Hong Kong died by suicide, a UK jury has found. Matthew Trickett took his own life after a public services firm failed to locate him and fit his electronic tag. Matthew Trickett, one of the three men charged by London police on suspicion of spying for Hong Kong. Photo: Royal Marines. In May 2024, the 37-year-old was found dead in Maidenhead’s Grenfell Park. He had been arrested and charged under the UK’s National Security Act weeks earlier for allegedly assisting Hong Kong’s intelligence service. Trickett – a Home Office immigration officer – was seen attempting self-harm in his cell while in detention, but was released on bail two days later. 💡 If you are in need of support , please call: The Samaritans 2896 0000 (24-hour, multilingual), Suicide Prevention Centre 2382 0000 or the gov’ t mental health hotline on 18111. The Hong Kong Society of Counselling and Psychology provides a WhatsApp hotline in English and Chinese: 6218 1084. See also: HKFP’s mental health services guide. On multiple occasions, Serco – which provides judicial and correctional services to the UK government – “failed to take reasonable steps” to locate his address, the jury at Reading Coroner’s Court found on Wednesday, according to the BBC. Peter Wai and Bill Yuen, Trickett’s co-defendants, were jailed for 10 and eight years, respectively, in June for assisting Hong Kong’s foreign intelligence service. Wai, a former UK Border Force officer, was convicted of conducting a “shadow policing” operation upon the orders of Yuen, an office manager at the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London. From left: Hong Kong Economic Trade Office (HKETO) official Bill Yuen and former UK Border Force officer Peter Wai. Photos: Metropolitan Police. The two British-Chinese dual nationals targeted Hong Kong pro-democracy protesters living in the UK. Hong Kong denied any link to the apparent spying . In full: Explainer: Why UK authorities arrested 3 men linked to Hong Kong’s trade office The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (HKETO) in London. Photo: Wikimedia Commons. Among those the pair were said to have surveilled was activist Nathan Law, who is wanted by national security police in Hong Kong with a HK$1 million bounty on his head. Fear of ‘humiliation’ Trickett had penned a final letter to his family dated May 23, 2024 – the day before he was due to appear in court. “Upon learning that police were trying to locate him and fearing he would be arrested and taken back to custody, Matt brought his plan forward and re-dated his letter to May 19,” the jury reportedly said. One of his friends told the court last week that Trickett, who had worked as a private security consultant since 2013, feared the “humiliation” of a possible conviction and had warned he might kill himself. Matthew Trickett, one of the three men charged by London police on suspicion of spying for Hong Kong. Photo: LinkedIn via M. Trickett Senior coroner Heidi Connor said Serco had yet to carry out an internal investigation, adding that the company must “improve its systems” to mitigate the risk of more people dying. A simple Google Maps search could have averted what she nevertheless said was a “very rare” scenario. Following Wednesday’s ruling, a spokesperson for Serco said the company would review the coroner’s report and recommendation.

title: Hong Kong man jailed for life for murdering yoga instructor ex-girlfriend in luxury hotel
zh_title: 香港男子在豪华酒店谋杀瑜伽教练前女友被判终身监禁
summary: 一名香港男子因四年前在豪华酒店房间内刺死瑜伽教练前女友而被判处终身监禁。高等法院。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周五，32 岁的亚历克斯·罗 (Alex Lo) 在高等法院被判处无期徒刑，一天前，由五男两女组成的七名陪审团一致判定犯有谋杀罪。他被判于2022年6月29日至6月30日在西九龙丽思卡尔顿酒店谋杀瑜伽教练Aqua Chow。在一封缓解信中，罗向周、她的母亲和朋友道歉，并说
content:
一名香港男子因四年前在豪华酒店房间内刺死瑜伽教练前女友而被判处终身监禁。高等法院。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周五，32 岁的亚历克斯·罗 (Alex Lo) 在高等法院被判处无期徒刑，一天前，由五男两女组成的七名陪审团一致判定犯有谋杀罪。他被判于2022年6月29日至6月30日在西九龙丽思卡尔顿酒店谋杀瑜伽教练Aqua Chow。据法庭新闻媒体《见证人》报道，罗在一封缓刑信中向周、她的母亲和朋友道歉，并表示他只是不认罪，并根据一位未透露姓名的律师的建议接受审判。 “如果定罪20年、30年监禁，我相信我最早就会认罪，”他用中文写道。根据香港法律，被判犯有谋杀罪的成年人将面临强制性终身监禁，认罪后不得减刑。罗说，他从未希望公开披露他与周的关系细节，并补充说她是他“最心爱的女人”。 “我在这段感情中用了错误的方式去爱，我愿意承担后果，”他写道。然而，法官郭定邦认为，罗只表现出了轻微的悔恨，并指出他试图让陪审团相信他的行为源于“盲目的爱情”以及与周的财务纠纷。
法官表示，罗刺伤周是出于愤怒、仇恨和嫉妒，“也许根本与爱无关。”法官补充道，如果他真的爱她，他应该饶她一命。Aqua Chow。照片：yoga.aqua，来自 Instagram。法官援引政府法医病理学家Gary Ying的证词指出，周身上有43处刀伤，最深达15厘米。法官称，被告将周放在浴缸里，并在离开酒店前换了衣服，称他的行为冷静且深思熟虑。法官表示，他在审讯期间也没有说出真相，而是声称自己在周女士的挑衅下刺伤了周女士，以减轻自己的罪行。周去世时年仅23岁。 2022 年 6 月 30 日，她的尸体在酒店浴缸中被发现，当时她原定飞往美国参加瑜伽培训课程。法庭在庭审中获悉，罗与周于 2021 年 2 月成为情侣，并于次年 1 月分手，但仍保持联系。罗作证称，他带周女士去高档餐厅并为她购买奢侈品而欠下了巨额债务，并表示他非常爱她。他说，债务让他产生了自杀念头，因为贷款公司追着他还钱。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong man has been sentenced to life behind bars for murdering his yoga instructor ex-girlfriend by stabbing her inside a luxury hotel room four years ago. The High Court. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Alex Lo, 32, was given life imprisonment at the High Court on Friday, a day after being unanimously found guilty of murder by a seven-member jury comprising five men and two women. He was convicted of murdering yoga instructor Aqua Chow between June 29 and June 30, 2022, at the Ritz-Carlton in West Kowloon. In a mitigation letter, Lo apologised to Chow, her mother and friends, and said that he only pleaded not guilty and stood trial on the advice of an unnamed lawyer, according to court news outlet The Witness. “If there were a fixed penalty of 20 or 30 years in jail, I believe I would have pleaded guilty at the earliest stage,” he wrote in Chinese. Under Hong Kong law, adults convicted of murder face mandatory life imprisonment, with no sentencing discount for pleading guilty. Lo said he had never hoped to publicly disclose the details of his relationship with Chow, adding that she was his “most beloved woman.” “I used the wrong way to love in this relationship and I am willing to bear the consequences,” he wrote. Judge Anthony Kwok, however, found that Lo only demonstrated slight remorse, noting he sought to convince the jury that his actions stemmed from “blind love” and financial disputes with Chow. The judge said Lo stabbed Chow out of anger, hatred, and jealousy, and “perhaps it was nothing about love at all.” If he really loved her, the judge added, he should have spared her life. Aqua Chow. Photo: yoga.aqua, via Instagram. Citing testimony from government forensic pathologist Gary Ying, the judge noted that Chow had sustained 43 knife wounds, with the deepest reaching 15 centimetres. The defendant placed Chow inside a bathtub and changed his clothes before leaving the hotel, the judge said, calling his actions calm and deliberate. He also did not tell the truth during the trial, instead claiming that he stabbed Chow after being provoked by her in a bid to lessen his offence, the judge said. Chow was 23 when she died. She had been scheduled to fly to the US for a yoga training course when her body was found in the hotel bathtub on June 30, 2022. The court heard during the trial that Lo and Chow became a couple in February 2021 and broke up the following January, although they stayed in touch. Lo testified that he had run up enormous debt taking Chow to high-end restaurants and purchasing luxury items for her, saying he loved her very much. The debt left him suicidal, he said, as loan companies chased him to repay the money.

title: Hong Kong security chief hits out at The Washington Post over ‘scaremongering’ op-ed by wanted activist
zh_title: 香港保安局局长猛烈抨击《华盛顿邮报》，指责通缉活动人士发表“危言耸听”的专栏文章
summary: 香港保安局局长对《华盛顿邮报》进行了猛烈抨击，称其是被香港国家安全部门通缉的美国活动人士许慧娴发表的“危言耸听”的评论文章。保安局局长邓克里斯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在谈到活动人士黄之锋被判处 10 年监禁时，许表示，在备受瞩目的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 贸易会议上，商界领袖应向官员提出“政治犯”案件，并要求明确香港的国家安全立法将如何适用于企业。
content:
香港保安局局长对《华盛顿邮报》进行了猛烈抨击，称其是被香港国家安全部门通缉的美国活动人士许慧娴发表的“危言耸听”的评论文章。保安局局长邓克里斯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在谈到活动人士黄之锋被判处10年监禁时，许表示，在备受瞩目的亚太经合组织(APEC)贸易会议上，商界领袖应向官员提出“政治犯”案件，并要求明确香港的国家安全立法将如何适用于在香港经营的企业。保安局局长邓克里斯在周五的一封信中表示，许的文章“严重歪曲香港维护国家安全的法律”。 “我们绝大多数从事普通公民生活的居民，包括新闻、国际交流，最重要的是合法的商业活动，没有什么可担心的，”唐说。
唐说，具有讽刺意味的是，该报发表这篇文章时，美国“维持着最广泛、最严厉的国家安全法律框架之一，对任何可能与外部势力勾结危害美国国家安全的人采取零容忍态度”。他还驳斥了许氏将黄家驹和民主派媒体大亨黎智英描述为“出于政治目的”而入狱的说法，两人均因串通相关罪行而入狱。黄之锋于2019年6月17日从荔枝角接待中心获释。资料照片。 “在香港，任何违法者，无论其政治立场、背景或地位如何，都必须承担法律责任。反过来说黄和黎因政治原因入狱，完全是歪曲事实，”唐说。另请参阅：黄之锋的监狱信件揭示了香港活动人士面临又一个十年牢狱之灾的内心转变 2023 年 12 月，香港国家安全当局对许先生发出逮捕令，并悬赏 100 万港元以获取导致她被捕的信息。被指控与外国势力勾结的许慧琳现居住在美国，并于 2022 年获得美国政治庇护。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong’s security chief has hit out at The Washington Post over what he called a “scaremongering” opinion piece by US-based activist Frances Hui, who is wanted by the city’s national security authorities. Secretary for Security Chris Tang. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Pointing to the 10-year jail sentence handed down to activist Joshua Wong, Hui said that business leaders at the high-profile Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) trade meeting should raise the cases of “political prisoners” with officials and demand clarity on how Hong Kong’s national security legislation will be applied to businesses operating in the city. In a Friday letter, Secretary for Security Chris Tang said Hui’s article “grossly misrepresents the laws of Hong Kong for safeguarding national security.” “The vast majority of our residents who engage in ordinary civic life, including journalism, international exchanges and, most importantly, legitimate business activities have nothing to worry about,” Tang said. ‘Political purposes’ It was “ironic,” Tang said, that the newspaper had run the article when the US “maintains one of the most extensive and toughest national security legal frameworks with zero tolerance of anyone who may collude with external forces to endanger US national security.” He also rejected Hui’s characterisation of Wong and pro-democracy media magnate Jimmy Lai, both in prison over collusion-related offences, as being jailed for “political purposes.” Joshua Wong released from Lai Chi Kok Reception Centre on June 17, 2019. File photo. “In Hong Kong, anyone who breaks the law, regardless of their political stance, background or status, must be held legally accountable. To conversely claim that Wong and Lai were imprisoned for political reasons is a complete distortion of the truth,” Tang said. See also: Joshua Wong’s prison letters reveal inner shift as Hong Kong activist faces another decade behind bars In December 2023, Hong Kong’s national security authorities issued a warrant for Hui’s arrest and offered HK$1 million for information leading to her arrest. Hui, who stands accused of colluding with foreign forces, lives in the US, where she was granted political asylum in 2022.

title: China, US, Russia issue ‘Declaration toward Peace’ after first summit
zh_title: 中美俄首次峰会后发表《和平宣言》
summary: 中国、美国和俄罗斯领导人举行史无前例的峰会后于周四发表了《和平宣言》，提出了改革联合国和控制国际刑事法院的共同目标。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会期间，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京、中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达麒麟山庄参加三方会议时合影留念。照片：Vyacheslav Prokofyev/法新社。习近平、唐纳德·特鲁
content:
中国、美国和俄罗斯领导人举行史无前例的峰会后于周四发表了《和平宣言》，提出了改革联合国和控制国际刑事法院的共同目标。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会期间，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京、中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达麒麟山庄参加三方会议时合影留念。照片：Vyacheslav Prokofyev/法新社。习近平、特朗普和普京在中国会晤的背景复杂，俄罗斯在乌克兰的攻势持续多年，特朗普在中东陷入困境，而崛起的中国则希望加强在东亚的影响力。白宫版本的声明称，“三位国家元首就当前国际形势深入交换了意见，致力于维护战略稳定和国际安全。” “我们讨论了民主问题。什么是民主？它是什么？这是某些圈子联合起来的自由秩序，现在仍在试图强加给全世界，”普京在南方城市深圳举行的新闻发布会上说。三人围坐在一张深色的大圆桌前，围绕从核武器到乌克兰战争等重大话题发表了开场白，圆桌中央摆放着粉红色的花朵。
麒麟山庄的闭门讨论在一个小时二十分钟后结束。特朗普称领导人正在“创造历史”，普京则称他们写下了“外交史上新的一页”。习近平表示，“三个国家在维护世界和平方面有着共同的观点”。在返回华盛顿的途中，特朗普召集了一次欧洲领导人会议，讨论乌克兰问题并向他们通报三方峰会的最新情况。 2026 年 2 月，布鲁塞尔欧盟委员会总部前悬挂着乌克兰和欧盟旗帜。照片：欧盟委员会。并非所有欧洲领导人都对此印象深刻：德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨称特朗普-习近平-普京会谈是一次“合影”，法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙表示，这不会“导致世界重组”。特朗普表示，他将于周五举行新闻发布会，介绍他的“伟大且具有重大意义的中国之行”。国际刑事法院、联合国和石油在联合声明中，特朗普、习近平和普京“认识到国家同意和尊重国家官员豁免权的原则至关重要，并同意国际刑事法院和其他类似机构不得滥用管辖权”。普京受到国际刑事法院逮捕令的制裁，而特朗普政府则誓言要“一砖一瓦”解散该法院。国际刑事法院。资料照片：维基共享资源。
领导人表示，他们“致力于改革联合国，使联合国能够更有效地应对全球挑战，履行其国际和平与安全的基本使命”。联合声明称，各国计划增加成品油供应和生产，并重申“稳定能源流动”的重要性。这次峰会引发了人们的担忧，担心这三人想要将全球划分为势力范围，例如通过做出影响乌克兰而不是基辅或欧洲的决定。但特朗普表示，他希望“欧洲站在他一边”就乌克兰问题达成协议

【原文 English Original】
China, the United States and Russia issued a “Declaration toward Peace” on Thursday after their leaders held an unprecedented summit, laying out common ambitions to overhaul the UN and keep the International Criminal Court in check. Russia’s President Vladimir Putin, China’s President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump pose for photos as they arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China’s southern Guangdong province, on November 19, 2026. Photo: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/AFP. Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China against a complex backdrop, with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, Trump bogged down in the Middle East and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. “The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security,” a White House version of the statement said. “We discussed the question of democracy. And what is democracy? It’s what? It’s the liberal order that certain circles put together and still now are trying to impose on the whole world,” Putin told a news conference in the southern city of Shenzhen. The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa ended after an hour and 20 minutes. Trump said the leaders were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”. “The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said. On his way home to Washington, Trump called into a meeting of European leaders to discuss Ukraine and update them on his three-way summit. Ukrainian and European Union flags in front of the European Commission headquarters in Brussels in February 2026. Photo: European Commission. Not all of those European leaders were impressed: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the Trump-Xi-Putin talks a “photo op”, and French President Emmanuel Macron said it would not “lead to a reorganisation of the world”. Trump said he would give a press conference on Friday about his “Great and Highly Consequential Trip” to China. ICC, UN and oil In their joint statement, Trump, Xi and Putin “recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction”. Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant, while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”. International Criminal Court. File photo: Wikicommons. The leaders said they were “committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security”. The joint statement said the countries plan to boost supply and production of refined petroleum products, and reaffirmed the importance of “stable energy flows”. The summit stoked fears that the three men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence , for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. But Trump said he wanted to make a deal on Ukraine “with Europe by his side”, accourding to special US envoy Jared Kushner. ‘Reducing nuclear risks’ Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”. Putin responded in English: “Nice to meet you.” Trump and Xi then came together — their third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting a “very special relationship”. Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said. Beijing, Washington and Moscow previously gave different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, a forum of 21 economies around the Pacific Rim. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. Washington had also flagged up the Iran war and nuclear disarmament as topics of discussion, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. China’s nuclear arsenal. File Photo: CCTV screenshot. The final statement said that the countries would “conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.” ‘Cheap violin’ Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi met Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and a flyover. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting would be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin. The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions”, said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute. “Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said.

title: Jensen Huang question gets reporter ejected from Trump-Xi-Putin summit
zh_title: 黄仁勋提问导致记者被驱逐出特朗普-习近平-普京峰会
summary: 据报道，一名彭博社记者在中国共产党领导人在场的情况下向美国总统提出敏感问题后，被逐出美国、中国和俄罗斯领导人之间的历史性三边会议。据《华盛顿邮报》报道，彭博新闻社首席政治记者、该媒体主要节目《彭博监控》联合主持人安娜玛丽·霍登问道：“特朗普总统，黄仁勋是否对美国不忠？”随后，第二位记者开始在 Ch 之前问第二个问题。
content:
据报道，一名彭博社记者在中国共产党领导人在场的情况下向美国总统提出敏感问题后，被逐出美国、中国和俄罗斯领导人之间的历史性三边会议。据《华盛顿邮报》报道，彭博新闻社首席政治记者、该媒体主要节目《彭博监控》联合主持人安娜玛丽·霍登问道：“特朗普总统，黄仁勋是否对美国不忠？”随后，第二名记者开始提出第二个问题，随后中国官员让该小组闭嘴。目前尚不清楚特朗普是否能够回答这两个问题。福克斯新闻的白宫高级记者雅基·海因里希（Jacqui Heinrich）10日表示，亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会的东道国中国告诉记者，“大声提问被认为是极其粗鲁的”，任何这样做的人“都会被从房间里拉出来”，这可能暗示了这一决定的背后是提问的性质，而不是其内容。黄仁勋突然辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，成为过去几周的重大丑闻。
尽管他承认有外遇，但他没有透露第三方的名字，据报道是 Megaspeed 的中国高管 Alice Huang，她还被指控将价值 75 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国，并向中国情报部门传递信息。 近年来，美国和中国一直处于竞争之中，人工智能是中国共产党重点发展的行业之一。这场争夺人工智能“霸主地位”的竞赛导致白宫对其最强大的芯片实施出口管制，并禁止包含美国技术的硬件进入中国。但即使特朗普来了个180度大转弯，最终在2025年12月允许英伟达H100芯片进入中国，只要该公司能够获得出口许可证，英伟达最先进的Blackwell和即将推出的Vera Rubin芯片对中国企业来说仍然遥不可及。除此之外，华盛顿还正在堵住一个漏洞，该漏洞允许中国人工智能公司通过将数据导出到位于其他国家的数据中心来利用美国的计算能力。尽管有这些控制措施，人工智能芯片走私的谣言仍然存在，包括 Supermicro 联合​​创始人 Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw 在内的一些人因芯片转移而被捕。中国还对其记者实施更严格的控制并审查敏感话题。作为APEC峰会和三边会议的东道主，它可以排除它认为违反其标准的记者。
海因里希表示，白宫主张霍登参加三边会议，但中方似乎拒绝对他们的决定做出让步。

【原文 English Original】
A Bloomberg reporter was ejected from a historic trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China, and Russia after reportedly asking a sensitive question to the U.S. President while in the presence of the leader of the Chinese Communist Party. According to The Washington Post , Bloomberg News journalist Annmarie Hordern, the chief political correspondent and co-host of the media outlet’s leading program, Bloomberg Surveillance , asked, “President Trump, has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?” A second reporter had then started asking a second question before Chinese officials shushed the group. It’s unclear if Trump was able to answer both these questions. Senior White House Correspondent for Fox News Jacqui Heinrich said on X that China, the host country of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit where the trilateral meeting was happening along the side, told journalists that “yelling questions is considered extremely rude” and that anyone doing so “will be pulled from the room,” possibly implying the nature of the questions' delivery, rather than its content, was behind the decision. Jensen Huang’s sudden resignation as the CEO of Nvidia has been a major scandal in the past few weeks. Even though he admitted to having an affair, he did not name the third party, reported to be Alice Huang, a Chinese executive for Megaspeed who’s also accused of diverting $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China and passing along information to Chinese intelligence. The U.S. and China have been locked in a rivalry in recent years, with artificial intelligence being one of the industries that the Chinese Communist Party is focusing on. This race to achieve “supremacy” in AI has led the White House to impose export controls on its most powerful chips and to bar hardware containing U.S. tech from making its way into China. But even though Trump made a 180-degree turn and finally allowed Nvidia H100 chips into China in December 2025, provided the company can secure export licenses, the most advanced Blackwell and upcoming Vera Rubin chips from Nvidia are still out of reach for Chinese companies. Aside from that, Washington is also closing a loophole that allowed Chinese AI firms to take advantage of American compute by exporting their data to data centers located in other countries. Despite all those controls, rumors of AI chip smuggling still persist, with several individuals, including Supermicro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw , getting arrested for chip diversion. China also puts tighter control on its journalists and censors sensitive topics. As the host of the APEC summit and the trilateral meeting, it could exclude reporters that it thinks violate its standards. Heinrich said that the White House advocated for Hordern’s inclusion in the trilateral meeting, but it seems that the Chinese refused to budge on their decision.

title: Indian Navy Exploring Development of Rotating Detonation Engine Powered Supersonic Cruise Missile
zh_title: 印度海军探索发展旋转爆震发动机动力超音速巡航导弹
summary: 印度海军已表示有兴趣支持开发旋转爆震发动机（RDE）驱动的超音速海军导弹。该问题陈述是在 2026 年 10 月举行的 Swavlamban 2026 海军旗舰展览期间发布的纲要的一部分，旨在展示国防创新。问题陈述的全文如下：该问题陈述确定了与旋转爆震发动机 (RDE) 研究相关的拟议本土超音速海军导弹计划。 RDE 研究将旋转爆炸作为推进原理。挑战
content:
印度海军已表示有兴趣支持开发旋转爆震发动机（RDE）驱动的超音速海军导弹。该问题陈述是在 2026 年 10 月举行的 Swavlamban 2026 海军旗舰展览期间发布的纲要的一部分，旨在展示国防创新。问题陈述的全文如下：该问题陈述确定了与旋转爆震发动机 (RDE) 研究相关的拟议本土超音速海军导弹计划。 RDE 研究将旋转爆炸作为推进原理。面临的挑战是确定它是否为所述海军应用提供可靠、可支持的能力途径。评估应区分科学可行性、组件成熟度、综合演示准备情况和服务使用资格。需要独立的证据来证实所声称的相对于现有推进替代方案的优势。该计划应在整个评估过程中保持明确的要求、配置控制、专家安全监督和结果的可追溯性。国内设计所有权、制造可重复性、环境适应性和长期支持是核心考虑因素。预期结果是对可行性和成熟度进行基于证据的评估，并得到授权研究和评估的支持。
在其他航空航天应用中取得的进展不应被视为海军导弹已做好准备的证明。燃气轮机和冲压发动机等传统发动机通过亚音速燃烧过程（也称为爆燃）产生推力。爆震发动机利用持续超音速燃烧（也称为爆震）产生的冲击波来产生推力。这意味着，对于相似的尺寸和重量等级，与燃气轮机或冲压发动机相比，爆震发动机不仅可以提供更大的推力，而且可以提供更高的效率。一家名为 D-Propulse Aerospace 的印度初创公司于 2026 年 7 月在 DRDO 测试设施测试了 RDE 原型机，在 24 小时内进行了五次静态测试。 D-Propulse 随后公布了开发 RDE 动力的吸气式超音速巡航导弹和旋转爆震火箭发动机 (RDRE) 动力的微型 SAM 的计划，用于反 UAS 应用。 《海军新闻》联系了创始人兼首席执行官 Saurav Jha，询问该公司对海军问题陈述的看法：D-Propulse 打算利用其吸气式 RDE 技术来制造超音速巡航导弹，这种导弹比传统系统更小、更便宜，但仍能达到作战射程。这将允许迄今为止只能承载距离更短的系统的平台进行承载。较低的价格将使印度军方能够实现真正的大规模精确化。
毕竟，超音速巡航导弹比其他类型的系统到达目标的概率要高得多。因此，超音速巡航导弹的弹匣深度是当今情况下的关键要求，我们的目标价格点应该能够实现这一点。 D-Propulse 的马赫 3 超音速巡航导弹的 CAD 渲染图（图片来自 D-Propulse） 在回答有关与海军就 RDE 海军导弹进行谈判的问题时，Jha 表示，D-Propulse 一直在与相关利益相关者就其正在开发的系统进行磋商，包括通过既定机制寻求支持。在海德拉巴测试的发动机已在 Swavlamban 2026 上展出，是经过验证的发动机

【原文 English Original】
The Indian Navy has expressed interest in supporting the development of a Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) – powered supersonic naval missile. The problem statement was part of a compendium released during Swavlamban 2026, the Navy’s flagship exhibition meant to showcase defence innovation, held in October 2026. The full text of the problem statement is as follows: This problem statement identifies a proposed indigenous supersonic naval missile programme associated with Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) research. RDE research examines rotating detonation as a propulsion principle. The challenge is to establish whether it offers a credible, supportable capability pathway for the stated naval application. The assessment should distinguish scientific feasibility, component maturity, integrated demonstrator readiness and qualification for service use. Independent evidence is required to substantiate claimed advantages against established propulsion alternatives. The programme should maintain clear requirements, configuration control, specialist safety oversight and traceability of results throughout its evaluation. Domestic design ownership, manufacturing repeatability, environmental suitability and long-term support are central considerations. The expected outcome is an evidence-based assessment of feasibility and maturity, supported by authorised research and evaluation. Demonstrated progress in another aerospace application should not be treated as proof of readiness for a naval missile. Traditional engines like gas turbines and ramjets generate thrust by subsonic combustion process, also known as deflagration. Detonation engines utilize the shockwaves generated due to sustained supersonic combustion, also known as detonation, to generate thrust. This means that for a similar size and weight class, detonation engines can not only provide greater thrust but also better efficiency compared to gas turbines or ramjets. An Indian startup named D-Propulse Aerospace had tested an RDE prototype at a DRDO test facility in July 2026, conducting five static tests in 24 hours. D-Propulse subsequently unveiled plans to develop RDE powered air-breathing supersonic cruise missiles and rotating detonation rocket engine (RDRE) powered micro-SAMs for counter-UAS applications. Naval News reached out to founder and CEO Saurav Jha to inquire about the firm’s views regarding the Navy’s problem statement: D-Propulse intends to leverage its air-breathing RDE technology to build supersonic cruise missiles that are much smaller and cheaper than legacy systems and yet reach operational ranges. This would allow carriage by platforms that hitherto could only carry much shorter ranged systems. The lower price point will enable true mass in precision for the Indian military. After all, supersonic cruise missiles have a much higher probability of arrival over target than other types of systems out there. So, having magazine depth for supersonic cruise missiles is a key requirement in today’s scenario and our target price point should enable that. CAD Rendering of D-Propulse’s Mach 3 Supersonic Cruise Missile (Image via D-Propulse) In response to a question regarding talks with the Navy for the RDE naval missile, Jha stated that D-Propulse has been in consultation with the relevant stakeholders for the system it is developing, including for support through established mechanisms. The engine tested at Hyderabad was put on display at Swavlamban 2026 and is the proof motor of a flight-capable design. Naval News has learnt that based on that test data, new iterations will be fabricated and tested at the company’s newly constructed large connected-pipe Combustor Test Facility. D-Propulse aims to compress the developmental cycle significantly with this facility and has offered the facility to other small engine developers. Naval News also requested comments from Jha regarding the rationale behind the planned development of the RDRE micro-SAM: The idea behind the RDRE-powered micro SAM is to flip the economics of war in the favour of the defender. RDRE-powered micro-SAMs will be faster and more maneuverable than existing systems, allowing the user to address a wider range of incoming subsonic loitering munitions. Our studies show that RDRE technology can bring down the cost of effective systems greatly, perhaps even to the point of these being seen as ‘consumable ammunition’ if the production runs are large enough. And given the saturation scenarios we are seeing across conflict zones such as the Persian Gulf, where literally thousands of low-RCS subsonic munitions are being lobbed at air defence networks, I believe that our RDRE power counter UAS micro SAM will be required in very significant numbers in the near future. D-Propulse intends to offer the air-breathing RDE powered supersonic cruise missile for user trials by the end of 2029 and intends to offer the RDRE powered micro-SAM by mid-2028. Globally, extensive work is being done in the United States on developing RDE technology. Under the DARPA GAMBIT program, RTX’s Pratt & Whitney had completed a series of RDE tests in 2025. AFRL has also worked on RDE technology and recently expressed interest in combined-cycle RDRE , seeking a flight demonstration to validate the system’s operational viability. GE Aerospace had tested turbine- based combined-cycle RDE in 2023. In January 2026, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace demonstrated a liquid fuel RDE for missiles. Venus Aerospace , L3Harris and IN Space LLC are also developing various types of detonation engines. In the Indian context, an RDE powered supersonic missile would be complementary to the BrahMos . While the latter with its proven production run and ever increasing range will remain the mainstay weapon of the Navy, lighter subsonic and supersonic missiles are likely to proliferate due to cost and weight benefits. Missiles like the NASM-SR and NASM-MR are being developed by DRDO. The lighter form factor of an RDE powered naval missile may make it analogous to the BrahMos NG, which is currently in the R&D stage. Dr. Jaiteerth Joshi, CEO of BrahMos Aerospace, recently told ANI that the first model of BrahMos NG is expected by 2029. Once fabricated, several rounds of trials are required before the missile can be inducted. Dr. Joshi also confirmed the development of a 1,500 km ranged version of the BrahMos, up from the current maximum of about 800 km . The range extension will continue to occur in a phased manner and the 1,500 km range version has been designed and is currently undergoing simulations. BrahMos Aerospace has a nearly a full orderbook and continues to bag export orders. After ordering three batteries for $370 million in 2022 , the Philip p ines is reportedly exploring purchase of “at least six additional BrahMos batteries.” India has also offered to explore the integration of BrahMos on Philippine naval vessels. Five Akash SAM regiments and the Pinaka MLRS are also being looked at by the Philippine Marines and Army, Firstpost reported. Earlier, India’s defence secretary had confirmed that initial deals were signed with two more countries in Southeast Asia for the BrahMos. Vietnam is likely to receive a single coastal battery worth about $100 million while Indonesia has signed two $100 million contracts. Both countries are expected to place larger orders in the coming years. Philippine Marines showcase the BrahMos anti-ship missile system for the first time during the service’s 75th anniversary. More on Swavlamban 2026 Other notable firms with flagship projects present at Swavlamban 2026 included: Sagar Defence Engineering which developed the Matangi USV. Sagar Defence has commenced delivery of 12 meter class USVs to the Navy in 2026 after receiving an order for 12 USVs. Xinfinti Aerospace is developing Naval Chetak Autonomous System (NCAS). NCAS is supported by the Navy under iDEX program and seeks to convert HAL Chetak helicopters into uncrewed assets, an endeavor attempted and aborted by a HAL – IAI combine in the 2010s. Kalam Labs has obtained an iDEX contract from the Navy for the development of floating aircraft carriers. Co-founder Ahmed Faraaz told Naval News that the product will be an airship that can transport Kalam Labs’ suite of propeller driven high-altitude proven swarm-capable UAVs to altitudes exceeding 50,0000 feet. The altitude will enable the airship to stay protected from anti-aircraft munitions while conducting ISR and deploying UAVs for various tasks. Kalam Labs has deployed its UAVs from altitudes greater than 100,000 feet using balloons. Faraaz told Naval News that the firm has also bagged iDEX contracts from IAF for development of a supersonic autonomous spaceplane and mesh enabled space drone swarms. content:

智利的研究人员发现，通过减少太阳能发电生产的绿色氢气可以实现低至 5.58 美元/公斤的氢气平准化成本 (LCOH)，而最具竞争力的风电项目为 7.27 美元/公斤。这项名为“减少太阳能发电的绿色氢气：真实数据分析”的研究评估了 2023 年 7 月至 2024 年 6 月期间 56 个太阳能发电厂和 44 个风电场的运营数据，总装机容量为 10.4 吉瓦。大约 25% 的记录每小时间隔发生这种情况，主要是在低功率水平下发生。研究人员利用基于质子交换膜 (PEM) 电解槽的技术经济模型，确定了 10 个表现最佳的项目（全部位于智利北部）的最佳电解槽容量为可再生发电厂净有效功率的 5% 至 13%。这些项目实现了 LCOH 值 5.58 美元/公斤至 6.97 美元/公斤，电解槽容量系数为 25% 至 30%。与最佳电解槽尺寸偏差高达 50% 的氢气生产成本增加不超过 3.8%。这项即将发表在《能源报告》上的研究发现，尽管储存、压缩和运输成本仍然是额外的考虑因素，但减少可再生电力可以支持具有竞争力的氢气生产。智利经历了严重的可再生能源削减，特别是在该国北部的太阳能发电厂。 Qair 在法国奥克西塔尼开设了 Hyd’Occ 可再生氢气生产设施。

【原文 English Original】
China has started operating a 195 km hydrogen pipeline connecting Darhan Muminggan United Banner with Baotou, Inner Mongolia, reported Xinhua News Agency. The pipeline has an approved annual transport capacity of 100,000 tons of hydrogen, potentially increasing to 240,000 tons. Developed by Inner Mongolia Huadian Huameng Pipeline, the infrastructure will connect renewable hydrogen production facilities in northern Baotou with industrial consumers in the south. Pipeline transport could reduce hydrogen delivery costs from about CNY 13 ($1.83)/kg by tube trailer to approximately CNY 3/kg, according to Xinhua. China has been expanding its hydrogen transport infrastructure to connect renewable energy resources with industrial demand. ACME Group has reached a final investment decision (FID) on a $3.6 billion green ammonia project in Odisha, India, with an annual production capacity of 760,000 tons. The facility, scheduled for commissioning in 2029, will feature a 2,200-ton-per-day ammonia production loop designed by Thyssenkrupp Uhde. It will use renewable electricity to produce hydrogen through electrolysis for green ammonia production, targeting customers in India, Japan and Europe. Brookfield has committed up to $600 million to support ACME’s green molecules platform. The project is expected to avoid more than 1.5 million tons of greenhouse gas emissions annually. ACME has also secured green ammonia supply contracts in India and is developing green methanol projects. Researchers in Chile have found that green hydrogen produced from curtailed solar electricity could achieve a levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) as low as $5.58/kg, compared with $7.27/kg for the most competitive wind projects. The study, “ Green hydrogen from curtailment: Real data analysis ,” assessed operational data from 56 solar plants and 44 wind farms with a combined capacity of 10.4 GW between July 2023 and June 2024. Curtailment occurred in about 25% of recorded hourly intervals, predominantly at low power levels. Using a techno-economic model based on proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers, the researchers identified optimal electrolyzer capacities of 5% to 13% of the renewable plants’ net effective power across the 10 best-performing projects, all located in northern Chile. The projects achieved LCOH values of $5.58/kg to $6.97/kg, with electrolyzer capacity factors of 25% to 30%. Deviations of up to 50% from optimal electrolyzer sizing increased hydrogen production costs by no more than 3.8%. The study, to be published in Energy Reports , found that curtailed renewable electricity could support competitive hydrogen production, although storage, compression and transport costs remain additional considerations. Chile has experienced significant renewable energy curtailment , particularly at solar plants in the north of the country. Qair has inaugurated its Hyd’Occ renewable hydrogen production facility in Occitanie, France. The 20 MW plant is supported by a regional network of hydrogen refueling stations forming part of the European H2 Corridor. Qair opened its first hydrogen refueling stations in Béziers and Narbonne in spring 2026. A second development phase will double the plant’s installed capacity to 40 MW, increasing annual hydrogen production capacity to 5,400 tons. Total investment amounts to €130 million. Plug Power has launched GenEco Scale, an integrated electrolyzer plant offering for utility-scale hydrogen production. Arcadia eFuels has selected the system for a 280 MW hydrogen facility at its Project ARC development in Texas. Plug Power said it has completed the project’s technical evaluation and front-end engineering design (FEED) study. Once operational, the facility is expected to support production of approximately 23.2 million gallons of electro-sustainable aviation fuel (e-SAF) annually. Plug Power previously signed a 280 MW electrolyzer supply agreement with Arcadia eFuels for a separate project in Denmark. Protium has completed due diligence for two green hydrogen projects under the UK government’s second Hydrogen Allocation Round (HAR2). The South Tees Net Zero project in northern England and the South Wales Net Zero project have both advanced to the Invitation to Offer stage. The 70 MW South Tees facility is designed to produce up to 11,000 tons of green hydrogen annually, equivalent to about 433 GWh, for industrial consumers in Teesside. The projects will now progress toward Low Carbon Hydrogen Agreements, which provide revenue support to reduce investment risks. Protium is also developing other UK hydrogen projects , including a 15 MW electrolyzer project that secured support under the first Hydrogen Allocation Round. Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

乌兹别克斯坦拥有适宜丝绸生产的气候、悠久的丝绸制作传统以及就业机会稀缺的农村社区。政府将该行业视为创造就业、减少贫困和增加出口收入的一种方式。
这些雄心壮志对于生产蚕茧的农民和农村家庭意味着什么？乌兹别克斯坦人权论坛的一份新报告记录了农民如何被迫生产蚕茧，以及在家养蚕的农村家庭如何面临剥削条件并难以获得报酬。
卡什卡达里亚干旱的卡马什地区的一位棉花和谷物种植者没有适合养蚕叶子的桑树。然而，2026年4月乌兹别克斯坦论坛观察员采访他时，他已经被告知要向区丝绸加工企业运送80公斤茧。
他的土地租约要求他种植棉花和谷物，没有义务种植茧。
今年年初，该农民表示，他签署了一份空白合同，其中仅包含他预计交付的规定数量的茧。程序与往年相同。他没有收到合同副本，也不知道将支付什么价格。
“也许他们根本不会付钱给我，”他说。
前一年，他没有收到任何报酬，因为他没有达到当地官员设定的配额。他从交付的茧中获得的收入低于生产它们的成本，因为他必须支付蚕卵和其他资源的成本。
所有接受报告采访的农民都表示，他们认为生产茧没什么意义，但又不敢拒绝。
“在交付茧时同意并购买茧比与地区当局发生争执更容易，”这是一种常见的解释。
乌兹别克斯坦生产丝绸已有数百年历史，是世界第三大蚕茧生产国，仅次于中国和印度。政府将丝绸产品视为战略出口产品和外汇来源。它还期望该行业能够创造就业机会并减少农村地区的贫困，因为农村地区通常很难找到稳定的工作。
该报告探讨了这些雄心壮志对于茧生产者意味着什么。 2024 年至 2026 年间，独立权利监察员对乌兹别克斯坦和卡拉卡尔帕克斯坦 5 个地区 21 个地区的农民和家庭茧生产商进行了 85 次访谈，审查了立法、合同、媒体和社交媒体以及管理该行业的官方文件。
报告的主要发现是，当前的茧生产体系依赖于国家强制农民劳动和对低收入农村家庭的剥削。因此，发展该行业的目标与提高R的目标之间存在很大差距。
